Okay, in all seriousness, this game is great. In fact, it's so great, that it deserves a multi-category review where I judge it on gameplay, story, graphics, and sound, each with a rating of "great", "good", "subpar", and "terrible", with a final rating in the end.
So, gameplay. Gameplay varies across all types of game, and shows you how they play; whether it's a 2D platformer, a top-down RPG, a first person shooter, and more. However, this game is very unique, as it is actually a first person puzzle game. I know this might sound complicated at first, but hear me out, it works beautifully. To sum it up, you have an Aperture Science Handheld Portal Device (AKA the "portal gun") With this, you can create two portals, and walking through one leads you to another. Sounds like an easy game, right? Not exactly. Different obstacles come across your path, such as...
-"un-portalable" walls
-doors that can only be opened by placing cubes on buttons, pressing buttons, and shining lasers at things.
-TURRETS.
-letting your companion cube go *sniffles*
-and just simply challenging levels!
The new game mechanics are also wonderful as well. As mentioned earlier, lasers are in the game, along with "hard-light bridges", excursion funnels, a gel that makes you go fast, a gel that makes you bounce, and more.
Another key part of Portal 2's gameplay is it's challenge. Portal 2 is one of those games that start off very simple and easy, and become increasingly challenging as you go on- and I mean VERY challenging. However, no challenge is large in comparison to the amazing feeling you get when you beat a level. If I were to kind of describe it, I'd just say doing the most challenging thing you've ever done that you knew you could do and was very possible but still took you a while and shouting out "HECK YEAH, I JUST DID THAT!"
In terms of content, the game has tons. To start off, it has a very extensive campaign of 8 chapters, each with a bunch of levels in them, some of which have multiple "test chambers" as the game puts it. It also have a 6-chaptered co-op campaign, which is also VERY challenging, and each chapter has 8 levels. However, going even further, the game have workshop support, meaning people can upload their own levels and play levels other people have made in the level editor! Oh yeah, I forgot to mention that. The game has a level editor. Anyway, there are THOUSANDS of levels already on the workshop, and people are making more as you read this very review.
So basically, I give gameplay a "Great". It's really solid, and tons of fun as well.
The story of the game is just amazing. Basically, it leaves off a long time after the first game ends, but nothing really happened  inbetween then and now. Basically, Aperture Science was a sciency-research center thingy, that made lots of stuff- like shower curtains. Anyway, one of their creations was GLaDOS, or the Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System. One thing led to another, GLaDOS is pretty much crazy, and she kills all of the employees with a deadly neurotoxin, and tests on some of the surviviors. Chell (your character) is one of the survivors, and it's GLaDOS's time to test on her. [MAJOR SPOILERS FOR THE FIRST GAME AHEAD] Anyway, you get through the 19 chambers hoping to be greeted with a cake she's bee teasing you with, but instead she tries to kill you, so you go rouge, find her, destroy her, and escape. However, you get dragged back in to the facility and put into stasis until Portal 2 begins. (I probably got some parts of that wrong, but oh well.) [SPOILERS END HERE]. Anyway, Portal 2 begins with you in stasis, and you've been in for quite a while. However, you're greeted by this ball-thing named Wheatley, who is one of Aperture Science's personality cores. He tries to break yout out of the facility, but adventure leads to mishaps, and a certain someone is rebooted. The certain someone does tests on you again, while Wheatley tries to break you out once more. It may not sound interesting so far, but there are some HUGE relevations and plot twists that make this story amazing. Unfortunatley, they're EXTREME spoilers, so I can't share them. You'll just have to play the game for yourself.
In terms of personality and dialogue, this game is action packed! The certain someone has a very sarcatic personality, cracking jokes at your faliures and mishaps all the time. It may sound annoying, but believe me, it's hilarious. The monotone voice she has increases the humor by at least 50%. Wheatley is pretty much an idiot. The game states it. His lines are amazing though, for his ignorance and stupidity lead to some of the best quotes in the game. Then you have Aperture Science founder Cave Johnson, who rambles on about the most odd, yet funny things. Although he doesn't have many lines in the campaign, he greets you with a message every time you play a community level. When pretty much any of the characters converse, it's utter hilarity, but don't think the game can't take itself seriously, as it also has it's fair share of serious and dark moments as well.
The co-op campaign is pretty starightforward though. You play as two robots, Atlas and P-Body, doing tests with the someone I have mentioned numerous times in order to prepare for finding a crud ton of humans preserved somewhere in aperture- to test on of course. While the co-op mode isn't story heavy, most of the dialouge is still as funny as the single player campaign, with even more laugh-out-loud lines.
Overall, I give the story a "Great". It's the perfect blend of humor, darkness, seriousness, and solidity that makes the story so amazing.
The graphics in Portal 2 are awesome. While it doesn't have such a varied color scheme (walls mostly consisting of black and white panels), the story and overall feel of the game mae it work REALLY well. It kind of gives you that gloomy, "you're trapped" feeling which goes perfectly with the game. Also, since it's been quite a while since the first game, and there's not exactly any "cleaning crew" in Aperture Science, there vergetation and broken panels ALL over the place for quite a while, also adding to the feel of the game. However, the graphics quality is AMAZING in my opinion. When this game does shading and lighting efects, it does it perfectly. Not to mention, the deterioration everywhere really shows you how much has changed since the first game, and it really is amazing
Overall, I give the graphics a "Great". They really make the game work, and I can't imagine a Portal 2 without the graphics it has right now.
As for sound, it's also wonderful. The intense, slightly creepy music just gives you the feeling that you're just absolutley trapped in Aperture Science, and no matter how hard you try, there's no way out. The music and graphics definetley work together to form the the overall feel of the game so perfectly. In fact, you can find the entire soundtrack for free on Portal 2's website
. It's in "media + downloads") in case you want to listen to it.
I give the soundtrack a "Great".
Overall, Portal 2 is one of the best games I've ever played. I give it a "Great".

So the servers are down for maintenance so I thought Id write a review. If they werent down I would be playing robotcraft because it really is that much fun.
So heres a few basic things you Id like to comment about:
1. Your initial robot design will probably be terrible and you will end up copying what other players make as you advance in tiers. That doesnt mean designs are not original, but they all kind of copy a certain trend such as helium rail gun pilot seat etc. because that works.
2.  Alot of times you will get lol stomped when you enter a new tier because high tier players will be playing in lower tiers not so they can lol stomp on you specifically but because they may not have gotten all the tier points they need or because they are doing a new build with new items they dont have enough of. You should all know that playing in higher tiers is always better because you get so much more rp to buy items.
3. After about T2 the battlefield becomes way more distance based because of the rail gun and plasma launchers, kind of annoying but if your fast you can stomp these guys out pretty easily and soon after you can fly. The problem with flying is that people fly to slow it seems and get shot down way to easily so hopefully they make flying more viable.
Overall Id give this game a 8/10 and thats really good for alpha. Also as I have read on the forums there are a lot of good suggestions like tank treads, artillery, huge ships etc that all sound very enticing so I am positive I will play every day until tier 8 at least so I can do some boss battles. This is a good casual game and if they actually introduce new guns etc it will be awesome.

1. it has keylogging built into the computer and we are told to trust that they won't decide to use it on this game
2. it is designed in such a way that it requires administrator priviliges and provides an easy entrance for malware
3. it isn't supported on all systems and will cause the game to crash on these computers
Do not download this game until you can confirm that the issues regarding Easyanticheat have been adressed and it no longer poses a security risk to any computer it runs on.

Portal 2 is one of those rare games that manages to combine immersive and stunning visual environments while also implementing characters with great  sense of humor. From the very start, the game opens with a spectacular set piece that helps envelope the tone and setting of the game. Everything feels very authentic. I felt like I was actually trapped in a futuristic, experimental facility, attemtping to escape with the assistance of a comical robot named Weatly.
The puzzles in the game also get progressively more difficult, but they are fun to figure out. The only drawback of the game, is that sometimes, for brief periods, the puzzles may seem a bit redundent, but the game manages to switch things up frequently enough to prevent you from feeling like the game is mundane or tiresome. I strongly recommend this game to both casual and hardcore gamers, I feel like most people will find something they will enjoy. Valve has once again, done a superb job.

This game is amazing
in a world where triple-a titles only focus on the action and graphics while making it extremely linear, this game however focuses on creativity and simplicity.
this game has many mechanics to it but it is extremely user friendly and anybody can pick up this game easily because of how simple it is, as proclaimed in the subtitle: Build, Drive, Fight.
The building is very easy to use and creating structures beyond your wildest dreams is very simple thanks to the unique first person control system. Most of the time the buildingprocess  is not boring at all as you are constantly trying to think of new ideas on how to improve your design. You could build a dragon, your name or even a shape thanks to the variety of shapes available for use. The tier system and tech tree system adds a sense of accomplishment to every battle fought as it adds more options and variety on how to build your bot.
The combat does not lose out to the building at all. The various maps add a startling diversity of environments to experience, be it flat, rocky or snowy, the game designers made the maps incredibly detailed. The design choices in building your bot add real weight in battle like the placement of wheels or thrusters. The damage system is also great because you need to put thought into the strategy of defeating enemies, or risk getting your weapons immobilized and chunks of armor removed. The wide variety of weapons and mobility options are also commendable. The no respawn system also puts emphasis onto the strategy of engagement instead of rushing in guns blazing.
In short, this is one of my favorite games of all time because of how people can use their creativity in gaming rather than just slogging through linear and repetitive storylines like in modern shooters. Also, it is free to play and available on a plethora of platforms.
Also, if the game devs ever see this, can you please add a 1/3 cube and fix the power for the railguns and plasma cannons? Thanks.

"Daddy, I want a portal gun".  My 6 year old tells me one afternoon.  "Um, sure, okay" I say.  The idea never enters my mind that he is talking about a video game.  A few days later, I notice something while he is playing Scribblenauts.  Right there in his inventory of scribbly things is a portal gun.
THE PORTAL GUN.
"OHHHH!" I say.  Now it hits me.  Where on earth did he see that?  I must be a terrible parent.  Okay.  "Daddy can play for you" , I say with a gleam in my eye.  We proceed to install Portal 1. Right when I start the game, he grabs the keyboard and takes over.  Before I know it, he's blazing right through the levels.  Then, he says, "Let's play Portal 2!"
"Portal 2?"
"YES! I want to play Portal 2!"   Well.  I actually do own Portal 2, so fair enough.  It's been on my backlog for too long.  We proceed to install Portal 2.  And on to the beginning...it's as if we are transported to a movie.  He's a little scared.  I ask him if he wants to stop it's okay - it may be too scary.  He squirms around, but as soon as the puzzles start he is ALL OVER IT.  Wow, this little guy really knows how to play.  Physics in a hole - WHATEVER - a 6 year old is blazing through this.  He gets stuck on level 15.  I GET STUCK ON LEVEL 15 TOO.  This puzzle is wrecking my brain, but then I realize I simply did not notice something.  Solved and on to the next.  The both of us play through the game off and on for a few months, he turns 7, and we put in a good chunk of puzzle solving together along with a fair amount of co-op play.  I even bought a controller adapter for a PS controller so we could play side by side.  A week ago we both finished it ( on the really scary parts I let him leave the room ).  I can't remember the last time I had so much fun completing a game with a partner.  My own little guy.  Thanks Valve for making a great game that is a also a wonderful father-son game to play together.  He proudly wears an Aperture Laboratories t-shirt now.

This game was actually not that bad. Until you got to the second tier. Robocraft is a free-to-play game that showcases in -game purchases to reduce grinding to virtually zero. As I said earlier, the first couple hours are fun. You design a vehicle, form a platoon and go out and play noobs just like you when you begin. The beginning is very fast paced. You unlock things in the skill tree and depending on how many skill points you have, can choose to unlock things. Tier two and beyond, then you encounter the problems. I felt like I was grinding for hours just to save money for enough armor blocks to finish my design. Skill points are not too hard to come by but when you start to unlock advanced stuff that can only be unlocked via 'Uber points', it just gets frustrating. As the timer counts down and you start driving toward the enemy capture point you instantly get wrecked by a 2 by 2 by 1 thing floating on the world limit with one railgun and helium blocks is very frustrating. The cash system sucks. If you die you receive almost no money and that little amount is spent on repairs. If you sacrifice yourself to defend a flag, guess what, almost no money and a skill point or two if you were lucky enough to get past the railguns and get an assist or two. I have no problem with free-to-play games but when made so blatant pay-to-win as this game is I just want to cry. Overall this game has potential if it wasn't pay to win. I would rather pay say, 5 bucks then go through the nonsence in the game. I felt as if I was ripping my hair out more than I actually got to play and spent a longer time grinding for cash then EA does trying to milk money out of customers. Sorry if this was too long but this is my opinion. Maybe if they fixed the pay-to-win I will come back.

For those who don't know, Robocraft is a robot construction/fight game that will see you build your own robot with blocks and then fight other players with it in third person shooter style.
+ Easy to use and  easy to learn how to use (the basic functions that is)
+ Intuitive for the most part
+ Simple (block system is a good one indeed)
- Too many unorganised information: On each block there are specifications that dont really mean anything to the unexperienced user, especially since there are no indications given as to what they could mean. Also to note that the information will not always be written in the same order depending on the block which makes comparison quite annoying.
- Weapon effects not detailed enough: The weapons have a huge problem in this game. Specifically, I, for one have absolutely NO idea how the guns are supposed to fire in this game. For example, I dont know if each gun has a fixed fire rate (which is not given) and I dont know whether or not the adding of weapons will slower the firerate of some weapons in order for all of them to be able to be fired. And that is something quite crucial in a game like this.
- Blocks: how do they work. So the general idea is quite simple, but in detail it is hard to understand how even the simplest of blocks work precisely:
Armor Rating: This information is given as if it was obvious what it was. Well it isnt. at ALL. Armor rating could be HP, it could be a percentage removal from damage income. it could be anything really. Saying armor rating without any definition isnt really the way to go. But, given how the blocks disappear when you are shot, Im guessing armor rating is in fact the HP of the block in question. but then new questions appear: how is damage calculated, what happens when you shoot a block that only has one HP left? will the rest of the damage affect the block behind it?
Weight: the weight system is not at ALL detailed either. how does the weight affect your speed, if it does at all. is there a limit you cannot pass if you only have that specific set of wheels? is it progressive? which means that the heavier you are, the more difficult it will be to move? Also to note that there is absolutely no mention of how much your current robot weighs, which seems stupid, in this case I'll just assume it's written somewhere in there but I couldnt find it.
- the Garage. For now, my biggest problem with the garage is taht it doesnt allow you to use blocks on a robot if they are already used on another robot you are NOT currently using. I think this is a stupid way to get people to buy more blocks and should be fixed immediately.
The levelling in this game is quite particular. What I understand so far is that there are two separate things, "levels", which represent the amount of load your CPU can offer, and "tiers", which will define against whom you will be fighting and what kind of technologies (new blocks) you will be able to research.
To level up, you wil have to  be a badass in multiplayer combat, to access higher tiers however (and something that I did not find was explained well either) to tier up you will need to have current tier blocks equipped. For example if you want to access tier three, you will have to have some tier 2 weapons and wheels on your robot, ect. (the system is a bit more complicated but Ill leave it at that since it is easy to understand)
+ The most positive thing about this system is that you can (and will) have access to every technology available and generally unlock all the technology of each tier easily (speaking of tier 3 and below).
- This could be treated as a good thing but also as a bad thing as ti discourages people to differentiate themselves and to specifify themselves in one specific branch. I think this is a shame because when Igo into battle as I see my allies and enemies all I can think about is how their robots all look extremely similar to mine.
First off there are very significant pros and cons to the matchmaking system.
It is extremely quick in matching you with opponents, which is always nice to have, however for this you sacrifice the choice of map and you cant really choose you you get to play with.
However, I have had a few problems with connectivity issues where I'd say 1 match out of 6 approximately will not load and will send you back to hangar. I have also experienced some major lag, mostly when looking at my allies and seeing some alarmingly frequent teleports (which means that instead of them moving fluidly from one place to another, they stop, then jump to the place where theyre supposed to be, then stop, then jump again, ect.)
The match making system also has a huge problem in the fact that it does not create teams based on the players' previous battles but purely based on what tier they are on. which leads to some extremely one sided fights.
And now the most important part of the game, the battles.
Starting with the obvious: there are only two maps and one game mode (which is go capture the enemy base) until tier three, then another more intersting game mode called boss battle which is indeed quite the interesting addition. (I havent played it so far so I'll update the first impressions later)
The fact that there are only two maps makes the game a bit repetitive and boring especially since the mas arent that well designed either (basically think of it as a dota or LoL map with a huge traversable area in the middle) There is some verticality, but not enough and still bugged, as there are some times when you cannot shoot an enemy as the game considers there to be a wall since he is on a ridge above you. (weird invisible walls... ll probably get corrected).
Combat otherwise seems fine, in that it requires you to aim (though not as much as Id hoped) and be semi-tactical in your approach of ennemies in order to win.

Ill start off with what I think is most important here, the fact that this game is EARLY ACCESS but that it has a fully functionnal in-game shop. This is eomthing that has been in a lot of games lately and that really needs to stop. If you want to support the devs of an early access/ beta game, fine, but do NOT add an in-game shop. This is completely stupid and beats the purpose of what an early access / beta game is.
Other than that, the in game shop functions exactly like in Planetside 2 or LoL, that is, you can buy everything with real money, but can unlock all non cosmetics with in game credits. Therefore there is no need to spend a single cent in order to play this game fairly. This is a good system, but like I said, an early access game should not have an ingame shop. Or, if it does have one, it should be purely for testing purposes and not require actual money.

This is perhaps my favourite game, ever.  The puzzles are exciting, and they all feel like they have unique solutions, even though there are a limited number of elements from which the puzzles are built.  It's such a rush to say, "Oh, I can do *that*!"
The game builds on the strengths of the last game, adding a set of tests like in the original, but then you enter the *old* testing grounds, with a host of new elements and ideas.  The single-player mode is about three times as long as the first Portal, with different phases and different enemies along the way.  The co-operative mode is an entire second game that is just as challenging as the single-player, though less varied.  I'm playing it through with my son right now, but I imagine it would be near impossible just using gestures.
The characters are absolutely brilliant.  GLaDOS, Wheatley, and Cave Johnson provide hilarious banter, with Ellen McLain's GLaDOS standing out because of her incredible character development.  Nothing beats solving puzzles while being taunted by a passive-aggressive, psychopathic robot.
I'm only sorry that the game ended.  It's not very replayable, since you only get the rush of solving the puzzles once (something the game actually alludes to in game), not that that stopped me.  Awesome game.  10/10.

Original review text, "The thought you put into your design, either helps or hurts in matches. Learning how to shield important parts has definite benefits. Since your bot tends to get destroyed quickly, having a well designed bot is less important.
Original review text, "Matches can be unorganized due to lack of an in-game voice communication feature. Typing anything meaningful while in combat is impossible. Note only one type of weapon per vehicle is allowed but multiple types of movers."
In-game voice is supported by 3rd party software. Very few people are using voice in game.
Original review text, "Play the first couple of match tiers for free. If your enjoying yourself, then I'd suggest getting a 3 month or 6 month subscription to reduce the grind. Subscribers get no direct in combat benefits."
Currently, I wouldn't suggest subscribing.

Of the games I've played in this genre - WoT and War Thunder, er, others that I forget right now, this feels like the fairest to the players across the board.

First of all i would say i recomend this game. It is extremely addictive and basics for very good game are present, however, game still needs polishing.  Some of the mistakes are plain silly, like in technology three when buying new technology it ALWAYS says you do not have enough tech points, even if you do. Network code is a bad joke, Me and my friend tried to get to same platoon but each time game showed that one of us was  offline even though we were both online. tried to restart game, game and steam and finally remove friend as a friend and it finally worked when we unfriend each other and restarted game and  sent friend invites.
Few weeks ago i nearly stopped playing because in every match there was someone cheating with hacking tool, but still i constantly wonder if someone is actually "hacking". Game has reporting system, but when there was cheater in every game they should have had paid me to do their job of doing those reports. Luckily they have mostly sorted that out.
Then we come to actual gameplay which in my opinion has few flaws that should be fixed. Biggest flaw in my opinion is the tier system and how it is implemented. Someone can use tier 10 (highest tier) gun in tier / game. Well nothing wrong with that, since that robot will be extremely fragile, but the problem is that those who have just passed tier 7 have tier 6 stuff and are there to earn tier 7 stuff via tech points. So guys with more experience are able to use better equipment than less experienced players, which in my opinion is not fair. At least my opinion is that fair system would be that first tier ppl are given blocks/weapons etc that they can use as a gift for starting the game and nothing else could be used in that tier. This would avoid people with more experience to go tier 1 with higher tier plasma cannon and  armor which allows him to  basically one shot kill first time players while still being able to take decent amount of hits. All in all it would be better to have system where you first earn technology to advance to next level rather than pushing less experienced players against more experienced players with better equipment.
Reason they are actually doing this is that they want people to buy premium or and technology converting points which allow you to convert lower technology points to higher ones, and premium basically gives double experience and reward. This is actually bad design point imo. Basically they give people opportunity to pay to play less because you advance really fast with premium. I got 3 days free premium and jumped from tier 7 to tier 10, which is kinda big jump when you consider that game has only 10 tiers and last ones should be harder to achieve.  I would recommend that they give premium users change of a cosmetic item from each match won where they get at least one kill. If they were good enough rewards i would have been more interested to pay for premium than getting double the money... especially now that i have reached the final tier.  Combined with steams market, it might be gold mine for them.
It still is good game as i said, it gives people ability to build very different robots and i rarely see multiple similar robots. It also allows what most games wont... extreme customization. It is possible to make robot that can one shot kill but is fragile or is clumsy or has other downfalls. Fast and fragile is also good way to go for some but for new players i would recomend to go as heavy tank which cannot be destroyed with one shot like robots that have block under the seat showing.  Later in a game it is refreshing to have 3 different robots in one of each slots given by the freejam. So you can build few different robots that give you rather different experience and allow you to use those items you cant use on your best robot.
I love and recommend this game for builder, fighter, and maybe even for role players who could build giant people. Overall it is amazing.   /[';']\

If you didn't play Portal 1, don't let that put you off from playing Portal 2. I myself was hesitant at first for this reason.
Portal 2 isn't a game about blasting stuff into oblivion or using mind-wracking puzzles to drive you to insanity. Instead the game teaches you a bit of a life lesson: Perserverance. Without giving away too much of the story (what exists of it), you will be solving little tests... some easy as pushing a button and racing across the room. Some hard such as diverting beams of light in front of sentry turrets and deactivating force fields so your platform can carry you across the toxic water below. All the way you will be crucially analyzed and hazed by GlaDos (Don't worry, you'll love her). Her soothign voice attempting to grind you into insanity while playfully informing you that she is just teasing (for the most part). Philosophically, the game is genius. You will be tested through out life and forced to reevaluate decisions that you have made. People will criticize you. But you do this all... for the love of science.

UPDATE: I recently revisited Robocraft after it's massive expansion, and I have to say all of my original complaints about this game have been completely nullified.  I think it was a good move to do away with the different block tiers, it really leveled the playing field and made your robot design matter again.  The changes to the weapons also are a vast improvement, and I think the regeneration out of combat makes the game much less frustrating.  The new game modes are fun, and I really like how you can buy other people's designs or sell your own now.  Way to go Robocraft devs for keeping the dream alive!
ORIGINAL REVIEW: Robocraft is a great idea terribly executed.  I spent way too many hours trying to make new cool designs only to discover they are all ineffectual in actual combat, and the same lame uncreative designs still win every time, ie the 'gunbed'.  Building new ships was enjoyable for a while until the futility of my efforts sank in and then the game just became annoying and frustrating.  If you're looking for a casual creative game to build a giant rolling phallus for people to shoot at, then this game is good for a laugh or two.  If you expect to be able to build badass custom ships and pwn people in serious battle with your brilliant designs, be prepared for a major letdown.

It's a sequel to a classic Valve title. It's got co-op. And a whole pile of chapters..
Why wouldn't anyone want this? The puzzles are pretty nice - often improving where the original game failed - and there's about 3-4x the content the original had. The graphics are very improved, still feeling comparable in beauty to many of the 2014 releases we're familiar with.
The workshop support really gets to me. Yeah, you can make a whole pile of really nice looking chambers, fully functioning. ..But they're all big, open boxes in plain new aperture theme. They lack the aesthetics that make Portal 2.. Portal 2. Every single wall or floor is just a box. There's not really a lot you can do with it, and it's alright for blocking out before you open it in Hammer.. Which makes a lot of the workshop submissions - even top rated ones - look shoddy unless they go through the full effort of making it within the Hammer editor.
Overall though? 8/10

POSSIBLY THE BEST FREE GAME ON THE INTERNET...
It's a game of a simple idea, near flawless execution, and addictively replayable.
You start of with a small wheeled vehicle with guns.  After getting used to driving your vehicle around the landscapes and shooting down enemies in the practice area you enter the battle arena where you do the same except everyone else is divided into two teams doing the same.  Depending how well you do you will receive a certain number of tech points that can be used to purchase the RIGHT to use new blocks (better wheels, better weapons, better armour etc) and Command Points which you actually use to buy the blocks (in appearance imagine Minecraft).  You can then rebuild and reorganise and rebuild your vehicle in your garage before test driving it again.  Add enough improvements and your vehicle becomes Tier 2 And so on up to Tier 10.
There are flaws.  There are only a few maps.  You are allowed to instal higher tier weapons on a lower tier vehicle so newbies  (and more experienced players) can find their Tier 3 vehicle one shotted from the other end of the map by a vehicle that is basically just a floating Tier 7 or 8 Rail Gun (Sniper Rifle).
These irritations apart the game is still amazing.  Weapon balance is good (although the forums are full of posts on the line that paper is overpowered against stone), at higher levels vehicles can float and fly, and some of the designs are amazing  - if impractical.  I loved the Starship Enterprise and TIE fighter that I saw on the battlefield.  And once a church.
I have never had so much fun on a Free to Play game.  And I've played a lot.

So it’s been a while since my buddy and I did our co-op run for Portal 2 on my Twitch stream. We had our fun and solved the puzzles all while we gathered achievements even though I’m not the biggest fan of them. I also had my fair share of screwing my buddy over by flipping a switch or not and getting rid of portals at the “right” time. Fun was had (at my buddy’s or my personal expense) and I figured I should now probably tackle the single player campaign.
The story carries over from the first. You’re the same woman (Chell) and I believe you’ve been in stasis for 50 years. You still look as good as you did when you killed GLaDOS those many years ago. The story wakes you to a new player in the Portal universe: Wheatley. Wheatley is hilarious! I love the banter that goes on (I would say between you and him, but you don’t really talk) as he “narrates” the goings-on.
Warning: the rest of the review contains what someone could consider a spoiler even if it’s a mild one (just in case you’re like me and up to this point haven’t actually played Portal 2 yet).
The story evolves and you eventually come to the realization that GLaDOS was killed, but she wasn’t erased when you accidentally bring her back online thanks to Wheatley’s “help”. What then ensues is a back and forth comedy, loads of puzzles, and a few great twists and realizations that, while not Earth shattering, is very interesting Portal trivia to know. The story was very fun and if you don’t feel the need to get through it, I can’t understand where you’re coming from.
They introduce a few new elements as well to help differentiate Portal 2 from the first. There a gels that get splattered around certain levels that can help the player run faster, jump higher or even create new surfaces to put a portal on. This really added a new level of thinking for the sequel. Also, there are tractor beams (as shown in the picture below), light bridges (which were super fun in co-op) and laser redirection cubes to, you know… that redirect lasers and such (or kill a buddy).
The co-op is as fun as the single player. You miss out on the banter between Wheatley and GLaDOS, but if you feel the need to be called not as good as your friend and then have GLaDOS sing your praise and tear down your friend or sometimes just both of you at the same time, co-op has it all! That, and the puzzles require more thinking than normal since the two of you both have portal guns and you’ll have to work them in tandem with the usual timing and well thought out plans.
Score: Tasty!

With the fantastic humor in the solo campaign and the very well thought out puzzles for co-op, Valve did a great job with this sequel. The only lament that I’ve got is that Valve doesn’t tend to make trilogies (even though I can’t figure out how they would progress from this point). I guess they could do something with more of the co-op stuff… four player Portal anyone?

~UPDATE~ I cannot in good faith recommend this game anymore. As much as it pains me to say, look on this review as a memory of what Robocraft used to be.
~EAC UPDATE. FOR THOSE HAVING ISSUES, READ THESE TWO LINKS.~
-
This game is wonderful.
Honestly, I thought it would be a cool game for a little bit, and then it would decend into Pay to Win.
NOT AT ALL.
You start out being only able to create cars at Tier 1. No big deal. It's a ton of fun messing around with different configurations of blocks that DO NOT work at all, flipping you over at the start, etc. Then you see a guy with a giant flying swastika, or a TIE fighter, or a pirate ship, or a dinosaur. So you start thinking, and finally, you make a car that doesn't flip over. You get a couple tiers up, you start realizing how the physics in the game work. You start building smart. You start placing shields and weapons and radars, etc. strategically, not haphazardly. THEN, you get hovers. Or thrusters. Or plane wings. Or walker legs. Or Helium tanks. You build a hover that flies upside down the entire match, flipping your controls. Back to the drawing boad. You build a hover that flies upside down half the match. Back to the drawing board. Finally, you create your own masterpiece: a hover that doesn't FLIP. A plane that flies straight. A helium balloon that...floats. Whatever it is that makes you happy, you build it, and it WORKS. Until you get blown out of the sky by said giant flying swastika. JUST KIDDING, your creation absolutely wrecks him. You win the match with 3/4 of your vehicle gone, all but one weapon destroyed, limping your poor way to the enemy camp, and you capture it, winning the match. You go back to your garage, and you see your masterpiece. Your creation. Your weapon of mass destruction (or healing). You think, I built this. This is mine. This is MY tank/hover/walker/car/helium balloon/plane/etc. All without dropping a single cent.
Important points-
-The damage progression in each match is quite realistic. There is no healing, unless there is a medic player. Each different hit will do something different to your vehicle, depending on where you are shot. There are no health bars, simply each block of your vehicle that gets painfully destroyed piece by piece. However, that means that you can keep fighting, literally, to the last block of what you have. If someone takes out your wheels, you are now a turret. If someone takes out your guns, you are now cannon fodder. If someone takes out one wheel, have fun making donuts. All in all, the way damage affects you in each match is very realistic, very fun, and oftentimes, very funny.
-The physics in this game are phenomenal. If you build something unbalanced, you better expect to get flipped over. You have to make things balanced, and take into account how fast you will be going, where your guns will be, etc, etc. A very refreshing, albeit difficult, concept that is well implemented in this game, more so than anywhere else I have seen. And that doesn't even include what happens when different blocks of your vehicle get destroyed, which also affects your balance, depending on what was taken.
-Matchmaking is very well done, not perfect, but well done.  You can get people who go to a lower tier by having only one ridiculously overpowered weapon, but as you advance in tiers, this happens less and less. Eventually, you might find yourself being the one going back down to lower tiers to wreck noobs and relieve stress. You never know. Still, the way it matches players based on vehicle tier, not player level, is smart.
-You can access EVERYTHING except cosmetics with currency earned in game. In other words, NOT PAY TO WIN. (Thank you to CrAnKeD for noticing this error.)
-The amount of pride that you will get after you finally make a vehicle configuration that looks badass, holds its own in a fight, and is 100% your own...That alone makes this game worth it. Think minecraft, except you can take your creations into one giant arena and duke it to the last block with other players. Yeah.
Tl;dr - This game is awesome, and it's not pay to win. AND it's in alpha, so expect greater things. A must try, at the least.

One of the most easy to play yet complex games I've had the joy of sitting down and get to know. Have a grand 'ol time building your death machine of choice and battling it out with one of the nicest communities I've played with for something so competetive. You'll also have a few laughs here and there from all the destroyed robots you'll come across. Also, it isn't Pay-to-Win either.

First off, this game is still in "Early Access" and is complete fun (with from just my time a GREAT/HELPFUL community! As of right now I give this game a 4/5 (would have gave it a 5/5 but waiting to see if they add more match type that last longer than 2min lol). If you would love to build vehicles of your dreams and don't  mind earning your parts (which honestly won't take you long at all to get because you have so much fun even if you lose!) then going to a demolition with it then this game is for you! You can chose to drive on land, fly (after unlocking parts), or crawl (yes i said crawl, also after unlocking parts), as in you can put legs on your vehicle instead of wheels! At-At walker or At-St walker (StarWars) anyone!?! This game is completely free with the option to buy in-game currency, now that doesn't necessarily mean pay to win. As I've come to notice sure you can buy all kinds of things but you have to level your profile in order for you vehicle's cpu to gain more power. for instance (can't remember off the top of my head so this is just an example) at level 1 your cpu is at 100 and you buy a gun that takes 25, then you can't put any more than 4. I've also noticed I have always been placed with people on the same tier as I am (vehicle level) so no worries about being thrown in a match with someone 5 times higher than you! Now stop reading my review and get your hands on this game, you'll be glad you did! Out of all Free-to-play games this one is in 2nd place for me ONLY because I'm a huge fan of survival games which means this game only comes after Unturned (so take that as you may wish)!
P.S. When you die in a match as of right now (I have no idea if they intend on changing this in the future) you can go ahead and exit match and keep rewards (it'll tell you in the lower left hand corner after death), and jump right into another match and keep rolling!

Robocraft is a game where you build your own robot and fight with other random robots in a attempt to capture the enemy circle. It's pretty fun. Building said robot from the ground up and upgrading it as you travel up the tiers is rewarding, and they have a practice mode where you can test it out. And blowing up enemy robots is greatly entertaining, as your well-crafted robot (Or shoddy hover chair with a rail gun and a stroke of luck) cuts through the competition. It does have a few problems though. (Mostly nitpicks).
Cons:
Random team pairing means winning or losing is judged by the flip of a coin. (But a well made robot will still do well regardless.)
Slight problem of having to grind unless your premium. ( But again, they give out 1-day free premiums at record pace, and at least it's not Pay-To-Win.
People will sometimes make untouchable hover chairs and snipe you with no chance of retailation, but can I really fault the game for that?
In summary, robocraft is a fun little title that I recommend to anyone that likes robots shooting other robots, or online PVP in general. (It being free to play helps too.)
9/10 Would craft a robo again.

A few quick points about the game:
* Robocraft is essentially just like Lego. You design, build, test and then compete against other players with your creations. The gameplay environment is surprisingly competative. So, contrary to common belief, you won't see a lot of genitalia on wheels in game.
* The gameplay itself is fast paced, action packed; a single match generally lasts no longer than 7 minutes. If your vehicle gets destroyed you are sent to your garage and you can immediately jump right to the next match.
* Aquiring player experience points, tech points and credits to constuct your vehicles is actually very easy (too easy some might say), especially when you have a premium account. Grinding in this game is existant but it is not at all gruelling.
* The only two substantial downsides that are currently worth mentioning would be the matchmaker system and lack of map variety. Speaking about the matchmaker, it does not seem to take into account the types/classes of vehicles that are put to one given team. And since Robocraft is largely a team-based game, sometimes ending up in a team that half of it consists of medics, it can get a bit frustrating. But the game is still in Early Access and I'm sure things will change for the better.
Rating: 9/10
In short, if you like Lego, you'll love Robocraft. I mean, who doesn't like Lego?

Original Review Oct 29, 2014 @ 6:47am:  Seriously, a spectacular game; I have a hard time remembering that it is still considered to be in Alpha.  For those of you who played it, this game is (at least to me) the spiritual successor to Chromehounds, except better.  To be honest, I can't decide what I enjoy more: building new robots, or blowing the crap out of people with my new robots.
The four (at this time) weapon classes each have a completely different play style, which keeps things interesting, and the wild variety of propulsion systems and shield panels allows for some wild and inventive battle robot designs.
I have to mention that, based on the cmplaints addressed in the top listed reviews for this game, I almost didnt bother downloading it.  That would have been a huge mistake.  As it turns out, all of those major complaints have already been fixed (or are just the result of unimaginitive players driving poorly designed robots and getting stomped).
I will say that, when you are first starting out, the game is fairly opaque and it can be unclear how things work and what to do (becasue they dont have a tutorial yet).  So after you play your first few matchs using the default robot, go read some guides on steam and watch some videos online.  Then go have fun!

It can be a bit glitchy at times, but like I said, it's early access and still under construction, sometimes you'll just fall through the floor at the beginning of battle and will have to self destruct, I've only had this happen twice in the hundreds of battles I've done though, so not bad.

Overall, 9/10 and would definitely recommend

While i do applaud the developers for the interesting concept for a game, and while most times, normal battles can be fun, to me there are three major flaws with this game.
1) The "Tier" system.  It's not based on your overall level... or the tier of the weapons and armor cubes you used to build your robot.  It's based on a points system, which can basically allow someone who has weapons from a MUCH higher tier to enter games with nothing but other robots from a much LOWER tier, and just annihilate anything in its sights.
2) Not only can they do this with weapons, but with the armor and special armor blocks, too.... to the point where you can take out an enemy with one volley of like 8 plasma shells.... but these robots with higher tier armor you're lucky to damage 10% before they one-shot you with a railgun or a volley of higher-tiered plasma shells.
3) Coupled with point #1, it's far to easy for people with said higher tier weapons to just hover in the sky, incredibly difficult to see, and just snipe you before you even know they're there (aside from the exclamation mark above your craft... which doesn't tell you all that much, really, other than that something might attack you from where you cannot see or some such).  They don't even have to move, really.  It's usually just a block or two, 2/4 hover blades to lift them into the air, and a railgun.... and they can usually one-shot you.
Just makes for a complete and utter lack of feeling of accomplishment.

Awesomenauts has only a few things to look after and they do a poor job because they have no servers.
As for the gameplay of Robocraft, I really enjoy it. It's fast paced, rewarding and I genuinely feel like I am rewarded for my personal skill. If you die, even if your team wins you don't get much. This game used to be very VERY fun, but sadly I can no longer recommend it to anyone looking to spend longer than a few hours on it, the recent updates have made the game increasingly less focused on making the game fun for long time players in favor of making new players stay a few days longer, this means that the developers have sacrificed depth for making the game easier and more suited for children.
The game has also lost a bit of its uniqeness in customization with many colours and glass blocks being locked behind a paywall, effectively making players have to pay to make their robots look good. The two newest weapons added have been made for anti air combat so the most fun part of the game, building flying robots, has been made non competitive against ground robots.
There are still some things that have been added that are good, for example the community robot factory and "the pit" the former being a place to buy other users robots, if you're not good at building your own and the latter being a free for all game mode that probarly shoud have been in the game from the start. Also the community of this game has been filled with toxic kids, but that is not really the games fault. The game has not become pay to win, but it is taking steps in that direction.
TL;DR:
The game has been made easier and more "pay to win" in the latest months since i wrote my original review. (which I provided below for reference)
ORIGINAL REVIEW:
This game, while being called a Pay to Win (P2W) by some, is a very fun game.
Sure you can buy "premium", "Galaxy cash" or new robots, while this can help you in getting to the higher tiers faster, but this is in no way making you a better player on the battlefield and now with the new update everybody (including the other team) gets a 5% bonus for every premium in the game, so in short:  NO need to buy premium/galaxy cash/robots! therefore not a P2W
Now on with the review,
The building of robos in the game is very good in that a HUGE(!) variety of robots can be built, everything from gunbeds which are flat slabs with loads of guns (somwhere around 7+) often SMGs to the satellite which hide in the sky and snipes the enemy from afar.
What I like about the system of building robots is that there is not just a preset design that you can put guns on or modify a tiny bit, no no no, you acctually have to construct everything cube by cube which provides almost endless creativity.
Now on with the pros and cons:
Pros:
-   Varied maps
-   Fun gameplay
-   Extensive customisation
-   Teir system which matches you to equally stron opponents
-   Frequent updates which add a lot of content
-   Helpful community
-   And much more...
Cons
-   Slow and unstable servers
-   The teir system is a little unbalanced
-   Plasma and railguns are underpowered
-   lack of maps, only 4 so far
All in all I think this game is worth a couple of hours :)

I really like the idea and played this game more than I intended to, but there are some flaws that really bother me. Unless they're fixed, I won't recommend this game to anyone. First of all Robocraft suffers from terrible tier progression. The way tiers work, every component has a score, the higher the score the higher the tier. After a certain score your robot enters a new tier, but the problem is when you advance to a new tier, your equipment is  inferior to most of the players you play against. So of course you get decimated a hundred times before you get the better equipment, and it's not particularly fun to be honest. This goes both ways though, after you advance enough or get close to the next tier, you become the one who destroys the new players that entered your tier. This is all intentional of course, the game forces you to grind. I've been playing for almost 20 hours now and I barely scratched tier 4. Of course the more you grind the more difficult it gets, just as many other f2p games out there. Component prices turn sky-high rather quickly, and all this time you're eyeing that "Add Funds" button on the top. "But if I pay for premium I can advance twice as fast". It's an overused formula, and it's a shame that games with great potential like Robocraft turn pay2win quickly. I'd rather pay $20 for a balanced game than a stunted "free" one.

A wonderfully-crafted sequel to an already original FPS game! This is, in a nutshell, Portal 2.
Released 4 years after its predecessor Portal 2 offers the following new features:
--- While the core mechanics return some new elements are present and needed for puzzle solving. My favourite was the gel machine. These machines release gel and the gel-filled surfaces can be used to accelerate the protagonist in order to reach a much higher ground. Also, surfaces can be made available for the use of portals with the gel.
--- Again, we have an extremely funny, relatively long and story-based single-player campaign. We have new voice actors (such as Stephen Merchant who usually works with Ricky Gervais - those of you familiar with Gervais's comedies will probably grow to like Stephen immediately) and the usual dark sense of humour is present throughout the single-player adventure.
--- Co-op campaign is now available and demands that the two of you closely work together. Some of the stages can be tough (in both campaigns) but they are still heaps of fun.
--- Graphics have also been improved. As we are in the same facility but after the events of the first episode, many of the chambers have walls that show aging and / or deterioration. This immediately allows players to immerse themselves in the story and realise that many years have been passed since the previous adventure.
The game has numerous mods available and just recently a paint gun mode has been released. As the gel-mechanics was based on a game called Tag: The Power of Paint, it was only natural to see the gun incorporated into the world of Portal. In fact, the creators of that game were hired by Valve and worked on Portal 2.
Portal 2 is an excellent sequel and is worth every penny spent on it! This is a highly recommended game along with its predecessor.

As sequel to the seminal Portal, Portal 2 had a lot to live up to. Indeed, the game's presentation is of the highest caliber, with excellent voice-overs, a deeper than it looks plot, a surprising attention to detail and a few interesting twists. But games are about more than presentation and the first Portal treated us to new and interesting game-mechanics that created a different experience.
Unfortunately, this game is not the groundbreaking game its predecessor was. It attempts to be entertaining simply by reusing and slightly expanding the mechanics of the first game. A legitimate strategy I suppose, that would have worked perfectly well, if not for a "small" problem: the narrative of this game is much longer. Unfortunately, the various small additions are not enough to keep things interesting. Even worse, some of these additions, ie the new environments, do not integrate as seamlessly with the mechanics of the game and that may lead to some frustration.
That said, this is still a decent game and I recommend it. For the most part, it manages to succeed in offering an above-average gaming experience. Just take it in strides and don't expect another revolution, or you might be disappointed.

A wonderfully-crafted sequel to an already original FPS game! This is, in a nutshell, Portal 2.
Released 4 years after its predecessor Portal 2 offers the following new features:
--- While the core mechanics return some new elements are present and needed for puzzle solving. My favourite was the gel machine. These machines release gel and the gel-filled surfaces can be used to accelerate the protagonist in order to reach a much higher ground. Also, surfaces can be made available for the use of portals with the gel.
--- Again, we have an extremely funny, relatively long and story-based single-player campaign. We have new voice actors (such as Stephen Merchant who usually works with Ricky Gervais - those of you familiar with Gervais's comedies will probably grow to like Stephen immediately) and the usual dark sense of humour is present throughout the single-player adventure.
--- Co-op campaign is now available and demands that the two of you closely work together. Some of the stages can be tough (in both campaigns) but they are still heaps of fun.
--- Graphics have also been improved. As we are in the same facility but after the events of the first episode, many of the chambers have walls that show aging and / or deterioration. This immediately allows players to immerse themselves in the story and realise that many years have been passed since the previous adventure.
The game has numerous mods available and just recently a paint gun mode has been released. As the gel-mechanics was based on a game called Tag: The Power of Paint, it was only natural to see the gun incorporated into the world of Portal. In fact, the creators of that game were hired by Valve and worked on Portal 2.
Portal 2 is an excellent sequel and is worth every penny spent on it! This is a highly recommended game along with its predecessor.

Robocraft has gone through many changes and improvements over the years.  As the game stands currently there is loads of fun to be had with creative designs and a good selection of game modes.  The game has recently entered BETA and has seen regular tweaks and additions every few weeks since entering BETA.
Robocaft allows players to construct bots (vehicles) from a huge selection of basic blocks, movement types and weapon types.  Players can list their creations on the in-game store for sale to players who wish to purchase a ready made bot with currency earned in-game.
Game play centers around team based arena combat matches that typically last around ten minutes which is great if a player does not have a huge amount of time to play games.  Match queue time is usually around one to three minutes and very rarely exceeds five minutes.  The game checks connection for all players at the start and will close the match if a player has lost connection.  Should a player lose connection after a match starts the team that has lost a player will be slightly buffed to compensate.
Bots are limited in size to a maximum of 2000 cpu (one cpu is the energy used by one standard block) specialised parts and weapons will consume larger amounts of CPU.  Players unlock larger CPU as they reach higher player level.
There are several arena maps with different scenery and layout, and the objective is to capture and hold key points while eliminating any enemy bots.  Some game modes focus on a specified number of kills to acheve victory.  Another game mode requires elimination of the enemy with no re-spawning.
Action is fast and furious and every match will feel different as there are such a variety of bot designs and nuances of player strategy.
Robocraft can be played as a free to play game, but it is highly recommended to get the LIFE-TIME PREMIUM package as this provides some really nice perks which significantly speed up earnings potential and experience boost enabling the player to level up quicker and and accumulate parts for building bots faster.
Robocraft is a great competitive team based multi-player game and is already well polished with a large player base.  There are some players who post regular game play and building tutorials on you tube.
Game rating
9 /10
Note!  About a year ago I rated Robocraft 10 / 10, but some changes made do not appeal to me personally.
What are perceived negatives?
1. The smaller map sizes
2. The new game modes
3. The constant imbalance because the developers listen to the players TOO MUCH
4. The Custom games draw players away from the queue for normal games.
5. Bugs, glitches and exploits
6. The removal of the Mega Bots from the game
What are the big plusses?
1. Active player base
2. Addictive game play
3. The game keeps changing requiring players to adapt
4. The game stimulates and encourages creativity
5. No two matches feel the same
6. Differences between parts cause design choice decisions to be difficult
7. Sometimes the developers almost balance things a bit (before creating new imbalances)
8. The challenge
9. The game looks good
10. The sound and music is good
11. The into video is awesome ...
Robocraft is a great game, but not all the changes made have been positively received by veteran players.  Bearing in mind the game is still in BETA the potential for developers to improve or ruin the game for the existing player base is always dangling in the balance and only time will tell if they "get it right".
My hope is that the developers will continue to explore new ideas and enhance the game.
My biggest wish is that the developers manage to squash most of the bugs and glitches and stay ahead of the curve on game exploits and cheating.

This is a very fun game. The fact that the battles are usually over rapidly for good or ill means that you don't have to set aside hours to play it, though the "just one more game" aspect might make you do that anyway. The creators have consistantly updated the game with new features, many of which add depth to the strategy. When there are problems, as with the servers or etc, they seem to attempt to fix it right away, and even issued a free day of premium membership for everyone during the current minor problems.
Beyond all of that, the idea is simple: you have levels, which you gain through playing, that allow you certain amounts of stuff you can put on your vehicle. Each item has a cost in space, and in money. The money is, also, gained through play. Each new tier you gain is done by getting a vechicle loaded up enough to reach the new tier. Tiers have tech points you also gain through play, and which unlock new items. Later tiers have access to some improved items you can't get at first.
That's basically it. If you like to build things (minecraft, lego, etc I imagine), or play vehicle combat games, this is certainly worth looking at, especially because it's free!

As sequel to the seminal Portal, Portal 2 had a lot to live up to. Indeed, the game's presentation is of the highest caliber, with excellent voice-overs, a deeper than it looks plot, a surprising attention to detail and a few interesting twists. But games are about more than presentation and the first Portal treated us to new and interesting game-mechanics that created a different experience.
Unfortunately, this game is not the groundbreaking game its predecessor was. It attempts to be entertaining simply by reusing and slightly expanding the mechanics of the first game. A legitimate strategy I suppose, that would have worked perfectly well, if not for a "small" problem: the narrative of this game is much longer. Unfortunately, the various small additions are not enough to keep things interesting. Even worse, some of these additions, ie the new environments, do not integrate as seamlessly with the mechanics of the game and that may lead to some frustration.
That said, this is still a decent game and I recommend it. For the most part, it manages to succeed in offering an above-average gaming experience. Just take it in strides and don't expect another revolution, or you might be disappointed.

First game I got on Steam, and I've not reviewed it yet. It's time I did. This is not a game. This is a work of art. Valve struck gold in 2007 with the release of The Orange Box, a package which indluded games like Half-Life 2 and the episodes, Team Fortress 2, and Portal. Portal was an experiment, and yet was acclaimed as one of the most original games of that year. Developement of a sequel began right away. Usually it's difficult to live up to such an incredible game in a sequel, but Portal 2 showed just how good a sequel can be. An extended story, more characters and character development, and the almighty GLaDOS. The puzzles were increased in quantity, quality, and length. The gameplay was suberb, the story was even better, managing to not take itself seriously in some parts, and still managing to be serious where it needs to be. All in all, 9.9/10. Why 9.9? Because I never rate a game 10.

One of the most valuable skills to a painter is to know when you are finished (hang with me past these metaphors) and unfortunately, to me at least, it seemed this one was finished months ago. every addition to the game now seems pointless and the result is an overworked piece of art.
The simplest things work best and the old tier system worked wonders and gave depth and progression to a game that would otherwise be build, drive, destroy for fifteen minutes before getting bored. now the game has damn near no progression and all cubes have been irreversibly equalized completely ruining people who have worked into levelling up their bots to the best protection.
The game's progression-based core mechanics have been cut down in favour of gimmicky, shallower ones designed to attract newer players with bigger pockets. This game WAS award winning. This game WAS well structured. This game WAS good. I've genuinely never seen such an amazing game falter so badly. A lot of the rants I have seen in the reviews seem to have the same issue. Normally, this would be a huge issue. However, I think I see what is happening. They are complaining about being destroyed almost immediately. This may be because they are using low tier armor blocks which can be shredded by a higher tier weapon. I often see people using T1 armor blocks so they can use T4 weapons while in a T3 game. With a T3 SMG, you can cut through 4 of those with one shot. However, T4 armor will require a couple hits to remove.
Anyway, with the actual review!
First off, bots are in tiers. Each part has a weight value for the tiering system, as well as a weight value for pFLOPS. The pFLOP limit is a hard limit that does increase based on a secondary levelling system. That doesn't play too big of a role when it comes to battle. The tiering is a much bigger role.
As you increase your tier rating, you will enter into a new tier to compete in. This is important as all items are unlocked via tech points. You will need different tiered tech points for different tiered blocks. This prevents people from making an amazing T1 bot (keeping it under the T2 point limit) and farming up RP. You use RP to purchase the blocks. You need higher tech points to unlock better blocks.
It is possible to farm up RP to buy some expensive blocks by staying in a lower tier. This will not benefit you for tech points, but it can help with generating RP a little easier. This also might not be the best thing to do, as you do generate more RP in the higher tiers.
Overall, it is a balanced and fair game, you just need to be a little smart with your builds. Give more protection to your chair, I use an axel three blocks wide, and a side skirt to protect my wheels.

Robocraft is one of the best games, if you are skilled with a huge ammount of fantasy and burn to use it.
it is developed by a small group of developers, and there is allready a verry nice playerbase for the ammount of developers working on it. I spent over 120 hours playing this game, and can tell you, you can literaly feel the developement of the game.
even thou it is far from finished, on a weekly base you can see the introduced changes and improvements.
sometimes downtimes occour, but the developers where so kind and offered us free premium access as to make up for the downtime and que problems. strategicaly this game is quite similar to any other moba, where you use vehicles to battle, like World of TANKS. but robocraft would not have the world "CRAFT" in it, if the most important thing wouldn't be on how you craft your vehicle. as a mather of fact, the HOW you build you vehicle decides what role you take in fights.
are you highly social person, and prefear assisting your teammates on dealing dmg/destroying enemy vehicles??
than ground or hovering vehicles equiped with a nano disrupter (Healing Laser) will do for you.
do you want play sniper, and wait for long times before shooting some well aimed and deadly shots??
you are gona love the railgun. there are many ways to make a vehicle  thou.
the most know forms are:
tanks, vehicles with many cubes who can withstand a lot of dmg
Hovercrafts, vehicles who will have less armor, but are way more mobile, and since they are not touching the ground, have the same performance regardless on what kind of ground they are traveling (ex: sand, snow, bridges, ice, stones ect.)
Fast cars/racers are perfect for making fast attacks, and get out of the way before the enemy can counter. its a dangerous but highly effective strategy.
small size high speed high manuvrability planes, perfect if you want to feel the freedom of dancing in the air. you wil be hard to hit, you will just fly out of the view of other planes, before make an other attack run, and dealing critical dmg. they are perfect to fight the last categority in my list.
last but not least you have the heavy bomber, planes who carry a lot of weapons to allow them to make critical attack runns, dealing tonns of dmg specialy to enemies on the ground.
there are hundreds of build categories you can bild, for example satelites, minimalistic tanks ect, but these where just a fiew I have experience with and wanted to talk about.
I have allready talked about rail guns and nano disruptors, but isn't it time to list them in a proper way??
oldest entry in the list is the smg gun (subatomic machine gun), a laser machine gun, which deals moderate damage per shot, but has the highest rate of fire. in a 1vs1 close quarter fight, it is the strongest weapon, and its the best if you want to pull enemies out of the air.

the plasma canon is a weapon, which shoots energy balls in a panoramic flight to the target. they explode on impact, and deal high damage in the area of effect. all canons mounted on the vehicle will shoot at the same time. they have a short charge up time.
nano disruptors are the healing guns of the game. they deal only 2/3 of the dmg, a smg gun deals, and heals at a rate of 1/3 the dmg 1 smg gun will deal. they have a auto targeting system of allies, and 6 nano disruptors will fire max at the same time
so all in all I can say, I reached tier6 (out of 10) and plan to spend some money in buying cosmetic items and buy a additional garage, so I can store 4 vehicles.

[EARLY ACCESS REVIEW - OCTOBER 18, 2014]
Albeit some server instability, this game is shaping up to be a winner. Having played Space Engineers recently, this is a welcome change from the resource mining [in Space Engineers] in order to create a usable ship.
Playing very similar to World of Tanks, Robocraft allows players to earn ingame cash and tech points which can be spent on parts that can be unlocked in a decently-sized tech tree.
Vehicles are created using a block-placing technique popularized by games like Minecraft. Everything is custom; the player is able to place every single block that makes up their vehicle. When you sustain damage to your vehicle, blocks darken and eventually break. Poor structure can lead to large chunks of your armour (or worse) simply falling off. Designing a vehicle which can withstand a pummelling while protecting its vital attachments can be a struggle, but at the same time, identifying the enemy's weakspots and taking advantage of them in the heat of combat is just as challenging.
Even with a small monetary investment, you can help speed along your unlocks quite well, but even with the handy uber-tech points that you can 'create' with cash currencies, you are still required to play and win matches to make the most of it; the game is far from pay-to-win, and rewards both tactical and time-grind players alike.
As a free game, I definitely suggest you download it and give it a go; even in early access, this game has brought me quite a bit of entertainment, and I will happily say that I'll be back for more as the game develops.

The cake is a lie, but the Portal games certainly take it as my favorite puzzle games of all time. I've actually played this game on console, and played through both the solo and co-op campaigns multiple times. This is the sequel that Portal deserved for a couple of reasons:
First off, the story falls right in line with the first game. It's in depth, and builds heavily around a tight group of fully fleshed out characters.
Secondly I'd like to bring up gameplay. Just like the first one, no corners were cut with the physics in this game. The fact that the player can move so smoothly through the wide open test chambers makes the visuals that much more enjoyable, because there really are a number of awe-inspiring scenes.
Lastly I'd like to note why I bought this game a second time when I'd already played a considerable amount of it on console. I bought it for the community contributions and map editor. Playing fan-made solo and co-op maps are often more fun and more thought provoking than the actual puzzles in the game. The ability just to mess around in the map creator (with an EXTREMELY intuitive interface none-the-less) justified my second purchase of the game.
One of my favorite games of all time.

To those who are looking for a nice game please read on.
This game is unique in that you get to completely build the tank/robot/plane/mech from the ground up with all the physics and weights and movement problems (for the most part) you might encounter in real life.
There are currently wheels, legs, wings, hoverblades, and jet propulsion thrusters in game that can be used to move your hunk of metal across the field of battle. There are 4 types of weapons now and they are the Machineguns, plasma cannons, railguns, and nanodisruptors. From there you have all the other little things you can add to the robot to make it unique and able to do different things depending on what you want.
The limits of building are set by your level which increases as you do more damage to the enemy and change how much you can put onto your vehicle. Each item takes up some Cpu which is what is used to measure what you can add on. As you add more parts and use stronger weapons or better movement items your Tier slowly raises up. It is what determines what kind of robots you fight against. It is rare for you to fight anybody outside of your tier unless it is part of the new boss battle or a lower teir is being tagged alongside a higher one.
Railguns are what you might consider the sniper of robocraft in that they have long range and very high damage though take a long time to fire. Machine guns are the fastest firing weapon and do a moderate amount of damage that can slowly grind through a whole tank in a few seconds of controlled fire since each shot makes your spread increase ever so slightly. Plasma Cannons are robocrafts version of a grenade launcher that blows up on impact. They are capable of destroying large portions of a robot with each shot though take a bit to reload and have a very slow turning speed. The new Nanotech Disruptors are probably the only weapon i have any problem with at the moment due to the fact that they are only able to be used at close range though will lockon to the target and damage them at a slower rate then the machine guns though for some reason tend to only hit the seat first which has caused many people grief and rage. They are also able to heal allies though it is a slower process.
So far there are a few cons though. There are only a few maps and only 1 mode atm for them. The mode is called capture the point and its objective is to either destroy all enemies or take over their base. You only get 1 life per battle and they are relatively short. You will also run into higher teir players in a lower teir match with weapons and equipment that are sometimes over 2 tiers higher then the tier you are in. This can be a bad thing for those trying to learn how to play because you will not have access to those items till you get to that tier. Creating a very large robot is harder to do with the level restrictions and with only 3 garages to start out with it can be very frustrating trying to make sure you will be able to use that robot in battle without it just being a useless lump around your capture point.
A few things that I think should be implemented would be a way to see the center of gravity for building purposes and a way to save different builds seperately from those that are usable in your garage. I also feel that you should not be able to take a higher tier weapon into a lower tier but should be able to take a lower tier weapon into a higher teir match so that players are not faced with a tier 5 plasma cannon when they are only tier 2.

Robocraft. The game I always wished I had as a kid. Why? Well let me tell you.
Ever since I was little, I always dreamed of a game where you make your own "thing" and use it in the game. With this, you can. If you enjoy designing your own little part of the game, this is the game for you. You can design something, test it, realise it sucks, and try again. Eventaully you will become quite good at building vehicles and you will then rule the game.
Some people say this game is pay to win, however this is not true at all. The first thing about paying for things in this game, is it is completely optional. You can unlock every thing in the game with out paying a cent. Secondly, lets say I go and drop $100 on the game. Am I now insanely OP like I would be in many other games? No. Why? Because the way the game pairs you with other players is based on what materials you used to build your bot, therefore if you spent lots of money, you would simply be paired with others who had spent a similar amount of money, or had worked their way up to that point. Furthermore, it isn't even pay to have fun. After every battle, providing you have a decent aircraft build, you will be able to buy a few more parts for your robot. This way there is no grinding. Instead it is slowly getting better after every match.
Over all I give this game a 10/10 for potential, a 8/10 for enjoyability, and a 9/10 for payment options. Total rating is 9/10.
