I don't know what is with all of the negative reviews for the game. All of the problems encountered by the players writing the reviews I have not encountered once. This is most likely because all of these problems have already been fixed. Robocraft is one of the most enjoyable games I have played in my entire steam career. Grouping up with your friends is very easy with the Platoon System. Gameplay is fun and requires strategy against more skilled players. You can build almost anything you could ever want as a robot to fight with. I have seen people build houses with no wheels who just sit there and blow $#!% up. Although i will not say that this game is perfect. There are some balancing issues involved. At the lower tiers, the powerful weapons can one-shot. Tier 4s can be grouped with Tier 2s on some occasions, creating a highly unbalanced match. Connection issues also exist where you will be ingame but to your friends you will be seen as offline. However this is fixed by simply restarting the game.
All things considered, Robocraft is a great all-around game for anyone. It is easy to pick up and get in to matches. But the game does like to remind you that it is still in alpha with its Connection and Balancing issues.
But what are you waiting for? Its free!

This review has changed 3 times since the start of the game, and this says a lot about the developer. The game has gone from a really fun idea executed terribly flawed, to a midground, to being a pretty well polished experience that's loads of fun. The creativity you can see in robot designs as well as the team's constant quality updates means this game is well worth a look.
Important notes:
*This is not an abandoned early access game, updates are frequent, significant, and are always exciting!
*The free to play does mean people can pay to advance a bit, but they can't pay to win. All cash-shop-only parts pretty much just make your robot worse by adding nothing but making you more visible. You also can't advance to the endgame with cash shop money, the new megabot tier cannot be bought with premium currency.
*The game manages a good mix of skill and build quality, where in order to be the best you both need a quality robot and good gameplay skill, neither feel lacking.
Really with this game being a 5 minute download, free to play but not pay to win, and receiving frequent updates, there's no reason not to give this a try if you're interested in the idea

I am surprised that this is Early Alpha, because I did not have any problems with bugs so far (although it could simply be luck). I swear that I played full releases that were way buggier than this.
Basically you sculpt your vehicle from scratch and then engage in team warfare. The customization possibilities are endless. Heavily armored tanks, agile snipers, hover tanks, airplanes or just something funny like a submarine with wheels attached. There are many designs that can be very effective using the right approach.
It is a lot of fun to just tinker with your design and gradually improve it. Vehicles are made up of blocks and after each battle you can examine the damage. Just died from one hit? There is probably a vulnerability that needs to be mitigated. Or perhaps you took a ton of hits and just would not die. In that case it is very satisfying to see that all of the design elements worked perfectly - shields and armor absorbing most of the damage and protecting vital areas, such as weapon placements, propulsion and the driver.
One of the best things about this game is that every vehicle is unique. In every game you get to admire the creations of your teammates and opponents. Their vehicles can be functional, beautiful, funny or downright ridiculous. This way you can also get new ideas to try for yourself.

Love her or hate her, the demented, psychotic AI known as GLaDOS is back for some more portal-opening (and closing) fun! Portal 2 continues the story of the original game, with GLaDOS somehow managing to make a return. As usual, the puzzles introduced in the main single-player campaign are challenging and require patience and lots of thinking to solve. But that's the fun of Portal, that feeling you get and that little "OHHHH!" in your head that you have once you solve a particularly challenging level. Once again, GLaDOS torments you as you progress through the levels, but hey, admit it; Part of you WANTS to hear her gloating at you as you struggle through her "tests". Besides single-player, Portal 2 introduces a multiplayer challenge as well, bringing yet more playtime to the game. The multiplayer campaign is better played with a friend over Skype, so it's easier to communicate, but Valve has ensured that you are equipped with many pointers and icons to signal to your partner over the net if it's someone you don't know. And if you think your brain is finally done solving portal puzzles after the multiplayer campaign, think again! With so many active modders and mapmakers in the Steam community, single-player or multi-player maps can be downloaded at any time from the Steam workshop! Which basically means an endless supply of maps to play and puzzle about! May GLaDOS have mercy on your mind.

It would be a crime to not recommend this game.
Now, the old Portal was very good; it was a new concept, but it wasn't fully developed. Portal 2 is fully developed. The storyline is about six times longer and three times more fun as Portal, the graphics are incredible, the controls are better suited, the environment is more realistic, the voice acting is amazing, the levels are smarter, and I could go on. And just to make things better, you get the level editor and co-op mode.
What can I say? A very nice game that makes you play again and again. Each time trying to figure out new ways to pass the levels.

Being a fan of sandbox games myself, Robocraft seemed like a good game to try out, and it is. The fact that people can be creative with their robots and prove their skills in battle is what makes the game fun for me. While there are some things that need tweaking *cough* railguns *cough*, there are still many aspects of the game that makes me keep coming back to it. The game itself is a challenge because of the "cat and mouse" game people play in order to create the best robot. If you ever get frustrated at parts of the game, you can always go to the Steam Community for help. Whenever you need help creating a new robot, coming up with tactics against new enemies, or just want to talk casually about the game, just post a discussion and the community responds. This is one game that I'll be keeping in mind every time I start my Steam client.
EDIT (As of April 2016): With the removal of the pilot seat and introduction of health regeneration after 10 seconds out of combat, I can't recommend because essentially each vehicle is now just a health pool and increasing your overall dps through more guns or higher tier guns is more effective than trying to pick off important components, especially when said target can just chill around the corner for 10 seconds to regain all their health.
EDIT(As of May 2016): With introduction of loot crates, has made getting items less of a grind. Game is fun but only with friends.

This is one of those games were you know that only the biggest and dumbest fanboys were voting for it on Greenlight (Which is one of the many reasons Greenlight is a flawed concept but that's beyond the point.) how anyone could find this enjoyable, playable, or even in a state where it could be released is beyond me. This game is marketed as a Minecraft WOT hybrid which is true to an extent but this game unlike either of those games it gets nothing right and has awful replayability, now you can say that this game is still in alpha so critizing it at this point is wrong at you would be right if it didn't have premium accounts and a microtransaction system that seems to be more developed than the game itself showing that the game is meant to be in a state where it is playable so critizing it is okay in my  book. Speaking of this microtransaction system now would be a great time to get into it, you see this game has a thing called "Galaxy Cash" which is a currency that you pay real money for and can be used to buy parts at a much cheaper price than the normal currency called "robopoints" now these points can also be used to buy a premium account which increases everything you earn from matches by 50% and because of the ridiculous cost of parts on this game (A t9 part can easily run above 60,000 points but for a person who payed they only cost about 500 or less galaxy cash.) this system gives a ridiculous bonus to the paying players which is a awful way to sustain a f2p game.
Now next thing I want to discuss is the gameplay which should be the most important thing and it seems like the devs have put a notable amount of effort into it but there are numerous flaws in the game that hinder this such as the lackluster spoting system and the failure of certain weapons to mesh with the game, for instance the railgun has a massive problem on older maps and seems very clunky and awkward to use most of the time which when combined with the huge problem in balance this game have creates a very bad experiance when playing. This problem seems universal to all weapons in one way or another and I feel like the devs need to put a lot of work into this before it's out of the alpha. Movement in this game is.....strange to say the least. You see there are 3 main ways to move around in Robocraft and they aren't very well implemented at the moment leading to some very awkward and annoying things in the game, for instance the flying may as well be disabled for the time being until the devs can make it not be a horrible mass of problems.
Over all this game isn't very good and I question if the devs should have released it to Steam.

I had been holding back for a while on this one. I knew it would be the perfect environment for VR but I'm normally reluctant with third party Oculus Rift implementations. I finally got around to this game using Vireio Perception for VR support and very surprisingly, this peformed so well, it's actually a bit better than a few native implementations I've come across! While Perception's head tracking is by no means perfect I've been going through almost all of this game in VR so far because it's of the type that isn't too shocking, isn't too horrific, and really in many cases gives the player time to stop and look; in fact this happens extremely often.
So take this one not only as a thumbs up but as a thumbs up for those who want to relive this in VR! In my case I was lucky enough never to have played this game before stepping into this world VR style.
I started this adventure with a quick VR first impressions video, which marks the moment I initially got hooked to playing this game using my Rift DK1:
(Stereoscopic 3D video presented in the YouTube Flash player)
Since then I've tweaked the settings (seems I prefer an FOV of 120 for example, not 110 as the Vireio developers recommend) and got the hang of keeping my pitch matching my head's pitch as the mouse still affects it and this takes some getting used to.

Not much can be said on my part that hasn't already been expressed by others in ther reviews of Portal 2, but I feel that this game is the definitive adventure game sequel to come from Valve. Yes, I've played Half-Life 2. No, I didn't enjoy that. 1. Gameplay: The core idea that Portal 2 holds is very simple. Shoot two portals, walk through one, you walk out the other. But as you progress through the game it begins to add many layers to this formula which make it into the complex, semi-difficult puzzle adventure it's known as. 2. Story: While this may be somewhat odd to pick up without having played the first game, Portal 2 is definitely accessible to those new to the franchise's short plot line, and certainly welcomes them. The few characters you meet along the way all have very distinct personalities, and just ooze charm with some of their memorable quotes throughout. The main story line (SPOILER ALERT) is a sort of escape story at the start, just trying to find a way out of the clutches of GladOS, but after being betrayed by Wheatley, the story takes a turn for the more complex, giving inciteful backstory on Aperture Science and GladOS herself, makin this somewhat more entertaining for those who played through the first as well. In the end, it's got a good solid story, and the ending is amazing. Also, finding all the Rattman dens is worth your time if you're not planning to rush the game. 3. Control: The physics and controls in this game are some of the tightest I've seen in a 3D puzzle physics game, and that's absolutely necessary, because without pinpoint precision, you're not going to complete the tests, now are you? 4. Audiovisuals: The soundtrack for this game holds a mysterious feel throughout as ou explore the abandoned halls of Old and New Aperture, and although it never truly holds a forefront position in the game's atmosphere except in a few more intense situations, it holds it's own. The graphics are stellar and make for a nice attention to detail. This looks good for a game from 2011. Overall, Portal 2 is one of Valve's most solid titles and is certainly worth your time, more so than Half Life 2. And if you're seekin humor, I will say that without a doubt this game managed to make me chuckle a few times.

The concept in itself is rather cool: build you own war machine, then test it against other players.
Creating your own vehicle is in fact quite fun and satisfying.
Unfortunately, as soon as you get on the battlefield things start to go south.
Simply put, the game is terribly unbalanced.
That is caused by the fact that the game sets a limit on the total parts you can fit to your robot, but it does not set a limit on the quality of said components. That means that if you unlocked a top tier cannon, you can fit it to an otherwise barebone robot and use it against LV1 robots. Thus rookies get obliterated without a chance to fight back. It still happens to me after 8 haours of playing and it doesn't look as if it's going to end any time soon.
What's worse, because of this you also have a really, really hard time getting the points you need to get decent parts.
Realistically, the only way to unlock top tier components is to buy them with real money.
Yes, this game is most definetly a prime example of Pay-to-Win.
As for now, there's very little fun to be had, just a pitiful waste of potential.

I loved this game way back when. But what finally killed it was the crate system. I don't know what the devs were doing but it is sad to see such a great game continuously losing value. I have been playing this game for the past 3 years and have been through many of the updates including megabots, teslas, so much more. But once they started introducing the newest weapons (mid 2016) I started to hate the game. Things like rockets and shotguns and the rest became so OP. You don't even have to be hit directly with it to take massive damage. What made it worse was that you could no longer obtain as much money to build or upgrade your bot. You used to be able to go through a match if you were at least a few parts short. But in order to buy parts you have to have gc. But to get gc you have to win more battles to get more crates. Then you have to sell the items in that you may not need from the crates. But the amount you sell the items for is no where near what you need to buy more parts. So then you have to play more matches to get more crates to sell more parts. So the alternative is to spend actual cash if you want to buy stuff. Robocraft never used to be this way. I really miss the older versions and wish there was an ability to roll back and play those. Kind of like how you can choose what version to play on minecraft. It doesn't have to be 1.8.1. It could be 1.7.10 or 1.3.1 if a server is running it. Please freejam, fix the game. Just look at your ratings on steam. You used to have very possitive. It is now mixed. I don't want to see this game fade away like many others. One of these days someone may even fork it (create a robocraft clone).

I highly recommened this game. But I'll give people a rundown of the pro's and con's.
Pros-
-Very fun to build your ships while at the same time making you think about where you should put armor, weapons, electroplating ect.
-Games are quick and easy to get into, if you need to leave a game it's all good; games finish in under 8 minutes and you can leave mid game if you really need to.
-It's a pretty well balanced game; Im sure it needs a few tweaks but all the weapon class have their own weakness (such as reload rate, firing speed, accuracy ect., generally weapons will have a combination of weaknesses) which allow for gameplay to counter it. You may hear people go on about a particular weapon class, but with enough experience you can learn to cater your gameplay to reduce your weapons weakness while taking advantage of theirs.
-It's not really Pay 2 Win; alot of people like moaning about it, but the only thing that paying allows you to do is level faster or buy cosmetic items; which because of vehicle tiers means you can never be anymore overpowered then someone who has played the game up to that tier. Which is a big thumbs from me. If you payout the cash but aren't skilled you will still lose, it's just that you will progess through the tiers a little faster then you would have otherwise.
-It's an extremely well polished considering it's in Alpha, think late Beta level of polish.
Cons-
-It's an Alpha game with few developers; there are bugs, occasionaly lots of em, mostly minor, some major(platoons and friends list bugs *cough* *cough*) while they usually don't detract from the game, there are some times where it is quite frustrating. However it is in Alpha; compare it to other games in Alpha and this practicly bugless.

3. Unbalanced matchmaking: If you're tier 2, all you have access to is turrets. but somehow, someone else has plasma cannons and railguns. This doesn't seem to be a problem until you realize that you can be one-shot by superior tech.
Overall, this game was okay until you realize how annoying it is to get through the tiers. You can tell by my hours how quickly you'll realize this. If you can deal with this, or they improve it, go ahead and play it. Besides what I just mentioned, it could be fun. But at the moment, no.

Robocraft is a decent game, but needs a lot of work. I started playing when the microtransactions were already a part of the game, and to be completely honest, I was completely unaffected by it... until I reached Tier 4. The first 3 Tiers that I played were extremely fun to play with my friends, but even besides the Tier system, there was a lot that affected my experience:
- I would spend a lot of time strategically building my robot, but then when I battled, some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with a box on wheels and 6 rail/plasma guns would kill me in one damn shot. No matter how tactically you try playing, how much time you spent building your robot, how long it took you to fully upgrade your arsenal, or how strong your blocks are, you WILL eventually get wrecked with one shot.
- As you get more RoboPoints and buy stronger weapons, armor, etc, you won't notice any significant improvements to your durability or the damage to other robots. This is because everyone progresses (leveling up, advancing to the next tier, and upgrading your robot) at a similar pace, since there are no real tactics to use that will get you to advance much faster than the other players. Your survival is based off of how lucky you are when you're out in the field, or how long you hide for the duration of the match.
- What happened to me in Tier 4 (maybe it'll happen to you in different Tiers) is that you're going to die A LOT more frequently. What's the biggest issue to this? Well, let's say you get killed in a match and you earn 800 RP total, but you need to pay 700 RP to repair your robot. If you didn't get a kill/assist (and good luck getting more than 2 kills) or captured the base, you'll only get 100 RP profit (a new gun can cost 4,600 RP). You also won't get ANY Tech Points, which are used for unlocking new upgrades. Right now, I need about 30 TP to unlock a new gun, but I practically get 1-3 TP every 30 minutes. How the ♥♥♥♥ am I going to upgrade at this rate? From here on, you will get less RP/TP due to less kills and more deaths, and it will take you days to finally completely upgrade a function for your robot.. unless you're a member.. and we all know how that goes.
- The Ice maps are nice, but the Mars maps are dull and not immersive at all.
There are plenty more problems, but these are the ones that affected me the most. Your experience with this game may be entirely different, but chances are that they'll be more similar than not. I suggest that you wait for better updates and fixes to be released, but until then, I wouldn't recommend Robocraft.

A shameless clone of World of Tanks for the action game, and a very fun and thought provoking building game for designing your robots.
This game is essentially battlebots - Online Minecraft edition.
When you build your robot, you have to put thought into your build, and how it'll perform in combat.  When you're finish, you enter combat.. And have the enemy instantly reveal a flaw in your awful design which you fix.  I've been playing for hours and I STILL find flaws in the tank I've been trying to perfect.
The game used to have a tech tree you'd progress up to unlock new parts.  Unfortunately, the tech tree was unbalanced with the game, meaning you spent far more time grinding for money than for tech points.  On top of this, higher tech parts were more powerful than lower tech parts, so it was a race to get to the top guns.  Many claimed the real game didn't even begin until you reached T10 and had all of the parts.  To keep new players from getting killed over and over again by high tech parts, they balanced the "roboranking" of parts so that using many high tier parts would put you in a different game than people using many low tier parts.
Later on, it was realized this encourages people to buil a bot that uses all of the roboranking they could get for their target tier.  This restricted creativity, and this system was dropped in favor of making roboranking go by numbers instead of tiers.
Even later on, it was realized that the whole idea of tech tree parts discouraged creative building, and restricting robots to one type of weapon each also enforced a meta that couldn't evolve at all.  Tech tree was removed, and all parts were consolidated into models.
This doesn't mean there's now no more tiered guns.  There are still gun tiers, so you still get to choose whether you want a strong single gun or many weaker guns, and how powerful of a weapon your bot has compared to its armour.  If you constructed a cool but tiny hull design, it would be a good idea to put weaker guns on it so you don't get into high level matches, for example.
There are a few game modes, including the pit, where it's 1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1v1... (20players) and death match, where there are no respawns.
I have two gripes with this game.
The first is the meta is not the same as it is in World of Tanks.  What I mean by this is I wish it was possible to label your robot as a scout, heavy tank, light tank, so on, and get matched into games based on that.
The second is the new paint tool allows you to paint your robot the same colour as the background and make awesome camo patterns.  I love this.  The part I don't like is the paint tool restricts CRUCIAL colours I need for my UCP!  PLS FREEJAM FIX!  also let me pick which maps I wanna play on so I don't accidentally get my epic looking white and black camo tank into a desert map..
The MOBA style gamemode is amazing.  There are three towers you need to capture.  You receive bonuses depending on how many you own.  If you own 1 tower, your team gets a shield.  If you own 2, you get a clock cycle booster which gives you free EXP.  If you own 3, you get to attack the enemy base without their shield.  As you play, the parts of your bot that shine and which ones are dull becomes more obvious as you gain levels, which automatically increase various powers.  Eventually, if you gain enough EXP, you will be capable of destroying the enemy base by yourself.  If neither team is better than the other, you can easily spend a long time just slugging back and forth and gaining tons of points for money.

This game is an innovative approach to make a World of Tanks clone with fully customizable vehicles - wheel-based, hovering or flying! It's an awesome game idea and regarding customization only your creativity is the limit. It's great to play around with realistic physical effects! Especially in lower tiers you will enjoy a lot the creativity of other players because you can really create some crazy vehicles. It's fun! In upper tiers (5+) however crazy vehicles are rare as survivability and effectivness is a must to win. Wise use of the terrain is as important as knowledge about the own robot's strengths and weakness as well as idenfying the enemy's capabilities to effectively engage them in combat. Tier 5+ is a challenge as you will notice that the players from that tier on have learned the game well. Working together as a team is the key to win now.
But light always brings some dark shadows:
* without a premium account it is really hard (but not impossible) to earn money to advance beyond tier 4 (tier 10 is the max. atm)
* with recent patches the devs have limited the access to certain modules (weapons, movement types etc.) depending on your tier level (however once reached, you can use the modules also for your lower tier "creations")
* at the current state of the game there are still some exploitable glitches (it's not dramatic, so I do not want to overrate that)
* The chat system in the game is currently at a very early state with only very limited functionality (no blacklist, no manual channel switching or possibility to create custom chat channels on an invite-base-only, etc...) with the result that people have to bear a lot of mindless comments in chat.
* there is no ingame tutorial how to use modules effectively (but the game is very intuitive). you will learn a lot by trial and error - and if you are stuck at one point, youtube is your friend!
Overall I can say if you like to play around with physical forces, you are creative, you like World of Tanks-like games, you should definitely try Robocraft!

1K+ hours played here. Time to edit my feedback.
I have been playing since Feb 2014 and the game has evolved in the right way despite some changes in the meta I believe we could have avoided such as the possibility to buy other players bots for free, for example... It actually kills creativity as well as the personal achievement to build an awesome optimized robot, as anyone can buy polished robots online for 0 credits.
I used to spend NIGHTS having fun to optimize my drones to make them as fast and strong as possible while managing weight and gun clearance. Awesome time. Unfortunately, to keep the game on the right development path without losing the building fun and exclusivity, I believe FJ should definetely do something about the CRF (internal shop to buy robots made by other players with game currency) and make robots less accessible.
Now another problem: Drones.
People complain about drones. My mates and I are always insulted as soon as we appear on their screen and open them in half. Why ? Because drones are badly seen. And this is a shame because drones are the most advanced kind of bots you can build here ! It doesn't only take you to drop 500 miserable cubes and put weapons and legs on it. It takes you hours to balance weight, to place the right elements at the right spot for damage redirection. It's not our fault if your building skills are crap ! Instead of nerfing drones, nerf the access to them ! Force players to build their own instead of people spaming transactions on the CRF. That would avoid meeting the same drones too often, and as a consequence, meeting less highly optimized drones.
My recommandation :
- Download this awesome game NOW
- Don't give up too quickly as you might meet some strong robots in front, instead, think about how to optimize your creation (should you tank ? should you dodge ? ...)
- Be mature, don't whine or insult people every game you lose. Look at yourself and train more, with some experience you will master most game mechanics.

In its current state this game needs improvement because it is becoming and possibly is one of the worst things in the free to play genere, pay to win.
While at first it seems very innocent with wonderful design concepts and fun/intuitive gameplay. soon though you will see otherwise. Its mostly at fault with its repair system.
The system starts out nice at Tiers1-2 (tiers being the closest thing to a level system) at which point it does its job. Play bad, get punished. But then it becomes a ball and chain as it saps alot at t3-5 and by t6 and up it can actually take RP (in game non paying currency) or at least 80% most games.
To top it all of even at the top gameplay tier the repair system actually pays for some of your repairs. at the beginning its all profit with this and yes by later you will lose money, but by end game they shouldn't need to deaden the weight of the repair impact to your RP right? This mechanic means the entire system is advertising the fact you can pay past the system and by the end inflates the cost to make paying a more tempting offer while completely slowing all forms of advancement to a crawl  which turns upper tiers into a pay to win system.
The game itself is still very alpha too with very broken gunplay, bugs bugs bugs, and just so exploitable on so many levels right now. That is all icing on the pay cake.
on the bright side it is innovative and interesting to start, but don't expect progression past about t6 without extreme skill or a ganking squad on your side/alternate exploits, this is without paying of course.

Buying materials from the shop (in-game or premium money works) is a good feature. Although, I don't see why they didn't just give you infinite of the free blocks rather than having to aquire more by spamming buy (despite costing nothing).

Best things about it:
1.Puzzles are entirely logical, no need to cheat. You'll feel smart when you solve it!
2.Non-violent FPS, breath of fresh air!
3.Beautifully and professionally executed. Gameplay mechanics, physics engine, flow, pace, story, sound, texture mapping and art are flawless.
4.It will really make you laugh, it leaves you with a good feeling and wanting to come back for more.
5.Map creator makes the game virtually endless.
6.Multiplayer will make you cooperate, think and communicate.
7.This game is not an automatic FPS experience, it makes you use your reflexes like any good FPS should, but also makes you use your brain.
8.Improves over Portal 1 in that smaller percentages of surface are "portal surfaces", that plus more gameplay features like colored gels offers variety and more challenge over Portal 1.
Worst things about it:
1.While it seems original and never-been-done-before, the core mechanics of it is based on an earlier game called "Narbacular Drop" and the colored gels are taken from the earlier game "Tag: The Power of Paint". It is not so much a negative as Portal is a well executed big-budget mix of earlier indie games, but it did take away from my appreciation of the originality of this game. Many indie games have great ideas that are not able to be fully executed.
2.The environments are closed-in, you will experience room after room after room, after room. Although it might seem monotonous and claustrophobic, perhaps even divorsed from reality and the outside world, it is not entirely so as there are surprises along the way that change the game path, liven thing up so to speak, and advance the story. This itself is an improvement on Portal 1, as you will experience more of the world of Portal than in Portal 1.
The bottom line:
There are not many negatives to this game, and a lot of positives. Not being a pure FPS might seem as a weakness but it is a strength as it will appeal to another side of your gaming brain and a wider pool of players. It makes it more relevant in the present and future world of gaming.

Not to mention, when you DO have a friend to play with, and assuming they actually cooperate (Get it, co-op?), it is very fun, probably even more than the single player game. Speaking of single player, the main campain is very interesting, and the story is interesting, with a midway plot twist, and technically a side-plot. Completing the game, (In other words, getting all of the acheivments) Is very possible and actually kind of fun to do. It's almost like trying to find all of the content compared to actually using  ~ amazing skills ~ to get any of the achievments. (Except for the time trails). The community maps can add difficulty to those who actually want the difficulty, instead of the achievments. What a hard, almost impossible puzzle? Look through some of the community maps. Or make one, that works too.
Anyways, the music works really well with the atmosphere of the game. The music typically comes up whenever you happen to come across a puzzle, especially in the test chambers. What I loved about the music in Portal 2 is when you are flying through the air, whether because of the blue or orange gel, or because of the launch pads, overlapping music that would sound awesome on its own matching the existing music and it sounds great! The music itself sounds amazing to. The techno music fits the futuristic, robot apocalyptic atmosphere perfectly. The atmosphere itself makes the game just standout not only as a puzzle game, but as an adventure game, too. One of the main reasons I didn't go insane while I was trying to figure out a puzzle is the story, which is amazing on its own right. The story, (No spoilers don't worry) is set in a robotic apocalyptic setting, where the robots have taken over. You are a lab rat, going through experiment after experiment. Things have changed since the first game though. Everything is rotten, plants are overgrowing alot of it, and everything just seems discombobulated (is that a word?); and the atmosphere reflects this perfectly.
Overall, the game is very good, but for me, it was short lived. But, with Co-op and community maps, and the workshop enabled, this game can last quite a while. Even if you do play the entire game in one sitting, I guarantee that one sitting would last for more than 24 hours.

That's 100 continues for you in late tier and generous of the devs for a F2P plus, CP values in the market is justifiable. Gameplay-wise by not respawning, the game pasing feels fast and the more you participate in group battles rewards you better than hiding behind your tail and just trying to capture the base for the faster result, in that way the devs are motivationg you for good team combat rather than faster and lame winning condition.
The goodies:
- Low spec., runs fast.

- Physics and the damage value is good. You won't see anything flip flopping arround unless your craft gets so much spank.
- Fun and fast shooter.
- Reasonable F2P business model.
On the negative side:
- In game battle user interface is confusing...REALLY confusing at first until you get used to it.
- team colors are not definably solid to one side. Blue is = to ally and Red is = to enemy...its the same in the other side.
What it needs soon:
- A collosal boss battle.
- UI fix.
- Team color fix.
In the end I recomend this and is a thumbs up. This is a early access game and review so this may differ in the near future. What i can say is try it your self and look what i am saying.

Well, i honestly can say: I dont know what all the rant is about!
With this said, i will talk a little about the game:
Right now, in the Alpha on 11th August '14, you got 3 weapon types (Artillery, Machiene Guns, Sniper), several ways of moving (with wings, hooverthingies, wheels, and some Heliumqubes that simply make you robot lighter than air). You are completely free to arrange all the qubes you bought into whatever order to achieve a nice-looking, purposefull robot, or some mix looking like a Frankensteinian monster.
The weapons actually feel pretty balanced if you got the right robot under your♥♥♥♥♥(i dont know what all those guys rage about... snipers have reload times of over 30 seconds... just drive FAST in their face and kill them!) and the maps do help you with every way you want to play the game, just dont be a noob (newbie out of brain).
The ingame-money is achieved by damaging, scouting, killing, assisting and capping. You use this to repair all the damage you took in-fight, and you use this to buy new blocks to make even better robots (so all the idiots can qq around how SMGs suck... while they died camping in their base, fighting 3 snipers). All the guys talking about only getting arround 800 of the ingame-money honestly just suck, i get that money when i play on Tier2 (of 10) and only damage 1 Enemy and then die (WITHOUT PREMIUM!). Ofcourse i have to pay the robot, which will cost on this Tier like 400. But if you are only a decent player you will get almost all the time arround 1k, so you have to play 2 rounds to get a new gun, a new pair of wheels or whatnot (more rounds if you want higher-tierstuff...logically)
Having a premium actually fastens this up (by 50%, so instead of 500 you get 750), same for techpoints (which you need to reearch new parts so you can buy them and get into the next tier).
The gameplay is, as said, pretty nice. You can build lots of different thingies, like buggys, big fat tanks, driving pyramids (a often used shape), trucks that look like transporters or just a set of wheels with enough qubes to get your weapons on (they need some space in between each). But not only weels, but aso planes are buildable, and hover-tanks, and satelites, and baloons, and with the help of thruster jumping-cars.
The Weapons are Plasmacannons (artillery, all cannons fire at once, then like 3-4 seconds reload time), SMGs (each SMG you add will increase your overall firerate, as only one fires then the next) and Railguns (snipers, you get a ~3ß second reload time and then you can shoot with ever Railgun once, if you shot all...you have to wait), the damage is done as you would think...artillery has a big ♥♥♥♥ing splash and can onehit like a sniper, but aiming sux a bit, SMGs have barely or no splash and you need to fire a few rounds to eat through the enemy, and Snipers have a splash, but if you hit there is a big ♥♥♥♥ing hole. Counterplay is the same as in every game... Arty -> you can see where they shoot, dont be blind or lame and move your♥♥♥♥♥ SMGs -> dude, they cant aim, ask you sniper to kill them, Sniper -> get a second Pair of steering wheels and a good speed, drive up to them (los your first pair of steering wheels) and show them how SMGs work.
The Damage-Model is pretty cool too, if anyone of you played World of Tanks and WarThunder, its the later one that is comparable. The modules or qubes you destroy will fall off. So if someone has a long stick with wheels, shoot into the middle and see his car losing 50% of its heallth and everything that is not attached to the controllunit of his robot.
Right now there are 5 maps with different obstacles ( the 1 birdge in the middle map with only 2 small ways on the side; a big open place with only a few waves in the ground to hide; part-icemaps where you almost cant controll ground vehicles) and a different set of truly good bots on each of them.
The Rankingsystem is pretty okay, as everypart has some "Robotranking", the higher the overallvalue of your bot is, the higher the value is that of your enemeys (ranging from T1-T10). You gain research points in every of those Tiers, with these you can research the parts of the next Tier, then buy them and♥♥♥♥♥enemys up.
The Premiumfees are very, very low (btw...), for 3 month you pay no 20 euro, then you get 50% more ingame currencies, which helps, but is not needed if you are willing to make 50% more games (in T4 you need like 7-10 games to pay a T5 weapon, so nothing to bad)
The Interface is very nice, you dont need much keys to controll your bot, and they are very well placed on standart. The HUD  wont disturb you on your killingsprees, but it will help you keep track of stuff.
The Bugs.... well, this is a alpha, so you have to look over some of them! But hey... there are barely some to look over! You ahve some "stuckpoints", but i never encountered one, sometimes the game crashes (for me like once every 1.5 hours... which is totaly okay) or when you do something specific, untill last patch i wasnt able to minimize while in battle ie. One problem that sux is that there is a pesky bug where Platoons (groups of players that play together) sometimes have enourmous waiting times, but the devs are looking for the problem and try to get rid of it. until then: just regroup or just restart the game... thats way faster than to wait 1.5 minutes.
Since today they introduced ranked games, which is pretty cool, and the way they handled this is awesome too, as the queuingtimes wont change at all (and they are pretty low... 2-10 seconds most of the time). The ranking is made by the average ingame-money (without premium of repairfees) you made in your last 15 matches, and you have a list in which all of your friends are listed).
Ohhh, and one last word (respect if you made it down here!): Just try the game, its small (700mb) and it wont cost you anything (except maybe your soul and a girlfriend and your job and all of your nonexisting your sociallife)

RoboCraft is great in concept, and until recently I would have recommend it, but now with the most recent series of changes made to the game, I would not recommend the game. The pay wall has become painfully obvious. To that end a good example of this is that with the recent changes you no longer can access a true flying vehicle until you reach around tier four unless you want to convert techpoint to overall techpoint which costs. This is not the first update that removed features that allow more than ground vehicles early in the game without paying. Also in recent update they have removed a few early tier weapons.
I feel that with each of these updates the game is losing its originality and uniqueness. To compound this fact with each of the updates the robot’s in at least 1-3 have become more and more cookie cutter in style simply because you are unable to build unique vehicles that function because of the lack of variety of parts available at the lower tiers. Best things about it:
1.Puzzles are entirely logical, no need to cheat. You'll feel smart when you solve it!
2.Non-violent FPS, breath of fresh air!
3.Beautifully and professionally executed. Gameplay mechanics, physics engine, flow, pace, story, sound, texture mapping and art are flawless.
4.It will really make you laugh, it leaves you with a good feeling and wanting to come back for more.
5.Map creator makes the game virtually endless.
6.Multiplayer will make you cooperate, think and communicate.
7.This game is not an automatic FPS experience, it makes you use your reflexes like any good FPS should, but also makes you use your brain.
8.Improves over Portal 1 in that smaller percentages of surface are "portal surfaces", that plus more gameplay features like colored gels offers variety and more challenge over Portal 1.
Worst things about it:
1.While it seems original and never-been-done-before, the core mechanics of it is based on an earlier game called "Narbacular Drop" and the colored gels are taken from the earlier game "Tag: The Power of Paint". It is not so much a negative as Portal is a well executed big-budget mix of earlier indie games, but it did take away from my appreciation of the originality of this game. Many indie games have great ideas that are not able to be fully executed.
2.The environments are closed-in, you will experience room after room after room, after room. Although it might seem monotonous and claustrophobic, perhaps even divorsed from reality and the outside world, it is not entirely so as there are surprises along the way that change the game path, liven thing up so to speak, and advance the story. This itself is an improvement on Portal 1, as you will experience more of the world of Portal than in Portal 1.
The bottom line:
There are not many negatives to this game, and a lot of positives. Not being a pure FPS might seem as a weakness but it is a strength as it will appeal to another side of your gaming brain and a wider pool of players. It makes it more relevant in the present and future world of gaming.

I originally liked this game when it came out. It was a fun and interesting idea. I tried the various weapons and movement pieces and I came to the conclusion that I like the Rail Cannons, so I made my way to getting the best ones of those I could, which ended up being T3. Not long after I do so, an update comes out where I can't get the next level of them until Tier 4, which is reasonable, and I still got to keep the Rail Cannons I had, thus helping me get into Tier 3 and almost to Tier 4. Then I sign on today only to find they have rendered some blocks "obsolete". Not because the blocks were actually useless or anything, but rather they had to take them away from everyone who had them because new players couldn't access them until higher tiers.
In terms of fairness, sure, I can understand. But my whole setup was built around those Railguns, and suddenly I have to improvise with the other weapons because I don't want to dismantle the vehicle I have so that it's ready when I get the T4 Rail Cannons, but I don't have the RP to just make another T3-4 vehicle, since I'm not being destroyed and repairs cost like 90% of whatever I won in the previous match. And yes, I know they refunded all the RP from the pieces taken away, but I have to buy super expensive weapons to replace them to be in Tier 4 to get T4 Tech Points, meaning that when I do unlock the ability to get the next Rail Cannons, I'll be too poor ro afford all that many, and for Rail Cannons to be effective, you need more than one.
I understand this is an early access game, and people just jumping in now might enjoy it, but if it continues to do stuff like this, I don't think the game is all that great. Perhaps when the game is fully released and "done", such drastic changes won't happen anymore and the game can finally settle and be alright, but right now its like all the players are getting into a comfortable position only for Robocraft to then flip the couch they are all sitting in and putting in a different couch.
Also, changing the tech tree like you did because some people felt overwhelmed is really dumb. I wasn't overwhelmed and it was nice to be able to experiment with low level versions of the aerofoil for example, so I could see how it works and know if I want to spend any higher tier TP on them. But now I have to wait until I'm higher than what I am now to try and make an airplane, which will be expensive as heck, and probably a waste, but can I try making a cheaper version now to see if I even like it? Nope. And trying to keep everyone from experiencing the full game is bull. This game has upgrades and advancement, so having access to all the low tier stuff right off isn't a bad thing. Games like CoD have at least 1 version of most guns available at the start, but people still keep playing the crap out of it. (I don't know why though, as CoD also sucks, but I'm just making a comparison) Halo doesn't even have weapon and tech advancement (except maybe 4 in a way). All guns on each map are available to each person, and every still plays the crap out of it as well. (Which is good, as Halo is an awesome game)
I hope the game ends up well, but for now, the Early Access stamp should just be avoided.

I still love this game even after having spent 65 hours with it.
The singleplayer experience is amazing; although the game takes place in a totally wrecked Aperture Laboratories, alluding to the - spoiler alert - destruction of GLADOS in
, the plot of
remains independent, allowing the game to stand alone well.
In the game, the player is greeted by Wheatley, a spherical character who guides you through the Aperture Laboratories facility. As the game progresses, he/she is introduced to the game's identifying elements: the isolation placed upon the player by the enviroment, the Portal Gun, and GLADOS.
The player feels incredibly alone in this game: aside from Wheatley and GLADOS, the tester's assistant's voice and Cave Johnson's voice are the only other additional human elements in the game. He/she is left to solve the many puzzles that obstruct your path one after the other. As the game progresses, he/she is introduced to more and more puzzle elements, leading toward challenging "test chambers" by the end of the game. The dreary soundtrack and lack of noise from Mother Nature leave the player to himself/herself and to solving the puzzle. The world manages to immerse the player in the deserted yet oddly realistic world that is Aperture Laboratories.
Solving "test chambers" relies on the player utilizing the Portal Gun to the fullest. The Portal Gun, introduced to the player early in the game, allows him/her to teleport to various locations within a chamer in order to solve it. Passing through these chambers requires creativity, out-of-the-box thinking, and coordination: portals summoned by the Portal Gun maintain the velocity of anyone or anything flying through them.
GLADOS is a main character in the game but is not the guiding light to the plot like in
. In
, the guiding light in the plot lies between the conflict with Wheatley and GLADOS; as the player advances in the game, he/she will learn what fueled this conflict and what its impact is on the story.
When one is finished with the singleplayer,
has additional content to keep the user busy. Challenge Mode offers the player the chance to complete an already solved puzzle in the fastest and most efficient way possible, focusing on using as little time and as few Portals as possible.
In addition, the game's multiplayer mode is as solid as the singleplayer mode. The multiplayer is an extension to the singleplayer story; the main characters are GLADOS and her two robotic test subjects Atlas and P-Body. Atlas and P-Body are tasked with working together to solve "test chambers" that are otherwise unsolvable with only one person around. The emphasis on coordination is vital to winning the game; since the story is strictly two-man co-op, it is imperative that both players have an idea of what to do.
TIP: Keep a voice chat with your co-op buddy. One way of starting a voice chat is by clicking the arrow in the Steam overlay's chat window and clicking "Start Voice Chat."
After completing both the singleplayer and multiplayer game, the adventure does not stop. Ever since the game was linked with the Steam Workshop with the Perpetual Testing Iniative update in 2011, users have been submitting their own test chambers left and right. Many of these chambers are challenging and take liberties with level standards as well as throw in their own style in utilizing the game's elements. The game provides a level creation tool which is rather comprehensive; however, more sophisticated levels can be developed using the Hammer tool, a piece of software found in the Source SDK (Windows only).
The only problem I found with this game is that certain puzzles were hard; however, these puzzles were hard simply because I wasn't a great problem solver that time. Upon watching a walkthrough for the chambers I was stuck on, I realized that there was a practical solution to each and every one of them. Playing more puzzles allows players to become better at this game, and there are no levels in either of the main games that involve impossible-to-execute solutions.
I recommend this game highly to anyone interested in puzzle games in general. Valve has made this game have well-crafted and solvable levels and worlds, amazing aesthetics, a great soundtrack, and a sense of eternal fun. It is worth investing the twenty dollars as the experience is
unforgettable.
10/10. A+. 100%.
P.S. In multiplayer, players can let their Atlas and/or P-Body characters wear hats (which is seen frequently in
, another game by Valve).

A bit of disclaimer, I joined late, so I never get to experience that pre-premium era, so yeah, disclaimer end.

1.5x exp & RP for premium players? I'm fine with that. I didn't really quite feel the set back that non-premium player feels.
Rail Gun is OP? Yeah, they are, but hey, they earned it. And if they can squeeze a rail gun in a T1/2/3 game? Well, it gives double the excitement when you finally bring it down with your teammates. And if you unfortunetly become the cannon fodder, oh well, you still gain more RP than you initially started, so that's all good.
Remember, everyone wants to win, but someone got to lose. And plus, it's not like I lose all the time. And if you are wondering, at T1/2, my current win rate is around 1/3, and I'd say that's reasonable because 1/3 is the chances of our team succeed, 1/3 is the chances of our team fail, and 1/3, well, that's just being cannon fodder to those who came back down a tier to grind for more RP to buy more items to go higher tier. So, yeah, 1/3 win rate is pretty reasonable.
Now, as to what Flame Soulis has pointed out, impatient teammates who will ram into you and flip you up-side down - Well, that is why there's a BALANCER, GO GET IT. Well, I'd say the first question you should ask is, did you even take your bot out for a run in practice? I can bet alot of people doesn't and just decided to charge into real battle, only then when they realized that they have some fault in their bots.
So, yeah, those are my opinions, thanks for reading.

If World of Tanks and Minecraft are two of your favorite games, Robocraft is a must play. It uses the simple but easy to use voxel block style of building Minecraft is famous for, while utilizing World of Tanks' style matchs for gameplay.
Your building skills will be put to the test in this game, and while anything is possible, only the successful designs will win the day. There are dozens of different roles you can build your robot into.
Tanks, Planes, Artillery, and Snipers are just a few of the many kinds of craft you can build.
There is a pratice mode avaliable to test out your creations before going into battle, sparing you from spending half an hour building your bot only to realize that it can't move.
The Free-to-Play model here is very well developed. Everything in the game can be earned without spending any sort of cash, the only items that can only be bought with cash are entirely cosmetic and have no function gameplay wise. The rest of the blocks and weapons can be bought using the in game currency, RoboPoints (RP) that you earn every match.
In every match up until tier 4-5, you will ALWAYS make more RP than what is needed to repair your craft regardless of victory or death. After tier 5, you will need to use some skills and tactics in order to make a profit.
Most of the game is fairly balanced at the moment.
The infamous Railgun, commonly known as the "point-and-kill" weapon, has an emormous reload time and is difficult to use unless a player is completely still while firing.
It is purely a sniping weapon and as soon as anyone gets up and close with you, you can wave your bot goodbye as the turrets turn quite slowly, leaving you defenseless.
The Plasma Cannon is another widely critizized weapon due to its area of effect damage. However, as long as you play properly and build your craft well, dodging these weapons is simple as they projectiles have slow travel times and are very visible.
The SMG is commonly claimed as underpowered, but when used en mass, they can shed any craft apart at close range, and the higher tier versions can make for an effective long range weapon when used correctly.
As for the payment models used, I do not agree with the many players who claim this game to be "Pay-to-Win".
I strongly feel it is much more of a "Pay-for-Convinece" game as the tech tree model along with how the matchmaking works, prevents players with higher level craft from entering most lower tier matches.
While players can use higher tier weapons in lower tier matches, the resulting craft are usually fairly easy to kill as they cannot use higher tier armor and usually use inferior versions.
In the end, the player who has all the parts will still need to create a working craft, as there is no such thing as the perfect craft. Each craft built is specialized for different roles depending on how they are made, not to mention how well they are made.
The only benifit I see from buying parts and tech points is when you don't have to time to grind your way towards them.
There are no "premium parts" that gives paying players any advantage over non-paying players, the only things that count on the battlefield is your building, piloting, and fighting skills. Paying for items in this game only lets you get them sooner.
In the end, Robocraft is a well made, fun to play game with lots of potential. Updates are on the way with new features and the game allows players to get into a new match quick and easy after death, unlike WoT.
I strongly recommend RoboCraft to anybody who loves to create things and would love to see them fight against other player's creations from around the world.

Overhauled Review Update: May 31st, 2016
I've continued to follow Robocraft for the course of nearly two years, and the game has certainly gone through a rollercoaster of good and bad times. The most controversial update in recent times is the overhaul of its rewards system, which is a luck-based loot system that improves your odds of better items with game progression and scoring in your matches. While some enjoy the new changes, others loathe it due to its supposed gambling system, and in a game like Robocraft that attracts a younger audience, it's not the most enthusiastic change.
Do I still recommend this game? Of course I do; the core of Robocraft hasn't changed, and it's still a building and shooting game to its fullest. Overall, the game handles well with most major bugs and issues being resolved quickly (most!). The diversity of game modes can appeal to a high variety of players, and with more content being added, not to mention an increasing connection with the community to help benefit the game, I feel that the game is going in a promising direction. It's always worth it to download the game and give it a whirl since there is no dedication or money required to enjoy the game, but those who enjoy it are absorbed into playing the game for hours to try out everything the game has to offer.

I've played this game for the past few days now and from what I've gotten out of it are these four words: Overpowered Unbalanced Weapons System.
I cannot count the number of times in which I am in a tier 1-2 server and getting decimated by players with weaponry and defense that is supposed to be on a tier 4-6 server.
If you put a tier 3+ railgun or plasma gun on a robot whose tier is less that 3, that robot's tier should either automatically boost up to tier 3, or be restricted until that robot becomes tier 3.
So many players are tired of being one-shotted and hit-and-run by these practical nukes-of-weapons. The railgun is almost always a one hit kill, so long as the victim has weak enough armor. I despise players on servers who shouldn't be using weapons that are not the correct tier.
"Oh, you just need to get more experienced and buy better things."
To that I say ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, because in order to unlock things, you need Tech Tokens. Once you have enough Tech Tokens you can spend them at the Tech Tree, unlocking better weapons and defense.
However, the only way to obtain said Tokens is two things: Damaging/destroying an enemy, and winning a match.
Well, since I keep getting instagibbed by a railgun or plasma weapon, I can't kill any enemies quick enough. Since the other team has an overpowered weapon, my team (more often than not) gets destroyed in a mere couple of minutes, provided that my team isn't hiding or moving around.
Due to the fact that my team loses and I can't get a kill off of any enemies because I die so quickly, I can't get any Tech Tokens to spend in the Tech Tree, thus preventing me progressing my weaponry and defense.
Do you see what I'm saying?
The whole game depends on whether or not you are lucky enough to not be killed by an OP weapon, or if your team isn't stupid enough to capture the enemy base. If you aren't lucky, you can't progress.
Don't get me wrong, the game is a wonderful concept. Build robots and duke it out with other robots. But, this game didn't execute it very well, seeing as you can't battle people you want to battle.

Robocraft: an excellent game   BIG REVIEW
Robocraft is an excellent free to play game. one of the best parts about Robocraft is the feeling that you built this awesome machine of destruction and now you get to put it on the battlefield to destroy others creations (or get destroyed). One of the biggest things I question about this game is why everybody is calling it pay to win. Why do you think this? Galaxy credits, (The premium currency) gives advantages like 50% more robo-points, tech points, etc, but these can all be unlocked without the premium currency, it just takes more time. There is nothing you can't add to the tech tree that can only be paid for with galaxy credits. Sometimes the reason you see people with tier 3 or 4 weapons in a tier 1 match is because they have unlocked that weapon as they progressed, then built another robot with those high-tier parts. It does not necessarily mean they bought them. Even with just a small investment in time, I have been able to reach tier 3, the area with the high-powered weapons, and i have made a Tier 1 robot with those weapons. You DON'T have to pay. The only big advantage you have is maybe a four-man platoon. But that doesn't inhibit gameplay. So now that that aspect is covered, I'll talk about game play.
The game play is very fun, especially for an early acess game. while the creation part of the robot could be easier and faster, its just fine for where this game is in developent. Some better physics might help too but once again, it is fine for how far the game is. For right now there are only a handful of maps, which are just desert, and ice maps. More map variety in the future would be great. maybe add a city map, or a space station, or even a jungle area (i know the maps are based on mars, but hey, it could be a future, terraformed mars). Another thing that would be good if we can have more game modes. The control-point type game is definitely fun, but maybe adding game modes like, arena, capture the flag, or just straight team death match with re-spawn. (i know, the way this game is made re-spawn won't happen, just wishful thinking.) also about "rebuilding" the ship. When the ship is totaled, maybe you could give non-members just a little bit more robo points, maybe an increase of 15% so they feel like entering a battle is useless and they can't level up fast enough. Because your ship will be totaled. a lot.
Lastly, whenever my friends and i play, we have trouble with platoons and joining a game. we usually have to join the queue at the exactly the same time if we want to be placed in the game. Otherwise, even though it says the estimated time of waiting could be like 10 seconds, you can wait 2, 3, 4, minutes and still wont be put in a game. That is maybe the biggest issue in the game for me. But any way, this game really in the end is great, and I look forward to more updates and better game play. if you have not played this game, definitely try it out!
EDIT: since I've played a little bit more over the past few weeks, one other problem has surfaced. Sometimes I will be put in a game and the world around me will be completely frozen. My friends say they can see me move and shoot and do everything i would normally do, but the world around me is frozen. I can even see what they're typing in chat but i can't participate in the battle in a practical manner. Hopefully this problem will be fixed in the near future. This does not change the way i fell about this game, it is still great.

After putting many hours and reading the thumbs down reviews I felt I should bring up counter arguments to some of the "negatives" people claim this game has, plus add my point of view.
1) First off, you are playing a game in officially ALPHA, that means PRE BETA, that means FAR from finished (Not that it really looks that way)...that means the game play, pay to win stuff, number of maps, etc may or may not change completely.
2) It's true they only have a couple of maps, but how many glitches or problems are there in these maps? Near none that I have seen in all my hours of gameplay. The only glitch I have seen 4 times (once with myself) was spawning and falling through the map upon hitting the ground. Asides from that you can get stuck in some rock stuff when you fall off a cliff in nearly every map and hopefully that will be fixed up.
3) In ANY game, people will be as cheap and sinister/tricky/abusive as possible to gain any cheap♥♥♥♥♥upper hand possible, like sky camping rail gunners with guns from tiers 2 lvls higher and whatever else was talked about in other reviews. BUT here's good news, those instant kill rail guns and cannons were nerfed, now smg'ers stand a chance in hell. That plus you can always adapt, redesign your bot, shield your pilot so you are less likely to get 1 hit, put high lvl blocks around your pilot, etc.
4) Don't QQ cause you can't play, learn from your deaths, protect your wheels, shield your top from sky bombers and sky snipers, aim for your opponents weapons to blast them off and render them harmless, and most of all, teamwork man.
**5) This is a teamwork game, albeit many players don't play like it. So here is teamwork adice that can help you win matches...
Don't chase a near dead guy down a huge cliff like a bozo just for that extra kill, you not being there to backup the others when they meet 3+ enemies or to catpture their base as fast can literally be the difference between winning and lossing the battle. That scenario looks even more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when TWO people chase them down a cliff -.-
I also see soooo many people concentrate 100% on trying to finish off some near dead guy with hardcore armor blocks in a desperate attempt to get just 1 kill while being blown to bits by another enemy, when they could have potentially survived and gotten 2 kills instead of just 1 or 0 simply by using their head...
Don't worry, missing a kill or getting a mere assist won't end time as we know it, if everyone played like this battles would be a little more hardcore (in a good way), and you'll pass by near dead guys more often you can finish off, giving you a kill PLUS giving someone else an extra assist :)
Still a fantastic game, remember it's online multiplayer, and it can be a grind, that's normal as there are only 10 tiers.
Best of all it's free, so who cares, try it out, it's damn fun!

I want to love this game. I want to build my giant shield robot and guard my allies with it while our smaller robots capture enemy points and have tactics, but I can't. Alot of things in this game can be summed up with "You can't do that," same with games like Planetside 2. However, this game suffers from an even smaller game, and no MMO, wheras PS2 is large, so even an avid explorer can have fun in it.
You want to put a cannon on your robot? Well too bad! you have to play 24/7 for maybe a few months and then maybe you could afford to get that high up on the tech-tree. You want to be a jet? HA, you don't have the parts.
I admit, I haven't played much, but what I did notice is that people with money immediatley win. The reason this is is because of how the tiers work. You can buy tech, and parts, with real cash. this essentially means you can have a robot with a single, weak gun, verses a giant rocket-launching jet-plane from hell, but that's only if you manage to move past spawn!
Yes my friends, you read that right. Spawn is your REAL enemy. My robot, which I designed to LITERALLY not be able to flip over, flipped over a piece of geometry so hard I swear I could see the moon in close enough range to see the moon landing flag.
I recommend this game only to people who have alot of time and alot of patience. unlocking everything is the only real time you actually have a fair game - everyone has the same amount of placable parts, and everyone has the same gear, meaning the only thing left in your way is your building, and the pre-mentioned geometry. However, if you don't want to use 5 month's worth of full time job to buy every part ever, and don't have a year's worth of free time, thne this game is not for you. In fact, it isn't for you even if you DID have the money or time for it, just to spite the awful developer who decided that pay-to-win was a good idea. Shame on you.
To be honest though, I did thoroughly enjoy the game, to the point where I now miss it. However, I am not going to change the rating of my review, seeing as, while I will be playing it more and more recently, I really do think these are things that need to change - leveling up and achieving  parts should either bring more parts for your buck, or more rewards outside of leveling up.

Portal 2 lives up to the high expectations placed upon it after the award winning portal, and surpasses them.
For those who don't know, here's how the game works, you start off learning the very basics of the game in the way valve does best, with humor and semi-realistic reasons for it being explained. After you get the hang of moving and controlling your camera, you get the device called a portal gun, this lets you shoot 2 portals that are connected, from there you are released upon the rest of the game. Using gravity and portals, you fling yourself around the game to complete different objectives, with new things being added as the game goes on, but at a pace that the player has completely learned the use of something previous before the new items.
Valve lives up to its name once again with this game that uses humor, story telling, and puzzles in ways never before used. I definite must buy if you can afford it.

Despite that it's still in it's "Early Alpha", the game certainly is fun and has a lot of content already. If any of you guys have played Bubble Tanks Arena or Bubble Tanks 3 on a site like
, then you have to at least try out this game.
Despite that it's sometimes difficult to create a stable vehicle, the controls are satisfying (despite the fact that you can't change them) and most of your creations simply work immediately (unless you're gonna make flying vehicles, then good luck). It's graphics are not the best ones, especially the map graphics, but they look smooth enough to me.
The only thing I don't like is how high-tier hard to unlock items can be used in low-tier games. I've seen high-level railguns or Helium (which allows you to go way up in the air) on really small vehicles to get ranked in the "weak/new vehicles" tiers. Especially the railguns can really be exploited on those lower levels, since nobody is really fast or flying or has a railgun. Also, it has many tips and tricks that the game never really points out to you, and so I recommend reading this guide once you're done being bad at the game:
Pros:
- You can already make pretty complex robots
- It's fun to test your creations in the good working "Practice Mode" and then put them to the full test online.
- Currently, there are no weapons that can be bought with the "Premium" currency. (look at the cons)
- Currently, you can't really make the 'perfect robot' or an overpowered robot if you only use the items you have unlocked currently on the hardest tier you're playing. Meaning that people won't copy their cars and hurt their creativity (unless it's a scorpion).
- The chat window might be small, but people actually use it.
Cons:
- There is a 'premium' currency (aka a currency that can only be gotten by using real money), meaning that it has a (not horrible but existing) Pay2Win factor.
- Since so much has to be unlocked and because high-tier items are pretty expensive, it's difficult to get "good" at this game quickly (mainly in the beginning, since the SMG doesn't really have a big learning curve).
- You can only put one weapon on your car at a time, and there are no secondaries like Mine Placers, or passive weapons like Ramming Spikes.
- It's easy to use cheap strategies in this game once you've unlocked high tier items and go with them to a Tier 1-3 server.
- Currently, you can only have 3 different cars, which I don't find to be enough.
Notes:
- Don't play this if you have arachnophobia, I have seen lots of scorpion and spider vehicles already. :3

- The game is still in it's Early development. There will be added more over time.
- The game has a "promotional code" bar both in your registration and in your login. In case you still have to make an account (and in case the code didn't get outdated already), put this code in your Promo Code Bar:
- There might come a "boss mode" later on, which I accidentally thought of too, and I'm really interested in seeing that.
Conclusion: 8/10 it's Like Skyrim but with Bubble Tanks.

Good concept; poor execution. Lot of bad things with this game. Here's a brief list:
1. The only thing standing between you and death is the blocks your pilot chair is on. You can have all of your other armor untouched, but if someone takes out the blocks your pilot is on: instant death. Makes it feel like all that extra armor and design is pointless.
2. Repetive gameplay. Same 3 or so maps, with a capture the enemy base or kill them all mode. Gets really repetive after a while. Oh, and you only have one life to boot.
3.The game tech tree that determines what tier you go into got respeced. As such there are players with (now) tier 2/3 equipment designing vehicles to fight in tier 1 servers. Horribly unbalanced and painful to play after a while.
4.Poor reward system-You can do no damage to a player except get the killing blow and you'll reap a greater reward than the person who did all the damage. This encourages people to rush in and steal kills.
5.Poor physics. Take that jeep for a jump and land upside-down? Have fun, you're staying that way for the rest of the game until it ends or you die.
6.Team-work? That word carries as much logic as the notion of a dancing banana piloting a Death Star into Hoth does with Jar Jar Binks singing "Hakuna mata". It doesn't exist even in imagination land.
Synopsis: Good concept, poor execution, dull and repetive game play with a bad reward system.
Fun game that requires creativity. 7/10

RoboCraft was a pleasant suprise, to be honest. There are a lot of bad reviews for it, and after reading through them, I can assure you, many were written not based on the game, but based on that the author didn't like the game. Allow me to explain not the flaws of the game, but the flaws of negative reviews.
-Firstly, I've seen many complaints about "Premium Membership" and how the Free to Play idea has vanished as Pay to Win appears. This, however, is not the case. All equipment that affects gameplay are 100% accessable to every player, Premium or not. There is an alternate currency which can be obtained by purchase of real-world currency that is used to buy Cosmetics for your vehicle, regular equipment that can be bought with the "free" currency, and to upgrade Tech Points. This does not create any hinderance to the non-paying player. The Cosmetic gear you can purchase is, well, cosmetic, and doesn't affect gameplay. The equipment that can be bought with it is accessable to anyone using the regular in-game currency, without paying a dime. Lastly, the upgraded Tech Points are for when you have Lvl 1 Tech Points, and need, for example, Lvl 3 Tech points. The paying user must first obtain the generic Tech Points, you guessed it, just like everyone else has to earn them. And when all is done, and the paying user has his top-quality equipment and vehicles, he still must then compete against vehicles of the same level as his own, meaning that all he has done is save time, and ruined the RPG-like aspect of the game. That being said, if he buys his way up to a Tier 10, and a regular player earns his way up to a Tier 10, both players are on the same playing field. Neither having the upper hand in the end, as the real winner is the one with the most skill of the game.
-Secondly, I'll discuss the physics. Yes, if you happen to collide with another vehicle, you may encounter some physical issues. However, these issues are often very minor. As far as complaints about vehicles toppling over whilst turning sharply, the reason for this is simply the lack of ability to read, as each unit has specific wieght properties, and many players construct top-heavy vehicles that will likewise, flip over while turning a corner. Simple principles such as center of gravity and centrifugal force flee the minds of the incompetent reviewers, and hence the degrading remarks of poor physics. Might I mention one reviewer's disapproval of the idea that if a vehicle has a large portion cut off, then you take a lot of damage? My question is, what would you expect if you were driving down the road, and your car split in half? Wouldn't anyone say that a car being split in half is "a lot of damage"? Sir, I do ask that you think about a concept befor slandering a developer for a realistic quality and added challenge.
-As far as "bland combat" goes, I strongly disagree. It does require some skill to be successful in combat, as well as being familiar with the construction mechanics of your type of vehicle. Every block has a role in which can be life or death. This also brings forth resource management. How Robopoints  are used is up to the player, yet many resort to trail and error to discover the most efficient usage of materials as well as his prefered combat style. This being said, to the inexperienced player, things can seem quite bland; until you find the right combination of weaponry, armor, mobility, combat style, and raw skill. This is when combat truly reaches it's full potential. Only when the player masters his craft does it become bland, in which case proves to be the right time to change things up a bit.

To sum things up, many reviewers have, and I do apologise, low level thinking. They take what's on the surface as what the whole is. Don't be a low level thinker; delve deeper, consider another point of view, and never be afraid to give something a chance. That stands true not only for Early Access gaming, but for life in general. Practice such a skill, and I assure you, it makes all the difference.
