Don't get me wrong, I really want to recommend this game. I have had my fair bit of fun with this game and I encourage you to check it out. It's easy to build your vehicle and its relatively fun to take your creation out for a murdering-stroll. But it has some things that they really need to flesh out.
1. Its economy is actively discouraging good teamplay. If your vehicle gets destroyed you get punished with a repair cost, also, you are basically no longer part of the team and do not receive the victory bonus if your team wins. If there should be any penalty, it should be because your team lost, otherwise your team won and your effort should not be penalized. The current system encourages players to be more cowardly and use their teammates as baits. Also, you get more Tech Points from killing than assisting, which means it encourage some TP-hungry people to kill steal (delaying damage to get the last shot) rather than just shooting the enemy until its dead. Though, most people (I hope) eventually understands that TP really isn't the limiting factor to progression, it's RP.
2. They want to force you into buying premium. If you die before getting any kills on Tier 4 and above, you might actually lose more than your time. Your repair RP costs will likely exceed what you earned during the round. As far as I've played (T6), I have never seen this cost exceed the gain you get from premium. I actually bought a few days premium in the early tiers because I wanted a boost, but when I reached the higher tiers I realized it wasn't really designed as a boost, it was basically designed as a necessity. Which just made me wanna stop playing. If they just cut the repair-thing out of the game, I'm sure they would make just as much money but would have a larger and less grumpy player base. They still have the premium RP gain presented grayed out in the end of each game, which can be enough incentive to tease people into buying premium (like it did to me before I realized how greedy the repair-system really was).
3. The weapons are unbalanced. This isn't a major flaw to me since it will no doubt be balanced eventually (I hope) and if the above points get sorted out, it won't be as serious issue (but should of course still be handled).
4. Tiers needs to be better regulated. I'm a bit more unsure about this one, but I think one of the biggest issue for balance is that there isn't any restriction of which tier of blocks that can be used in which tier of games, everything is regulated by Robot Rating to determine which tier your vehicle is. So players usually have weapons from at least one tier above, pretty often two. Meaning one shot kills by rails and plasma aren't uncommon.
5. The end game feels uncertain. The game is pretty repetitive right now since there is only one game mode. This makes, at least me, focus a lot on the progression part of the game and I'm not sure they have a plan for people who reach T10? When you have researched everything, bought enough parts to be able to build everything you want, how are they going to make money? Is this why they keep repair costs high? If so, count me out.
6. The net-code is pretty glitchy. I've seen a lot of people falling endlessly through the level with no way to interact with anyone else, some has been frozen in place and in some extreme cases they have become desynced, being able to affect the gameplay in strange ways. A friend of mine found that everyone else had frozen in place, this was only how it appeared for him. So he went to the enemy base to cap, when he got there he was blown to bits by a defender, and that appeared to be it for him, he thought, and by all means it appeared so for him. However, for me and everybody else, well, he was still dead, but he continued to cap and the team got a victory. So... the server acknowledged that he was dead, but let him cap anyway. This ghost-capping have happened twice so far. I'm sure they will fix this eventually, but it makes the experience frustrating so I think its worth mentioning.
I'm sure there is still some stuff I forgot to mention, but lets not make this (un)recommendation too long. It's fun, for a while, until you notice the ugly parts. I really hope I will change this to an actual recommendation in the future, but we'll see.

Oh well, another F2P that I won't be playing again.

It baffles me as to why I haven't reviewed this yet. I've owned it for almost two years, and I've even created maps for it, albiet terrible ones. It's an amazing first-person puzzle game which offers players a chance to push their brains to the limits. And that's only the Singleplayer. For even more excitement, you can do the Co-Operative campaign, which offers an even tougher experience, as you need both players'... cooperation. Both stories are as amazing as the puzzles, so even if you find the puzzles easy, you can at least enjoy the story. And, again, even if you don't enjoy the story, there are literally thousands of community created levels from you to choose from, each with a certain theme. While most offer the 'Into the Multiverse' theme, narrated by the Aperture founder and CEO himself, others can have their own complex storyline and theme. I'd give this game a 10/10 rating. If you buy it, you'll likely get one of the best games on the market.

It is EASY for me to recommend the Portal games. I have played the Half-Life series, Dota 2, Team Fortress 2, a couple of the Wargame series, Rust, and Don't Starve as well as a few others on the Steam platform. Since Steam was released for Linux, I have been looking for a "goto" game to play. While I enjoy the Half-Life series (greatly anticipating HL3) they don't have a high replay value for me. Team Fortress 2 is just another "Death-Match" game with its fast paced action. Although, the team aspect of it does have some appeal. But the game that I keep coming back to is Portal 2. The puzzles and their requisite rethinking of space/dimension are challenging and fun. The coop mode adds a dimension (pardon the pun) of play that allows puzzle-loving friends to keep going after the main story has ended. The community puzzles let players keep going for a long time after that. And finally, if you want to create your own levels, you can and publish them to the community. Without question, this is my all time favorite game. I hope they make a Portal 3.

There is an in game currency which allows you to buy the extra blocks you just upgraded. I enjoyed making my own robots and testing them out. I personally really enjoy this game. Although it has some negatives, I find the positives far outweigh it. I have TL;DR at the end.
What I like about game:
I find this game insanely fun. I love building things and I love this kind of team based warfare. I love exploring how to build different robots. There is a wide variety of stuff you can build and the devs are working on adding stuff. This is kinda like a World of Tanks/War Thunder + Minecraft, which is awesome. It is so satisfying to fight since parts of enemy robots are flying off. You can try to shoot off your opponents' weapons or wheels or anything you want!
What I dislike about this game:
This game has 3 meaningful limitations on what you can build. I will explain all 3, but my only complaint is the third one. 1. Access to certain items. You need to research new items, I have no real issues with this. 2. Cost of items. You need to earn money to buy the components you have researched. I have no issue with this as well, you will make money in pretty much every game you play, I have NEVER lost money.
My real issue is number 3, CPU. The game puts a limitation on how many blocks/items you can put on your Robot via this restriction. Now how do you get more CPU? You need to level up. This really annoys me because I have played a pretty high number of matches and I still cannot make the Robots I want sometimes due to this CPU restriction.
My second main complaint is the match making queue. You get into matches pretty quickly if you are a solo player, but what fun is it to play by yourself? The game's queue system seems to break when you platoon. About half the time, you never get into a match (like if it takes 10seconds to get into a match as a solo player, you will sit in queue for minutes as a platoon). You have to reset your connection to the server my going into practice mode and then re-queueing for a match. This is really annoying, I hope they improve their platoon queue system.
My response to some complaints about this game:
1. It is too difficult to earn money.
Reply: I am inclined to agree to a degree, but if you compare this to something like World of Tanks, it is actually quite easy to make money. At tier 5 I easily NET 1000-3000RP a match. (Net meaning after repairs have been done). This is honestly pretty reasonable.
2. The weapons are imbalanced:
Reply: I disagree; I find the weapons quite balanced. SMGs are close range weapons that tear apart plasma and railgun robots. They lack long range impact but they are not meant to be long range weapons, they also are decent against aircraft. Plasma and railguns are strong, but electroplates easily counter both those weapons and railguns also have difficulty against large masses of strong bricks. A recent patch reduced plasma weapons by 20% damage and reduced railguns by 15% damage making SMGs quite strong.
3. I hate how the game has microtransations/subscription.
Reply: No one is forcing you to pay for subscription. Everything in the game can be unlocked without paying anything. I have sunk around 60 hours into this game at this point and I still have plenty game left to explore, build, and enjoy. If I can justify paying $60-$70 for a regular game title that I get 20-30 hours of enjoyment out of, I have no problem giving these devs some money for creating an enjoyable game.
5. General response to haters.
Reply: So I find many of these people are writing a negative review with very few hours/games under their belt. They complain about not making money, when they are clearly at low tier. They complain about weapons being OP, when they haven't learned to counter them. They complain about maps being back, when they haven't learned how to effectively work as a team and play the advantages and disadvantages of each map.

TL;DR:
Pros: World of Tanks + Minecraft = AWESOME!
Cons: Platoon queue system needs improvement, fails to get you matches too frequently.
Other Thoughts: Haters will hate, but I contend they simply don't understand the game.
Do not play if: If you have the attention span of a 2 year old, then you probably won't have the patience to play this game. If you have played other games like World of Tanks or Warthunder, then you will be right at home.

Nothing less than the greatest game I have ever played! I put this game far above any Call of Duty, I put it above Elder Scrolls and even Civilization as the greatest game I have ever played. The first game, Portal, established the concept of portals and introduced us to a whole new world/environment/universe. Things were not okay and we were left wondering what is going on on the surface; This leads to a lot of exploratory and imaginative thinking to figure out how this all came to be. Luckily, Portal 2 does not answer any of those questions, well actually it creates more questions then it answers. This is the beauty of Valve. They know how to create the perfect game. The concept of portals is so basic, yet so unique it seems like it was meant to be even though it has never been done before. Portal 2 takes all the portals and stories from the first Portal and creates the most beautiful world, the most ingenious of chambers, the most clever dialogues, the most amazing storyline and the most fantastic ending. FPS games are a very popular genre, so is RPG and RTS; These are basic genres loved by most gamers and have been explored by numerous game developers. Portal 2 does not fit into any genre, but rather creates its own. The simple concept and physics play a huge part into making this game feel as if it is not a new idea, but rather it is so natural we dont even realize that this game is new. The full purpose of gaming is to do something that you cant do in real life, Portal 2 exemplifies this. I haven't even mentioned the co-op mode, the custom chambers or all the easter eggs, but I will leave you with this. Portal 2 has changed my view of games, each game has its flaw, but Portal 2 has none. I never thought I would find that perfect video game, I just did. 11/10 and 3 thumbs up to the Greatest Game Ever Created!

Robocraft is an extremely fun price for the low low price of zero dollars. There's the optional premium, and the difference is definitely there - but the complaints I'm seeing in some of these top-rated reviews are absolute nonsense. You get double "RP" and double tier points as a premium user, however I find the matchmaking/tier system justifies this. Read on for more on that. The game is very balanced, and they're constantly working to patch and balance things further hence the recent railgun and plasma cannon nerfing.
This game lets you build your own robot, and fight against other people who have built their own robots. The matchmaking system is usually very fast and pits you against robots in the same tier (or around the same tier) as you. So say you are tier 2, you could end up in a tier 2-3 lobby with robots from each tier. It's a good way to keep things interesting without going too overkill with it.
As I said, the game is very balanced and the matchmaking/tier system reinforces it further. Beyond that, a recent patch has altered the unlock tree so that the game is more "gradually" introduced and I find this to be a great idea. It keeps things at a pace and keeps low-level fighters from being too "complicated" in a sense... as in you won't find any tier 1 snipers hanging in the sky miles away.
I greatly recommend this game for any creative individual who wants to also blow stuff up.

My advice: if you really care about winning more than you care about gameplay - don't play this.  In many ways this is a physics sandbox - but there's so much more.
First impression after playing about 4 battles or so - everything in the game looks like it's free!  Quite a bit of fun too.  I started out not understanding how to get more guns, so my tank was ridiculously easy to kill.  But after figuring some things out the game is pretty nice and engaging.  Can't stop playing.  I think they nailed it!
After playing for about 3-4 hours straight - it looks like indeed everything is free.
[Sure it takes a long time compared to paying - who cares?  Let impatient people pay for the servers I'm fine with that!  I have been surveying players "are you paying to play?" and so far the majority are playing for free.]
There are multiple tiers, which earn higher levels of technology.  Designing a workable tank can be very engaging too.  If you are careful about how you spend RP, you'll have a good ship for that tier.  If you spend too much on your ship, you'll go to the next tier and feel overwhelmed again by outclassed ships.  However, there seems to be some grouping of similar tier advancement and you'll sometimes see as many as 3 different tiers in the same match (very high tier 1s in the same match as very low tier 3s).
The tier mechanic is brilliant!  You can get higher level weapons and fit them on a tank and as long as the limits of the tank don't exceed the tier, you can go back to a lower tier with that weapon than the tier you used to get the weapon's (or armor's) technology.  The result is very high volatility in challenge level for matches - which means if you suck, keep trying.  Eventually somebody will show up on your team to help out.
Teams play about around 12 versus 12 "capture the flag" matches.  The games can be very close too - sometimes switching favor at the last moment.
In the forums you'll see people complaining about "balance" like they have something irritating them.  But the whole game isn't about some little nitpick of perfectly balancing the mechanic.  It's really this random hodgepodge of people playing a crazy game, and so often these very funny outcomes.
For example, I just flew my single seat with 2 hovercraft fans still attached after everything else on my ship was blown up.  No more guns.  I'd been blown up about half a mile from their base, and the controls are all backwards now because no more ship.  But something inside is saying "try to make it to their base" so I try flying up and past 2 or 3 enemies who somehow ignore me - fly it haphazardly into the enemy base, and spend about 15-20 seconds on the base going around in circles while an enemy is shooting others there.  I'm laughing the whole time and he finally kills me.  But it provided enough of a distraction that other team-mates could finish him and completely over-run their base.  Chat comments people laughing.  This is great gameplay.
The longer I play this, the more I get the feeling this game is as close to the "Road Warrior" experience you might find in any game.
.
.
.
.
.
.
Now after 67 hours logged playtime.  I STILL HAVEN'T PAID ANY MONEY.  Last night I got to tier 5 and bought some wings and a rudder.  This is the last new technology unlock.  After this all technologies are just bigger numbers of the same stuff.
I'm guessing I'm not a great player (I've never been good at shooters) - but 67 hours doesn't seem unreasonable FOR A FREE GAME to get access to all the major techs.
The only danger I can see is if you pay and somehow think that's going to make you uber.  It won't.
Playstyle seems to be the major factor of success in this game:
1 - learning how to play as a team
2 - slowing down -- see what the other players on your team are doing
3 - use the terrain to your advantage
The rants you see on all the forums posts and bad reviews seem to have developed a paranoid mentality "everyone else is probably paying more than I am" and so they don't enjoy the gameplay.  That's not the dev's fault.  This game is awesome.

This game is one of those addictive just-one-more-level games.
It has shoot 'em up action mixed with grinding for upgrades.  The best feature is the creativity this game allows.  You can build a floating carousel pony with lasers on it or a streamlined thick armored tank with cannons to take into battle - the choice is yours!
You can team up with friends or go it alone.  You will be matched up with robots of relatively equal strength and thrown into an all out battle to capture the enemy base.  If you die, you can simply restart another match or make improvements to your robot with the points earned during battle.  The more blocks and accessories you add, the higher your robot's tier will climb indicating the strength of your robot.  Earn enough tech points through battle, and you can unlock upgrades that allow for even stronger weapons, armor, and different modes of travel.
There is no reason for any gamer to not give this game a look no matter their favorite genre especially since it's free to play while in it's alpha stage.  I highly recommend giving this game at least a half an hour of your time to see what it offers, I don't believe you'll be disappointed!

The core of the game is beautifully executed and very fun for the player. But the framework around it ruins some of the fun.
In Robocraft, you can not only level up which increases the amount of things you can put on your robot, you can also increase the "tier" of your robot. The tier is dependent entirely on the equipment of your robot and the matchmaking works with it. This means that if you're tier 1, you'll play with other tier 1 users. However, the careful reader might have seen the flaw in this: The level has absolutely no influence on the tier. That means you can play for 1000 hours, be level 100 and ridiculously experienced and still make a tier 1 robot and stomp new players. But that's not the only problem - in Robocraft you have to unlock new cubes with tech points locked to your current tier. These new blocks are backwards compatible: You can simply play up to tier 3, unlock the very dangerous plasma cannons and put three of them on a new robot. With a bit of tinkering I've managed to make a tier 1 robot that deals around 3750 damage per burst. That means I can oneshot at least half of the new players.
tl;dr: good game but makes it too easy for veterans to stomp new players which can be incredibly frustrating for them

If you like to build vehicles from scratch and drop them into fast-paced, do-or-die arena combat, then you'll love this game.  The real joy for me comes in attempting to perfect a design that allows for maximum survivability in the arena...and the fact that you really can build a giant toilet (mentioned above) with guns on it.  How could you not love that?  Even spectating to see other players' zany creations is a blast.
So, here are the ingredients:
--Combat vehicle design and creation using blocks of varied shapes and other components (wheels, guns, etc)
--Zany team-based arena combat (point-capture or team annihilation, whichever comes first), which goes fast
--Vehicle leveling based on arena performance
--Unlock better and better building components through arena combat participation
--Easy to learn, get into the action quickly (also, little kids who love minecraft will love this!)
--Free to play (microtransactions available, not sure if eventually mandatory for better gear)
--Development team that seems open to (and even asks for) player ideas for improvement
This is a recipe for creative fun, ladies and gentlemen.  I highly recommend this game.

It's a game about design and constantly improving your vehicle based on experience. If you like critical thinking and problem solving or you just want to be creative with Minecraft blocks in a public setting I recommend this game.
Gameplay stays as fun and interesting as you make it. If you keep thinking up vehicles and crafts to design or improvements to be made on your existing crafts you won't get bored with this.
Progression (at the time of writing) is at a normal pace with the new tech tree. You'll be eased in to the new and various bot parts with the exception of the players from before the recent tech tree patch (you may see lesser variations of gear you don't yet have access to but this is far from game breaking).
Pay to win.... Not even. Premium membership only gives a multiplier of 1.5 to your earnings. Tech tree points cannot be purchased. And all blocks (save the cosmetic robot name tag, vapor trails and country flags) can be purchased with realistic amounts of earned in-game currency.
Development continues throughout early access with semi-weekly patches and new content being added.
TLDR:  I reccomend this game because it is as fun as you make, grinding levels and tiers isn't difficult but still feels rewarding,  the game has a good business model and is continuing to grow.

Valve does it again.  Portal 2 is a beautifully crafted puzzle-based FPS that builds upon everything established from the short, but tremendous original.  The puzzles hit a wonderful balance of being uniquely iterative without being too obtuse.  The is that each puzzle is very solvable while carrying a sense of accomplishment.  The story line is riddled with inside jokes and quotable one-liners that you will be well entertained throughout your journey through the world of Portal 2.  Steven Merchant is masterful as Wheatley hitting humorous, diabolical, and compassionate notes in recording one of the best voice acting performances I've ever heard.  As if the single player wasn't enough of a reason to purchase this game, the online co-op is magnificent.  If two portals are good, four is even better and each player must build upon the puzzle-solving skills from the single player campaign in order to make it through.  The way Valve constructed the rudimentary communications system of the robots, Atlas & P-Body, is equal parts functional and hilarious.  There something sublime about the discourse of two players fighting over whose idea will be used to solve the puzzle through a series of robotic pointing and beeping.  As frustrated as I sometimes was, it was made all the more rewarding to share the glory of solving a particularly challenging level with a friend.  I daresay you will rarely come across such a masterpiece as Portal 2.

This game is great, especially for still being in alpha.  You have to build strategically, drive tactically, and shoot intelligently if you want to beat the other players.  Cover and terrain are important, and if you shoot an opponent's guns off, they'll be unable to do anything but run.  Shooting the wings or hoverpads off of a flyer can send them spiraling out of control, making it much easier to finish them off.
You will see some goofy-looking bots out there, to be sure.  Sometimes people build something silly on purpose, and other times they try something wacky and forget to include crucial stuff (like not making a lopsided robot).  Sometimes, though, you see some FRICKIN' AWESOME robots.
Que times are short and the devs are very proactive in making changes to fix issues.  You can go all the way to the top for free, which is a nice draw.

A better tutorial needs to be implemented to introduce the elements of the game.
Controls
The controls are relatively simple and easy to get used to. WASD are obviously directional movement, and space goes up, shift goes down. Makes a lot of sense (except for airplanes, but I'll get to that later). Right clicking is a bit wonky in the fighting part of the game -- it doesn't do a whole lot to improve aim except for rail guns.
Physics
The physics are... ok. At first glance they seem fairly good. Until you run into a teammate or a wall. This is part of where the game suffers -- it has no idea how to handle your craft clipping into something else. I don't know how many times I ended up nose first into a wall or sending a teammate flying because of weird collisions. While in most cases this is benign, and somewhat amusing, this can result in really frustrating playtime. Aircraft suffer heavily because of this problem. Once your nose is in the wall, you are pretty much useless. And it punishes newbies who end upside-down without a realignment thing-a-ma-bob.
However, my favorite part of the physics was the destruction physics and how they affected your vehicle. Getting your wheels/hoverblades/wings destroyed results in very interesting predicaments which is a lot of fun. Finding out that your weapons can be destroyed makes you much more conservative on weapon placement and # of weapons.
Team Play
Team play is somewhat problematic. Sometimes your teammates are your best friends:
Cover you when you're under fire
Suppress the enemy while you ready another shot
Avenge you
But sometimes your teammates are your worst enemy:
Running into your back while you're trying to avoid buckshot in the face, usually resulting in death
Sending you flying from the aforementioned physics and clipping issues
Blocking your shot
Stealing your kills (and therefore your money and tech points)
Ditch you in your time of need
Additionally, team play also suffers from the lack of VOIP. Almost a third of all the battles I played in I ended up running alone because nobody let me know I was solo or that I should head a different direction. Needless to say, this generally led to me getting slaughtered.
Movement
For the most part, this is one of the most interesting parts of this game. You have 3 "options" in movement, technically 4 if you consider another element.
1) You get your standard wheeled vehicles which are fun until your wheels get blown off. Wheels are fairly straightforward and require little to no explanation.
2)You get your hovercraft, which sometimes work really well, and sometimes send you careening in weird ways. The hovercraft, for whatever reason, has a max height above the terrain immediately below you. On relatively smooth surfaces this works without any problems unless you are a bad driver. However, this becomes a problem on most slopes -- the hovercraft starts tipping and wobbling like a drunkard. If you go over a cliff, you can go shooting off in weird ways. The hovercraft has another weird problem. It has two "stable states" in which it can hold -- right side up, and wrong side up. This can result in aggravating play as the controls get reversed (game still takes the input in the same way as right side up).
3) You get your aircraft, which for some strange reason you don't unlock until late into the game. Aircraft are at the same time the most interesting movement method in the game, and the most frustrating. You have to spend a lot of time carefully placing your wings, rudders, ballast, and thrust to prevent the aircraft from death spiraling or flipping out (literally). This becomes all the more frustrating when a stray shot from an enemy destroys your carefully placed wing, its carefully placed defense, and sends you death spiraling anyway. IMHO, aircraft wings need a bit more armor and should be available sooner in the game. Additionally, coming from a background of designing SSTO's in Kerbal Space Program, the aircraft in this game need some basic design tools as well -- We need to know where the center of mass is, where the center of thrust is, and where the center of lift is. While I can forgive the unrealistic plane physics (this isn't a game devoted to physics), these tools would be immensely helpful in designing better aircraft. Additionally, the controls for aircraft should be reworked: W and S should be assigned as up and down respectively. Shift and space should control throttle. It makes no sense to fly at full speed or not fly at all. There should be a throttle.
4) While not technically a movement form, it's worth a mention. The helium/lighter-than-air allows for hovering platforms high in the sky. Generally these are heavily abused as sniper nests, hovering so high in the air that for plasma cannons and SMGs it is often sheer luck to hit these things. These need some rebalancing so that railguns aren't the only useful weapons against these enemies.
Weaponry
There are three forms of weaponry available to you. You get your SMG, your Plasma Cannon, and your Railgun. Here's my feelings on all three:
1) SMG. Because of the game mechanics, SMGs favor you spam placing SMG turrets all over your vehicle. Since there is a limit on how many SMGs can fire at any one time, the SMGs are that are not destroyed in combat are fired after the initial batch is destroyed. This is alright, seeing as the SMG is a close range weapon by design, and thus spares should be necessary. The problem with SMGs is that they are also highly effective long-range weapons that do not suffer the cooldown of railguns. A person who taps the fire button slowly with an SMG can hit accurately almost as far as they can see. This becomes a real problem for aircraft, who as I mentioned before, can go death spiraling when a wing is destroyed. Additionally, this issue leads to SMG users "softening up" targets at a distance when they really shouldn't be able to.
2) Plasma Cannons. Plasma cannons are IMO the most balanced weapon in the game. They have a cooldown that matches their utility, a sizeable kick that prevents abuse from hovering sniper nests, an arcing shot that requires practice to use properly, and their shots spread like a shotgun.
3) Railguns. Railguns are perhaps the most irritating weapon in the entire game, due to their ease of abuse. Railguns can snipe across the map with no damage reduction and penetrate armor. As a newbie, this resulted in instant death. As an experienced player, this resulted in my well-crafted tank being Swiss Cheese before I even got into firing range. The long cooldown and poor moving aim is only a minor inconvenience when a railgun user can hide behind cover to recharge (considering how far they are) and then pop back out to blast some more. Railguns are capped at 6 shots maximum, which also minimizes the problem of the long cooldown. Additionally, railguns are heavily abused by the aforementioned hovering sniper nests -- they can kill any enemy that can shoot them, often before the enemy realizes their presences. Because railguns have a relatively small kick, the sniper nests can usually spam fire before the movement penalty comes into play. The railguns need reworking, period -- They need a very heavy kick, to the point where even users in tanks would hesitate to use them on top of a cliff. this is a great game and i honestly played it for 24 hours in 3 days but i cannot recommend it as it is now. it took a great concept and made it happen initially but has stagnated. lets take its tagline as a basis for my argument: "build, drive, fight". pay-2-play opinion and TL;DR at the bottom.
the game has definetly delivered on the build aspect. the building is as easy as in minecraft and its easy to get a hang of, even for the jets/aerofoils. this gives people freedom to make♥♥♥♥♥♥♥shaped tanks all they want. i do feel that weapons are lacking, but it is still in early access and so it gets a free pass.
the driving is responsive and is affected by what you have made. if you made a wide base, your tank wont topple as easily. if you made a ballanced jet, i will fly straight. and so on. in that sense, the driving, IMO, is the only part of the tagline that the game has fufilled fully.
the last part, fight, is where it game has most issues. i wont complain about server downtime as steam does increase an indie games user base 100fold. what i will complain about is the lack of game modes, lack of anything unique in each map and matchmaking. there is litterally only 1 game mode. i expected the usual modes such as deathmatch and capture the flag. more modes mean that one would have an incentive to make more unique vehicles to win the match. while having 4-5 maps is fine, the only major difference between them is the ice. much like the game modes, maps affect peoples play styles and build. a map with only 1 straight path would entince people to make giant walls while maps with many paths(like the one on mars) would encourage backstabing and being stealthy.
the matchmaking and tier system are the worst things about the game. while its easy to understand how it works, it can be vastly unfair. the game sorts you into 10 tiers based on your robots ranking which is the total ranking based of all the parts you have used. using more or better parts equate to a higher ranking. this seems fair at first but soon you realise that people with tier 5 parts are making minimalistic robots to enter tier 2 games and they can actually decimate players with ease. this is the easiest way to feel like "god" in this game as you can get free kills and gaim money or RP easily.
unlike most people, i actually have no problems with pay-2 play. i think that its fair that they should get rewarded with 1.5 times the RP and TP for supporting the devs as they actually have to damage/kill people or capture the base in order to earn TP which is required to unlock blocks. there are also no exclusive paid blocks so i really dont see how pay-2-play is OP. it just makes the game less grindy. and i am fine with grinding.
TL;DR: robocraft is a great game with a great concept that is sowlying making its way to fruition but still has many small kinks that unfortunately overshadow its few but potentially overwelming points.

For anyone out there that enjoy building mechs, this seems like a fantastic game. This games default game style is a 12v12 mass battle between your team and others in a open map capture the point game. A upgradable tech tree and complete and utter freedom in creation of your own robot/mech.  If you come from the Armoured Core, Starmade, Space Engineers, Roblox or Mech game genre, get ready to get you hopes up!
and then ruthlessly crushed.
I hate to say it, as this game can be absolutely brilliant, but bad game design and pay to win schemes completly ruin what could be one fo the most strategic and fun games released this year...it could of even one day Rivaled LoL or Dota.
down the the details. The complete freedom in creating your robot/mech is no lie and this is quite a fun part of the game, however you are initially given a set number of parts in which you must build off or use a default pre-build tank thing. however the first problem comes in when your ownly really drip fed currency, you may win only 100-300 of the currency per match, a single low tier gun costs just that, with higher tier guns costing near 1000. simple armour and building blocks are not cheap either and your often require you to grind in order to build something with more imagination than just a box.  winnings do increase as you level but so do the costs of repairing your robot......effecitvly making your winning cut the same. its a slow progression.
now lets talk about the tech, the most broken thing in this game. Capturing your enemies point, surviving the match and killing someone can earn you Tech points and these are used to purchase Tech on the Tech Tree. A solid system. Except, A tier 1 robot can only earn tier 1 Tech points, which only allows you to buy Tier 1 Tech....which is not much. you must now, using all the Tech 1 gear, make a robot powerful enough to place you in a new tier 2 lobby, allowing you to earn Tier 2 Tech points and so on and so forth.
By the way, this is not a Tech Tree, this is a Progression System disguised as a Tech Tree. and its bs. back to the Tech stuff.
now you unlocked your new gear does not mean you own it? o no o no. you must buy it in the store now, individually. so you want 4 guns? you gotta buy it 4 times. and it is expensive. now each item/weapon/piece or armour has a tier cost. meaning the more powerful the robot, the higher place in the tier match making you are placed. Except.....and here is the broken part.
People with tier Tech 4 or 5 or 6 gear can jump in on tier 1 match making and have a ball. provided that dont make robots that are too big or dont have too many weapons. So you have new players and people just getting started in their respective tiers being faced off against other players capable of 1 shotting them in an instant. And this problem exsists in all the match making tiers.
of course, you can pay real money to get tech early, effectivly ingoring the progression system....making this a play to win game.
Matches are not down to skill in this game, they are down to luck. If you are lucky enough to have more players on your team from a higher teir, you win. if not, you lose. games are rarely RARELY down to the wire and often win in land slides. not to mention almost every games plays off in a base race. you make it to the enemy base before the enemy makes it to yours.....you pretty much win in 30 seconds. almost noone actually stays to defend their base.
I wont mention the odd gameplay flaws or bugs or lack of maps or game types. Thats perfectly excusable for a early access game and I have no problems with it. I dare say they will be adding more content before they even think about even remotly fixing this broken tier systems.
So....listen, if you REALLY enjoy building stuff and you love strategic games? Go buy a better game. but if you have no money, try this out....it could be something grand in the future, it might get re-balanced, more content will be added. but pay to win and the broken mechanics are enough to pull anyone away from this game.
Its no, for now.

After reading some of the negative comments, I must say it's not as bad as they paint it...
The game's about building vehicles like they were lego's and putting guns on them and pin your creation against other peoples creations. It's fun!
Satisfaction comes from seeing your creation bust up the creation of other people as you shoot them. At the end of the match, you return to your mothership to make repairs and/or changes to your ship before the next match. Repair costs increase the higher level you are, but you usually earn more than what you loose in repairs. At higher tiers it does start digging into your pockets, but it creates an environment where careful strategy against the enemy becomes the main focus, and not some rambo crazy kamikaze attack because you'll literally end up paying for mistakes with credits you can use to otherwise upgrade your ship.
Sure, there are "premium" users, but that's not a huge deal... all they get are blocks that you can also get with some game-time. They still have to level up to use enough of them because of the "CPU" Point system, so it's not exactly Pay2Win (Because, I must emphasize that you can get what they can the more you play)
My favorite part about this game is the physics engine. You can't just make any vehicle work out, so it's funny seeing people at spawn flip over onto their backs or flying ships going haywire because they can't get good weight distribution.
Overall, it's a great game to pick up, play for a bit and then do something else. You won't regret it.
Oh, did I mention it's a free download? ... yeah ;)

TL;DR: Read the suggestions at the buttom of this, for how I think they could improve and balance out the weapons and stuff.
Was fun for the first day I played, then they released a patch that broke the game.
They ♥♥♥♥ed up the Tech Tree by removing certain items they believed were OP, but let anyone who had previously purchased them, keep them. Those items were not OP, but not being able to have them, and then facing someone who does have them, that gives them a severe advantage. They also nerfed Plasma cannons, and Rail guns. I barely ever died to those things. I usually died to guys with about 14 SMGS just eating my vehicle alive because they shot my wheels, or my guns off. Okay it's still fun, but not as much as it was my first day when everything wasn't broken. Now SMGs are really OP, and plasma cannons aren't as usefull. Rail guns are only useful for longrange support, and if you actually get in any sort of real fight, you just die. Everyone thinks they are OP but they aren't. I'll explian.
You see if your pilot is hit by anything, your entire vehicle is destroyed. Same thing happens if the block your pilot is attached to gets destoryed. Rail guns act like snipers. You fire, and it instantly hits right where you aim. You even get to scope in. So people get one shot, because the rail gunner aims for there pilot. Then they ♥♥♥♥♥ about them being OP. Now rail guns are nerfed that you can't actually break anything off of there ship very quickly, which you can easily do if you use SMGs. You have to wait for someone with an SMG to drive up, and eat off their armor, so that the pilot gets exposed. At least before, you could shoot the armor off, and then hit the pilot.
See SMGs don't really have a down side. Before the attraction to Plasma and Rail guns was that they did more damage, but they had a long reload time. SMGs never need to reload, and never overheat. You can just eat anyone who isn't using them alive, and not give a♥♥♥♥♥♥ Rail guns have a 25 second reload time, if you don't hit your target you have a long wait time, and they can't reload until you have shot every last one of the rail guns you have on your vehicle. Plasma Cannons, had a shorter reload, about 8 - 10 seconds. They arc down, so long range is hard to aim. You fire all of them at one, kind of like a shotgun, and they do not all go right where you aim, they have spread. You could one shot with these because they did area of effect damage to blocks, and if you could break the pilot's block hes attached to, you insta kill. SMGs can do this too. if they hit the pilot, hes blows up, and if you break the block hes on, same thing. but they have a spread, andtheir damage is just dealt to a single block. But they each fire once per second so if you have enough of them, you can literally eat everyone who gets close to you. You can also hit players that are farther away, though the slight spread of bullets makes it a bit luck based, you can still snipe just as you could with a rail gun, especially at higher teirs with more powerful SMGs.
So here's my suggestions to make things a little more balanced.
1, Bring everything back to the tech tree. And I mean EVERYTHING. I want to see 1 - 10 of every last block type and I don't want excuses. If something is OP, then rework it. Don't just nerf its damage, thats how you screw things up with either Over, or Under powered issues.
2, The pilot block. Make this block be only 2 blocks tall, instead of 3, he needs to be easier to protect. This is a major part of the reason that people keep ♥♥♥♥♥ing about how Rails, and Plasmas, are OP.
3, Rail guns should charge up. Have them do less damage if you simply click on a target. Make it so that the longer you hld the fire button, the more damage it will deal, untill full damage is reached. And when full damaged is reached, you instantly fire. This will make hitting people a bit harder because you have to follow them while you charge up.
4, Plasma guns. Actually, I main these when I play, and I still got eaten and lost fights against SMG player before they were nerfed. sometimes I won. sometimes I didn't. really, it came down to ship design, and driving skill. I don't think they were OP, but if they were tomake them fly slower through the air or something so that they are easier to dodge, that would be cool.
5, If you take if from the Tech Tree, take it from everyone who has it too. Give them back their tech points as Uber points, and give them back the GC worth ofthe items. It's the only fair, and right thing to do.
6, Realize that just because the community thinks its broken, doesn't mean it really is. Go and play games yourself, and see if the things they are complaing about are actually a problem. Some of them will be, and you should deffinately fix those. But not everything, is actually broken. Sometimes the issue is that they are just too attached to their original ship design. Maybe their ship just sucks.
I have a lot of other ideas that could make the game better, but they aren't for this review. I hope this review was somehow helpfull, or something. I rate this game a 8/10. Will probably play again, if for no other reason than to build a flying Office Building. I hope they improve the game, and find better way of fixing things, not to just nerf, or buff.

For those who want a game that thrives on creativity, tactics, & non-pay to win gameplay, RoboCraft is definitely something you'd want to play for hours on end. Robocraft is a multiplayer arena type where you can customize your "robot". You could add  wheels for ground movement, wings for actual flight, boosters for direction change (speed), and hovers for slight off-the-ground assaults (negating the friction of the land). As of right now, there are only 3 types of weapons: smg(mainly close range), plasma(mainly medium range), and railguns (mainly long range). I used the word "mainly" as any of these weapons can be useful anywhere if you have some skill. There are few tweaks to be made regarding the physics (such as proper force being applied between crashing robots), but nothing is too aggravating. It's very rare to see people with the same exact robot (though variants of very close relation are expected). The system of the skill tree stands as one of my favorites as it adds plenty of variety for how to approach your unlockables, and the tier system (rank system) is more balanced than most AAA games out there. WIth non-premium, you can maintain a private squad of 3 people (joining about 7-9 other random comrades) to tactically dismantle your opponents.  In my opinion, the best way to play this game is with a squad of friends, steam group voicechat, and some snacks nearby.

A fun idea, but executed in the most uninspired way possible. At first glance it looks like it could have all sorts of possibilities for crazy vehicles and constructions, but due to the very limited number of origional parts, all vehicles are basically a bunch of cubes with guns stuck on them and some wheels or jets. There are many parts you can buy, but they are all just the same parts made slightly better. The list of parts is, currently, as follows: structural blocks, (including square and angled bits,) wheels, jets, hover jets, flotation blocks, wings, armour plates, and three types of guns; basic slowish shot, lobbed shot, slow long range shot. Most of these parts, namely everything but the blocks, wheels and basic gun, is locked when you start, so to actually build anything besides a box with wheels and a bunch of guns tacked onto it you will have to either pay hard cash for them or put in many hours of play.
On top of all that, the only workable design for a vehicle seems to be your command seat surrounded by as much mass as you can pile around it, and as many guns as you can fit on the top and sides, because there is no strategy to the game other than drive toward the enemy and hope you can shoot more than he can.
To conclude this rambling, I would not reccomend this game in the least. If you think the developers may actually get around to making this game less of an uninspired blob of sadly unexplored concepts, by all means keep an eye on this game, but for now don't waste your time. Or your money.

Example being after a match, a player that pays to win gets 50% more from awards. Most claim this makes this game a pay to win. Not entirely, it just makes the players who pay progress faster. I've had this game for a two days and 14 out of those 48 hours have went into this game. This is a well rounded game for it being in Alpha.

The only thing that might be upsetting are the gun balances. Drop the damage of the rail-gun, and we got ourselves a really great game!
*UPDATE* The developers of this game have been listening to the community and providing excellent feedback! The TP is now easier to obtain, and Railguns and SMGs have been nerfed. If there was any  doubt in your mind that this was a Pay-to-Win game, I hope these clear them!

Robocraft is silly, frenetic and fun.

Basically you craft your own ships (tanks, carts, planes, etc) and battle other players in a two team, base capture mode. There are 10 tiers of parts, and as you fight you can rank up your tech tree to higher tiers to unlock and purchase better parts.

The rank of your craft is based on the types of parts you use, and that determines which rank of game you're put into.

So far the game has been a lot of fun. The sense of progression is great, and you always have that "just one more match" feeling. The building system is simple enough to build things quickly and easily, but flexible enough to make some pretty cool things.

My favorite part though is just how goofy the game can be sometimes. You'll start a match and have some tanks on your team, a floating cube with no guns, a X-Wing, and a minecraft house on wheels. You'll pull of an amazing strafing run to then hit a rock, flip over and go skidding to a stop in the middle of the enemy's team. You'll get torn apart by a volley of lasers and be too busy laughing at your spaceman with one wheel and a chair, spinning a sad circle to be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off.

I would suggest: try not to take this game too seriously and I think you've be surprised at how fun it is.

PROS:
- Light, creative, fun.
- Great sense of progression.
- Matches can be started again after a win or loss very quickly.
- The community that I've seen so far is pretty decent.
- The free-to-play model is unobtrusive, progress can be made with a little effort.

CONS:
- Maps and game modes are very limited currently. (This is likely to change with further development.)
- New players will have to deal with players who have unlocked powerful weapons and tools playing in low tier matches. Be prepared to be one-shotted by mortars and snipers. (Due to how quick you can start a new game it's not too bad.)

Overall if you're looking for a not-too-serious and fun little action game I would totally recommend Robocraft.

Please look below at A Hedgehog's and Flame Soulis's reviews, they are pretty spot on.  After all that, I'd like to put in my two cents.  The balancing in the game is abysmal.  You can walk in with T4 weapons on a T2 match with extra armour and steamroll people.  The sad part is that this is a huge contribution to the complaints about gun balance.  I would main the Rail Cannon quite often and one thing that people forget is that I'm open for roughly 20 seconds.  I can't attack at all.  Yet they complain when I one shot them for not having harder armour below their pilot or a design that helps dissipate the damage.  You will be flipped by other bots much smaller than you.  You will have to deal with the guy who has 6 T4/T5 cannons and is somehow in T2.  Don't get me wrong, at one point I had fun, but it was a quick passing fun as I viewed the forums and observed what happened while playing.  For example; I play Warframe.  I've played it well beyond what Steam displays and have special items like the Dex Furis.  However, even though they have switched the interface over to console to appeal to PWE, though they have introduced "space dogs" (and without armour), and though they have made items like neurodes and orokin cells incredibly hard to farm, I still play it.  I still get that fun feeling from it.  The same feeling I get on TF2 and the same excitement I have whenever I play Mount and Blade: Warband.  This game, no.
TL;DR:  If you want a rating then 5/10. Go ahead and try it, just don't spend any real money on it.  The devs can't even put in a weight system for when bots collide (can be done).

1.  If you remove it from the tech tree, remove it from game - give them their RP back, but keeping it, ruins the experience for others.
2.  If you equip Tier 2 items you are in a Tier 2 match, ONLY allow Bots wielding Tier 1 items to match in Tier 1 games.
Without the above changes, this game is fantastically unbalanced, and virtually unplayable.

I will recommend it.  Why?  Because this game costs just a download and some time for you to try it out and form your own opinions.  This review will be about me voicing my experiences with Robocraft versus why you should get the game, and hopefully be useful to the devs.
I saw RC pop up on the Steam notification list and immediately my eyes lit up.  It was a free-to-play game, but it had KSP-like building action, where you could assembleLego creations and then pit them against my friends in combat.  This sounded exactly like a game I would have enjoyed as a kid.  I know, because I used to
as a kid.  (If you think repairing a tank is expensive and tedious, try picking up individual Lego pieces which were spread over a twenty foot radius due to a Fruit-Rollups-fueled combat round.)
The game is very straightforward.  Build a craft using a simple editor, then launch it against others.  And here is where you will discover the game is nearly a 1:1 clone of another well-known vehicular F2P combat game that also contains micro-transactions.
That's a good and bad thing at times.  Good, because this other well-known game has practically honed its F2P with MTX model to a bright shine.  So, overall, you will find the system is more or less fair if you are not wanting to pay a single cent.  You can grind to every point of the game, but it will indeed be a lot of grinding.
But it's also bad, in that a lot of the same gameplay mechanics from this other game are also included in Robocraft.  And while that made sense for a game that had a fixed amount of units that you can unlock and purchase, Robocraft literally lets you build anything.  Sometimes the inclusion of these mechanics really hampers Robocraft and makes it into a tedious F2P grind fest.
Robocraft is also a team-based game with an objective -- Capture the enemy base.  But largely, I find that people ignore that goal and engage in team-deathmatch style play.  I hope that in the future, the devs will give us more incentive to play as a team, and in fact, give us more objectives to complete which would require team-work.  Right now you can just run around as a solo fighter and make as much progress in the game than if you tried to help your team-mates.
Recently, the tech tree was rebalanced so that most of the gear is only available to higher tier levels.  While this allows you to experience a broadening of gameplay as you progress, I think it's detrimental to the core of what Robocraft is about.  Tinkering with all kinds of guns and parts at the beginning was a huge draw to this game;  Being limited to only a 5th of what was available before is a huge minus point.  You are required to grind for days in order to reach a tech level where you can build, say, flying craft or utilize sniping cannons.  (This will be longer if you are a casual gamer and can only devote an hour or two to the game each day.)
The game does include MTX in the form of in-game currency you can buy.  As of right now, the currency is only good three things:  Buying more tech, buying parts at a much lower price than using the earned-from-combat money, and buying additional slots in your garage so you can store more vehicles.  Only the first and last are useful to me.
You can also pay for a Premium account, which gives you a %50 boost to all earnings from game matches.  This is the only advantage.  Unlike the other vehicle based combat game, there is no form of Gold ammo or items, which minimizes the pay-to-win aspects.
Pros:
* Build anything.  Want to construct a Dalek and shout EXTERMINATE while shooting other people's Lego creations to bits?  Go nuts.
* Progress on every battle.  You will gain XP even if you damage no craft, make no kills, or capture a base.
* Very polished.  Looks, feels, and sounds great.
* Minimal pay-to-win.  Paying only allows you to unlock higher-tech equipment faster but does not actually give you an in-game boost.  (Note: Not entirely true, as currently it does.  See below.)
Cons:
* Very imbalanced at the moment.  The lower tier fights are absolutely fish-in-a-barrel scenerio as you can bring high-tech weapons into low-tech matches.  (I am told this will be addressed in a future patch.)
* New re-balanced tech tree makes it harder to explore all options the game has to offer without a significant investment of time (or money).
* Lack of team-based incentives, so players mostly treat game as team deathmatch instead of capture the flag.
* F2P/MTX model, if that sort of stuff bothers you.
* Weapons are currently overpowered.  Armor is of dubious usefulness.

=========================================================================
This game is pay to win. Plain and simple. Or, don't pay and watch painstakingly as you got murdered because you can't buy into the next tier yet, but the matchmaking decides to throw you into a higher tier. Oh, and you really have to question things when you are in a lower tier, and the enemy team has two or three guys flying vehicles around. And then you look at the tech chart, scratch your head, and ask yourself, "wtf". Can we at least agree on, 'pay to advance higher than everyone else you will be matched with'??
Look, I am not uh, discounting the uniqueness of this game. It really is quite something; and every part of me *wants* to love it.. and I will preface this with, *EARLY ACCESS": they need to a) rethink their pay scale. Pay to play ruins games, no argument there. I know that hosting servers for thousands, to millions of people to play on can cost money, but there ARE better ways to implement some kind of pay system. Path of Evil does a pretty damn good job. Point b) matchmaking needs to be fixed. There is absolutely no reason why I should be getting matched with enemies that fly around, and have top tier plasma guns that destroy me in one hit. No way.
Again though, this is *EARLY ACCESS*, which I can't stress enough. Some people won't care, and will play it anyway. Some people will blow a lot of money in it, and will be flying around in low tier games, plasma'ing the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everyone. Great. Whatever knocks their socks off. Personally, I will wait and see how it unfolds with updates and patches before I put any serious effort and time into it. However, in its current state, I can not recommend. Waste of time. Potential, SURE! But currently, a waste of time.
And for the record, my review is not the only one that has claimed this to be a Pay to Win game.. Anyone, feel free to my review and opinion (or anyone else's for that matter) for what it is: an opinion.

Very addictive game!
[editEDIT: awesome game, devs turned it around, really fun!]
Basically you build vehicles (I guess they're called Robots?) using different parts and you can build tanks, hovercraft, airplanes, blimps, etc. After carefully building your machine, you go into battle and see it smashed into pieces by other people's machines, but not before taking out a few of them.
In between battles you improve your design as more parts are unlocked. You get that "just 1 more match and I'll be able to get that new part/item" feeling.
The best thing about the game IMO is how you can take out a lot of bits and pieces from a Robot before it'll blow up, so a lot of the time you end up with halves of cars and hovercraft dragging one side on the ground.

I love it when at the end of the match, my flying warship thing actually looks like it was in a fight, it pulls to the side slightly due to a missing hover blade and all the shields on the front and left are gone, but I still make it to the enemy's base.
Of course it also happens that I get blown up, but before that, when I can't even fly anymore and only have one plasma cannon left, I can still get a lucky shot and blast an enemy or two.
Of course, there are a few issues, the game has frozen a couple of times, I got a few disconnects, but nothing too bad for a game that's still in Beta and being worked on.
The fact that it's F2P doesn't detract anything from the fun. If you pay money you'll progress a lot faster through the tiers and get more parts, but I don't feel that the progress for a free player is too slow. The matches are actually fun and I even went back to a lower tier a couple of times to try out different designs.
All in all, I recommend at least trying it, it's a small download and it's free! Get it now!

Robocraft is a very fun and addicting way to pass the time. Build
robots with friggen laser beams attached to their heads!
Now, I know it's in Early Access so things will change down the road, but here's my Pros and Cons so far.
1. Endless possibilities of crafts to build with 3 robobuilding bays (pay for more).
2. Getting Tech Points to unlock weapons, armor, and other equipment is relatively easy. Getting kills, assists, enemy base capture time, victory without dying, and others will earn you Tech Points.
3. 10 different Robo Tiers. Your Tier is based on what you build your craft with and what you put on it. The more weapons, armor, and equipment you put on, the tier will increase, IF those items are from different Tiers. When you're building a craft, there's a long line with dividers at the bottom of your screen, showing the Tiers. When you put stuff on your craft, that bar will grow. If I have a Tier one build with a bunch of Tier 2 and 3 armor and weapons, my craft isn't going to be considered Tier 1 anymore. The higher the Tier, the more challenging the lobbies will be. Because players will have stronger builds and more powerful weapons. Hope that isn't too confusing.
1. Pay-to-win-faster. Yep, money rules all. You can use money to buy "Galaxy Cash". With GC, you can turn Tech Points into Uber Tech Points. Uber Tech Points allow you to purchase things in the Tech Tree (if you have the amount it requires) without having to have the Tech Points from that specific Tier. For example if I play a Tier 1 match and get Tier 1 Tech Points, I can't go and unlock a Tier 2 part. But if I convert them to Uber Tech Points, I can. The brightside is that you can't directly buy Tech/Uber points. You have to play the game and earn those Tech Points. You can also use GC to purchase parts that you've already unlocked. You earn in-game currency to buy stuff you unlock but it gets used up pretty fast.
2. Platoons. When you want to group with a friend, you invite them to your platoon (make sure you add them in-game). The problem is that the platoon leader can't just go into battle and it automatically takes you with them. You guys have to go into battle at the exact same time and make sure you guys are the same robo Tier. So the issue is that if one of you guys into battle too soon before the other, you guys could get separated. They need to make it to where when the platoon leader goes into matchmaking, the members automatically follow.
3. Railguns. If you hate snipers, you're going to hate railguns. They are extremely powerful, accurate, and long range. The trade off is a long reload time and visible laser when they're aimed but it isn't much. So the issue I have is that they're quite overpowered. Make sure you use cover because they can see a long ways with their scope.
4. Getting stuck. Sometimes you get flipped over or fall on a rock and you're screwed.
But overall, great game.

A very good game that's fun to play. And far from pay to win. Everything can be earned over time and paying l'd almost consider a waste of money. Everything you get in the game can be easily earned through playing some quick matches (Most matches last 2-6 minutes). Your vehicle has a maximum CPU output, and every block takes up a portion of this, and you can't pay to level your vehicle (earned by killing or dealing damage to enemies); the amount of money earned is more than enough to fill this cap and then some. Paying just allows you to fill this cap in under 10 minutes rather than under 20.
The game also offers a large amount of customizeability and thoughtfulness, because a backend heavy vehicle is gonna fall on it's back, likewise with a front-heavy vehicle. And if during a fight part of your frame is damaged or a wheel is blown off, moving around can get harder. Or if you are left with a single propeller in a flying vehicle, your movement will be.. difficult. Learning to build your vehicle to avoid problems like that and having a tough frame to keep you alive are some important things among others to do.
This game is incredible fun and l recommend it to anyone who thinks it sounds cool to blow up enemies or build a vehicle and see if it holds up on the battlefield.
But first, here are the.. worse things about the game.
Don't play the game expecting to chat unless you start it and have some luck, the community of the game doesn't really do that much. But it does happen if you want it. Also, when joining a match, don't go in expecting to make it through to the end or kill more than 1 player; this game isn't against robots (well, it is, but they are human driven), and making it through to the end is.. rare. Although getting frustrated about it isn't something l've run into, just be warned. ;)

I'll be frank, this game is broken. The Tier system is a joke, you can have Tier 4 weaponry, but as long as you have only 2 or 3 of these OP guns, you can enter 1st level games. Each tier gets laughably harder, the first being pretty much how many guns you can fit on your robot. Then in tier 2, everything goes to hell, with pretty much every team running around with at least 1 person with a good number of Tier 4 guns, and by the time you get to Tier 3, you can see Tiers 5 and 6. Each tier scales exponentially in power as well as difficulty, making it essentially an extreme grind-fest. Want to get to the next tier for a new gun? Well you gotta upgrade your robot with items from that Tier of game. Once you get there, you need the next tier's weaponry just to survive. Then the next. Then the next. And each one takes longer. I spent about half a day in the first Tier, where it wasn't too bad, thinking it was pretty fun. The next Tier was a whole day, and I though wow, this game is getting interestingly harder. In Tier 3, every game you get sniped by someone flying at the top of the map with Tier 4 and 5 railguns, essentially like unseeable snipers in an fps. Or someone else that can insta-kill you before you can even yell "this game is crap." What's worse is the fact that it is riddled with countless bugs, even for an early access game. Later on there is a bit of a grind to this game if you plan on getting to the higher tiers and actually being good, you need to invest a lot of time building up the points to upgrade your bot.
The game seems to throttle your progression which I didn't like. For example if you run around and just die, you seem to get points to replace your repair cost.  For example if you run around and don't die, but win or lose and never really do damage to anyone else yourself you get nothing points wise.  Now for example if you do some damage, maybe kill someone you get some good points, but lets say you kill like 5 people, you barely make more then you did just getting some damage, and always if you die you get more points to offset repairs...  kinda wierd if you ask me.
Bottem line is your get to build stuff from your imagination, and its fun to just play.  And we should all give these devs a tip, because its games like this that will drive the future, where the content is created by the players.

Nice concept but is far from finished.
If you like bulding things out of blocks like LEGOs and puting them to battle against other peoples creations then this game may be for you. You start out with a handfull of blocks to choose from, and hundreds to unlock with skill points you earn in your battles.
There are three different weapon classes to choose from (although everyone starts with the Tire 1 SMG). There is The SMG, the Plasma cannon, and the Rail gun. The SMG is bacicaly a your bacic laser gun and does nothing all to special, but it is good when grouped with several other SMGs. The plasma cannon and Railgun i have ye to unlock as i have only put about an hour into the game but from what i can see the plasma cannon is some kind of explosive launcher that does splash damage. As fro the Rail gun, i have been killed by it enough times to know what it does. It is bacicaly the sniper weapon of the game and one shot can leave a very big hole in your creation, if not kill you instantly. The only drawback with that one seems to be the reaload time, which can be somewhat bypassed if you use like 5 of them on one vehicle.
Although the game can be very fun, it can also be very frustraiting with its various bugs and other irritations. I have gotten a wheel stuck in the side of a mountain and become unable to move. Or fliped on my side and cant do anyithing about it. Thest two things seem to happen at least every other game requireing me to wait for my death of be lucky enough for my team to save me by winning. Of course you could just leave the game. but there is a loss on Credits earned for that game.
There are other things i could point out but they are somewhat minor. All in all the game is not that bad content wise considering it is an alpha. But it is still lacking many things. If you are looking for an Alpha that can be played for hours on end wothout running out of game, this game has it. Just be aware that there are still various bugs at work as well.
Overall rating 7.5 - 10

I am really on the fence about recommending this game. The reason it is an "up" is because, well, it is free and it can't hurt to try.
The game seems swell, the concept is great and the gameplay is fun. I love destroying things, especially things people have built with their own blood and sweat (but a cheap price to repair it after makes it not so harsh). It is a "Pay-to-win" game. A lot of people confused pay-to-win with freemium. I was hoping it would be freemium, but no. There are different tiers of weapons/armor. Starting out on tier 1, you will see tier 2/3 and sometimes even 4 upgrades and weapons, making it impossible to gain the necessary tech points needed to also upgrade. The experience is ruined.
Although this deters for what could make the game playable for a longer time, there are still some quirks worth checking out.
You will see many strange creations that make you laugh. You will see people flipping over due to their err in crafting. You will see a giant middle finger shooting at planes in the sky or a retro styled art design of your favorite nintendo characters driving around just to get blown to bits.
In a nutshell, it is worth playing until something better comes along. Free games are cool, but if the experience is ruined, i would much rather just pay for a game for an equal balance to bring that extra enjoyment.
EDIT: the developer calls it a f2p with a pay-to-progress system. You can still level up in tiers without paying money, but other players will have a significant advantage by paying (hence seeing higher level people on lower tier battles)
Having initially reviewed the game prematurely with little play time, it could be ruled out it being a "pay-to-win" but I have added what the developers call it.
I have spent more time playing the game and have enjoyed it despite how often I have lost battles from flipping over and being unable to help. I keep the thumb up in confidence.

BUT: In this game the microtransactions aren't too bad. The game doesn't rely on you buying special coins to advance. The special coins are there to quicken you advance. But the game works on a teir system where if you vehicle has certain parts it fits into a certain teir. To get parts you use resaerch points. People who use these microtransactions can change these coins into 'ubercoins' which let you research items of a HIGHER teir meaning people in teir two can suddenly get teir three items. So people will get the best weapons and not teir up beacuse they havn't get the other items they need to teir up. So basically i've been in games where i constantly get 1 shot killed. People with railguns in teir two doesn't make sense. So this makes some balance issues.
But other than that it's a very fun game. The building is fun and can be used easily. The fighting is simple but still relys on you hitting important parts of the enemy ships and using cover/movement to avoid bullets which gives a tactical feel to the combat.
I would like to see a toturial or something since i was slightly confused when i was thrown into the game. Also a sandbox mode where you can build and test your ships out against AI would be cool.
But it's a good game. It's free. It's worth the download. Have fun

Heres a pros vs. cons review of this game
Pros:
+The game allows you to create your own set of combat vehicles to use in actual online battles
+There is an easy and interesting upgrade tree that allows you to unlock new items (i.e. weapons, armor blocks, etc.) that can be purchace at the store.
+Rank paring between higher and lower ranked players when creating online game sessions seems relativley fair and equal
+Large community so there is no waiting too long to join a new game
+Graphics are not bad for an early game (although some glass blocks need some work)
+The add-on equipment (i.e. satellite dish for radar, etc.) are creative and helpful
+Gameplay feels smooth and is responsive
+The demand to make an in-game purchase feels low, except for more vehicle slots
+Steam wallet money can be used to make purchases
Cons:
+*Some sounds in the game feel really sharp and uncomfortable (HUGE EXAMPLE: the checkout and purchace noises at the store and after capturing a position with the noise of some beam buzzing )
+The learning curve is relatively high with little help or explanation of building effective vehicles
+The aim down with some of the guns is frustrating at times when you fire a weapon and you are unaware the weapon is blocked
+Only having three vehicle slots can feel restricting
+Railgun feels a little OP compared to other weapons
+**As far as I know, there is no vocal option for chat
*Request: Please fix the agitating sounds!!! They're really a nuisance to playing the game!!
**I'm not 100% on whether or not there is a vocal chat
Score overall:
8.8/10
Tips:
(If the dev's are reading this, I thought of a few ideas I think should be considered in the game)
+More tips of how stuff works to shrink the learning curve (and an option to turn it off if necessary)
+Some kind of blueprints for different vehicles to give the players different ideas on what to make (or to copy the vehicle in the blueprints if they are starting out)
+Options to use or not to use vocal communication so there is a larger sence of strategy with other team players

+Graphics are not bad for an early game (although some glass blocks need some work)
+The add-on equipment (i.e. satellite dish for radar, etc.) are creative and helpful
+Gameplay feels smooth and is responsive
+The demand to make an in-game purchase feels low, except for more vehicle slots
+Steam wallet money can be used to make purchases
Cons:
+*Some sounds in the game feel really sharp and uncomfortable (HUGE EXAMPLE: the checkout and purchace noises at the store and after capturing a position with the noise of some beam buzzing )
+The learning curve is relatively high with little help or explanation of building effective vehicles
+The aim down with some of the guns is frustrating at times when you fire a weapon and you are unaware the weapon is blocked
+Only having three vehicle slots can feel restricting
+Railgun feels a little OP compared to other weapons
+**As far as I know, there is no vocal option for chat
*Request: Please fix the agitating sounds!!! They're really a nuisance to playing the game!!
**I'm not 100% on whether or not there is a vocal chat
Score overall:
8.8/10
Tips:
(If the dev's are reading this, I thought of a few ideas I think should be considered in the game)
+More tips of how stuff works to shrink the learning curve (and an option to turn it off if necessary)
+Some kind of blueprints for different vehicles to give the players different ideas on what to make (or to copy the vehicle in the blueprints if they are starting out)
+Options to use or not to use vocal communication so there is a larger sence of strategy with other team players

I bought this game with the money I got for Christmas, and after waiting for Amazon to deliver it, and four hours of installation, I finally got to play it yesterday.
I must say, the graphics are brilliant. To the point where I had to play it on my brother's Windows, since my seven-year-old, second-hand Macbook Pro could not handle it.
It seems to be a rather short game, considering there are apparently ten chapters and I've played through about half of them in the four hours plat time I've gotten. However, it's probably something I'd come back to many times.  Now all I need is to find a way to play the co-op.....
The puzzles have been easy enough in the beginning, but they get very interesting, and sometimes complicated to the point where I had to look up  walkthrough for that particular test camber.
Plot...
Very interesting. You are a human, with apparent brain damage, trying to escape the old, run-down Apeture Science facility, with the help of a small robot. However, after messing up and waking up GLaDOS, another robot, you are put through several testing chambers. Using a portal gun, several cubes, lasers, and some gel, you have to find your way to the exit, and sometimes power it. Along the way, GLaDOS continues to mock you, trick you, and distract you.
Overall, I'd give this game 9/10, after deducting a point for it's shortness.
Highly recommended.
