Portal is back and better than ever! The tests are as mind bending as ever, and they've added new elements, like light bridges and emancipation gates. The graphics are smooth and attractive, but nothing that's going to make your jaw drop. The controls are as simple and effective as the first game. But then, none of that was what worried me. I had no doubt that they would be able to recreate and expand upon the technical aspects of the first game.
My concern was whether or not they would manage to capture and continue the personality and sense of humor of the first game. I am very pleased to report that the sequel does not disappoint. The sequel pics up right where the first game left off, and GLaDOS holds a grudge. Her insults, passive aggressive comments, and general malice will have you chuckling throughout the game. Your new companion and guide robot also adds to the character of the game, though he can be a bit heavy handed at times.
If you enjoyed the first game, you will love the sequel, both for its expanded challenges, and its unique personality. As long as you enjoy a good puzzle and have a sense of humor, you will never regret this purchase.

The puzzle solving or 'Testing' can range from deceptively simple to deviously clever and working out the solution to each 'Test' is a rewarding experience in itself. But with great game design, some of the most memorable characters you'll find in any game and a brilliant sense of humour, this is a game that should be on everyone's wish list... unless you really hate 'Testing' that is.

The Co-Operative gameplay of portal 2 is some of the most fun you will ever have with a friend or your significant other. If you’re anything like me you will consistently be looking for good co-op games to play and find out the hard truth that there aren’t many to be had. With the lack of good co-op games to play, Portal 2 is a defiant must have, and one of the best co-op games you will play for years to come.  Valve is one of the few developers I don’t have anything bad to say about, their games are consistently in great quality and in great fun. Over all I highly recommend Portal 2 to anyone looking for both a good game to play on their own, but also with a friend.

-------------- Portal 2 ---------------
Graphics & Audio:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Portal 2's visuals is one of the strengths of the game. High tech machines working nearby, inmense descruction surrounding you, and environment detail gives the eye candy that any high graphical gamer is seeking. In addition, the audio is well designed. From robotic voices to collapsing buildings, the audio in it will not disappoint you.
Story:
~~~~~
Before reviewing the story, have in mind that I have not played Portal 1. I can not provide any helpful information that can link the 2 video games. For portal 2, however, I like to see the story from two different perspectives. The main plot is well designed and written, the side characters are well developed, and the humor in it is done correctly. You will find the story itself quiet interesting and hilarious as you progress into the game. However, the overall setting is never explained. It will leave you wondering (not a whole lot) after completion of the game.
Game-Play:
~~~~~~~~~
The game-play in portal 2 is very puzzling (really that's what the game is all about). If you come here expecting to have some shooting and action, you will not get it. Although you do encounter enemies on your way, it is not Portal 2's main purpose. It requires you to solve puzzles by creating portals that will allow you to teleport from one place to another. At times, you may believe that the game already has everything that it can possibly offer, but then you encounter new mechanics that make the puzzles crazier and more strategic.
Other Things:
~~~~~~~~~~~
The online workshop adds on a lot of user created maps. Even after you complete the game, if you are still enjoying the puzzles, you can download plenty of user created maps. You can even create your own. It also allows you to complete puzzles with friends which adds on the puzzles' difficulty since it requires for both players to work togethere (Have in mind some friends won't easly cooperate with you!).
Overall:
~~~~~~
Portal 2 is an amazing game. Its first person and puzzle mechanics make it very unique. If you love puzzles, you are missing out on Portal 2. I personally recommend it, and if I could rate it. I would rate it a 9 out of 10.

text:
DQSwordz's Review on Portal 2
So Portal 2:
Portal 2 is a sequel to the game Portal. The game is about your character (Chell) being stuck in the Aperture Science Laboratories,  you must find the famous gun named the Portal Gun. This isnt any old gun, this gun fires out orange and blue potarls these Portals transfer you to different places for example: if you fire a blue portal and fire a orange portal and walk through the blue portal, you will transport to the location of the orange portal. However, this game s not just about having fun with portals, Oh no, theres alot more to do. Your character has to do tests using the portal gun. These tests can be puzzling, but you will have to get through them! There is also a multiplayer option to this game, you and your friend can solve puzzles together, these puzzles can only be completed with your friend so you'll have to figure out what you have to do, and what your friend has to do. Depending on who is player 1 or 2 your characters are 2 different robots. Player 1 is the small robot named Atlas, and Player 2 is the tall robot named P-Body. Atlas has 2 differents shades of blue with his portal gun and P-Body has 2 different shades of orange with his portal gun. The singleplayer campaign is very fun (except for the puzzles that I mentioned earlier they can be frustrating but they can be fun also) the funniest part of the campaign is the voice actor for a small robot named Wheatly he has a really funny voice and says lots of funny things he is voice by Stephen Merchant. Anyway this game is very fun and exciting I would definately recommend it to all my friends and anyone else. 10/10 Because of... well baisically what I just said. This is a must buy! Thank you for reading my review. :) ~DQSwordz

The game IS weird, and not in a bad sense. Sometime I felt that it couldn't be just built by people, that someone else was involved.
I played the first portal when it first came out. I was just a few levels of finishing it, it just got too hard, so i didn't have the patience and/or time to finish it; nor did I think that I'd have much of a sense of accomplishment if I did.
That was part of the reason why I was reserved about Portal 2. I just didn't want to think and strain my brain to be frank. I wanted to play more or less mindless games and lose myself in the virtual world.
Boy was I wrong. It's hard to describe this game, nor is it just to simply stamp the description of "It's a puzzle game". This game has a heart and maybe even a soul if I need to stretch that. There are only a few characters in the game but their performance if flawless. The whole game is a stage and you are the main actor, albeit a mute one. That's the part that bugs me. You still have no voice, just like in the first game and you still can't see your legs or cast a shadow.
The writing is spectacular. There are no dialogues except between Glados and Wheatley. You, obviously, are a mute, so all you do is listen and progress forward. You have absolutely no verbal or intellectual input of your own. You have no opinions, all we find out about you is that you are adopted. No name, no personality; there are only brief glimpses of your appearance through portals. So the story could be even more engaging and dear to the mind if the protagonist was even remotely felt as a human being. Seriously, I might just as well play as a robot in the main story line - would barely make any difference aesthetically speaking.
We know little about the nature of the testing chambers that you go through, but as you play, the witty public announcements give you more insight. We learn that it was some kind of private company that was engaged in conducting science way ahead of its time. We also learn that dozens if not hundreds of years passed during your cryosleep. So when I finally finished the game I was excepting a more bleak outcome. I would rather make it so that the only "friend" left on earth was the one that just finally let you go, without a possibility of return. That would have been a nice and cynical twist I think.
At one point in the game, you are warned that you may see the future or the past version of you and you are instructed to NOT interact. I was so psyched about that. Sadly. nothing like that happened, although I do think they could implement a moment of two of seeing yourself in the past or the future. They could show you dying in the future for instance (without showing the string of events leading to your death) and then have you figure out a way to not die.
Overall, there are some great distinct moments in the game that will stay with you for a while.
I enjoyed Co-Op as well. Although I played with a close friend of mine via the microphone. I cannot imagine playing Portal 2 Co-op with some stranger online since there is a LOT of communicating involved. "Place the first portal there, jump over there and place the second portal there while in mid-air; NO you idiot, place the portal THERE". Done, repeat again and again and waste hours of time. It DOES get tedious. The co-op levels are MUCH MUCH harder than in the single player campaign.
The source engine is still as great looking as it did in Half Life 2 seven years ago and as it does right now with the Left4Dead series. It's a geometry engine. The textures look great, the physics are worked out and there are many sharp corners. I couldn't imagine playing Portal 2 on any other engine.

Portal seems to be one of those game series that is under what I call the Arkham Effect: each game is, in one way or another, better than the previous. Portal 2 easily shows this. You get a great expansion on the puzzle elements found in the original Portal, as well as the addition of updated graphics and an equally-as-puzzling co-op mode. Plus, the addition of Workshop integration can definitely add to the replay value if you find good stuff there. The only reason you'd really want to play the original Portal is to see what happened before the events of Portal 2, but I definitely recommend picking up the latter if you're into puzzle games.

As you can probably assume from the hours I've played Portal 2, I have a fair amount of experience with it. Portal 2, as the sequel to Portal, goes into much more depth of the characters, featured in Portal, in the story mode, as well as introducing new ones. In addition to the story mode, you have hours of gameplay in the Community Maps, Co-Op, and Challenge Mode. Community Maps allow for users to make maps, or play maps. You could challange your friend, or even play with them in Co-Op. Co-op play features it's own little storyline, and also can run community co-op maps. Last, Challenge Mode allows you to race your friends, or compete globally to be the fastest person to play a level, or use the fewest portals to solve a challenge. These features add so much more gameplay than the original game (which was rather short), enticing players to play more, and have fun. Portal 2 is my go-to game if I'm ever bored, or feeling the need to test.

My small rant aside, this game should be part of everyones' Steam library.

Re-writing my recommendation because I feel the need to go more indepth about it. Portal 2 is a fun puzzle game that has interest visuals and characters. As with most Valve games, the levels are extremely detailed and well designed. It comes great as a sequel to portal: it contains great puzzles that will take time to think over to even a player who was replayed portal over and over hoping to breeze through it, new and interest puzzle elements, and an interesting environment. I always find myself looking at the self-reconstructing panels with awe, it gives you a sense that place is alive and self-aware which sets a nice threatning atmosphere, even moreso with GLaDOS's lines.
However, there are a few problems with it. Such as the parts inbetween levels which can drag out for awhile because you have to look around large detailed rooms to find a way just to get to the next puzzle. Which are NOT puzzles themselves for the most part, since the problem usually is just finding a portable surface, and from there its almost simple. Thus it makes the game really long to where it loses replay value compared to the first portal. Co-op is a fun and interesting idea and introduces new challenges, however the only real problem with Co-op is the people playing co-op. Its usually one guy doing all the work and the other guy snapping because he didn't let him figure it out for himself. So I recommend Co-op with people you know rather than  matchmaking.
Overall and TL;DR: Its a GREAT game and I recommend it if you like puzzles or not. +there is custom level designs that create new experiences and challenges, making it an never-ending game of puzzles to enjoy for a long long time.

It's not very recent, granted, but Portal 2 is a great game. Not so complex puzzles that causes you to stop and think twice before starting a test chamber (i.e puzzle), yet not so tough that it makes you throw your keyboard (or mouse, a laptop is quite heavy) against the wall and, like the Stanley Parable's achievement, go outside and not play the game for 5 years.
The storyline is quite simple, yet it is beautifully written. You can see GLaDOS in a whole new light (not just the metallic Hal-like psychopath who wants to slaughter you and laugh at your demise) and one can appreciate the extent of Aperture Labs, perhaps even wondering about the ethical conundrums that preludes the whole corporation.
Ponder harder as you step into multiplayer and the "Perpetual Testing Initiative", a place where you can create your own test chambers and share them with the Steam community! Let your imagination run wild as you test other's test chambers while creating really wacky ones of your own. Do you want an ambush of turrets hiding around the corner, trapping the exit room door? Now you can! Do you want to create a laser grid that frys the test subject when he/she activates the wrong switch? Now you can! The sky is the limit! (Although due to limitations, one can't stack too much stuff into any one test chamber, so that is a challenge in itself!)
9.5/10 indeed. It is worth forking out the 20USD, more so when it is on sale! Own it and see for yourself!

Portal 2 is a fantastic successor to a fantastic game. The original Portal was a game that had everything it needed and nothing more, and while this made for a tight, filler-free experience from start to finish. it also failed to satisfy many people, who saw the massive potential the mechanics had and demanded more to whet their appetites. This is the game to satisfy those people. Portal 2 takes the original game's concept and runs with it, adding a ton of new ways to sove puzzles and interact with the environment, from light bridges to lasers to three types of gels, each having a unique impact on the surface it coats. While this adds variety and a greater play time, it comes at the cost of adding some flab to the slim as a whistle Portal experience, meaning that some of this game's playtime is wasted on pointless filler, something that could not be said of Portal 1. However, the advantage of this is a much greater sense of scale and ambition, making the game feel more substantial and leaving the player less hungry. It's like choosing between a small portion of a fantastic steak and a medium portion of a fantastic steak that's just a tad overdone. Which one you prefer will depend on whether you want the best experience possible of if you don't want to feel hungry at the end of the night. The story is also top-notch. The principle of more carries over here, as more characters are added and more time is spent developing the world and the characters and the plot. Again, which plot you prefer is down to personal preference, but either way you'll be getting a lot of laughs. Finally, on top of all that, this game has a fantastic co-op mode, which, unlike the single player mode, is short, sweet, and has no filler to get in the way of some of the most brilliant puzzles in the Portal canon. If you can find a friend willing and able to play, this extra alone is worth the price of admission.

Portal 2 is the second game in the Portal series. It is a bit better than the first part.
The gameplay didn’t change that much compared to the first part, but the graphics improved and the size of the general game.
In Portal 2 you still have a “Portal Gun”, like in the first part, but there are a few more game mechanics, which increase the size of possibilities to solve a test chamber.
Due to that increase of game mechanics the puzzles are harder to solve in comparison to the first part. Sometimes you stay a few minutes in one chamber looking around, trying to find the solution to the problem, just to find out that the solution was way simpler than expected.
The humor of Portal didn’t change at all; it is as funny as the first part.
One great plus, which makes Portal 2 definitely better than Portal 1, is the coop mode. You can play, not the main story but a side story, with one friend (or stranger form the internet). The puzzles you have to solve in the coop campaign should be as hard as the single player campaign, but they are more complex due to the extra 2 portals of your partner.
The build in voice chat works well and is enough to solve the problems, but I recommend something like Skype or TeamSpeak, because in the loading screen you can’t chat with your partner, which can be annoying.
The size of Portal 2 is bigger than Portal 1, not only because of the coop campaign. I needed about 12 to 15 hours to complete the whole game (single player campaign and coop campaign).
With the support of Steam Workshop there is even more content, because you can build your own test chamber and share them with your friends or the whole Internet. You can also play test chambers of other players, and rate them.

Portals, once a fantasy, now a science, and this game has perfected it to an artform. The story is a continuation of the first game. Creating new and very entertaining characters, including the most charming robotic sphere you'll ever meet and two new robot testers Atlas and Peabody, as well as old characters brought back in surprising ways. Aside from the basic portal technology that brings you most of the games puzzles, there are several new elements that bring completly new challanges. Walk ways made of light, anti gravity tubes, speed gel, bounce gel, and a gel that allows you to place portals on any surface. All of which carry over to the new multiplayer mode. Complete with its own, although llighter, story line that coincides with the main game. There are even moments where you can see Chell solving her own puzzles from the campaign while you are wrestling with yours. However, there is one issue, playing the mulitplayer, especially online, can end friendships. The teamwork required to complete the puzzles along with the lack of any communication system, aside from pointing to things, make the experience often times maddening. Plus the Workshop brings numerous user generated content that keeps it fresh long after you've mastered all the challanges the game has to offer.

Also, you can here quotes from Cave Johnson (who, in this multiverse, is alive (another reason I love him)) whenever you start a community test. The original Portal had the element of surprise. Its style of first-person physics-based puzzle gameplay was unique. GLaDOS, the murderous robotic villain, was new and vibrant and evil in the most charming way. Cake jokes and songs about surviving dismemberment were still hilarious. It was short, succinct and essential. Creating a sequel without playing all the same notes and making it feel like Portal: The Longer Version is a tough task. For Valve, it's apparently no problem.
From the first moments of waking up in the rusting Aperture Science facility to right before the credits roll, Portal 2 rarely falters. The world is bigger, the story thicker, and the character development more surprising. The mania of GLaDOS, the facility's operator, is molded into unexpected forms alongside a host of brutally funny personalities. The history of the Aperture Science facility is filled in, character origins discussed, and though its pacing suffers as it occasionally strikes a more serious tone, an abundance of cruel jokes and cheerfully sincere death threats prevent it from losing its sarcastic charm. When you're not staring at your screen with wrinkled, pained expression on your face trying to figure out a puzzle, expect to be laughing.
**Must Have**

Portal 2... nothing more to say.
A wonderful game, that's not only what I'm thinking, but also the other 134,617 people, who recommend Portal 2 at the moment.
Not only the idea of the Portal-Gun is new and unexploited, but also the gameplay is excellent. The puzzles are very complex - especially later on in the game - and your brain will have a hard time solving them.
The Coop-mode is motivating and extremely fun when played with a friend using voice chat, teamspeak or skype. The game takes around 25 hours of your time when you want to finish the campaign and the Coop-mode. Nowadays there are also some more features like the mod-suport or the challenge-mode, which make you spend even more time in the game.
The story is simply brilliant: GLaDOS makes you laugh nearly every second and the humor is again very cool. It's both humor for everyone but also black humor sometimes. I know nobody who doesn't at least smile while playing Portal 2. And then there's the ending. Phenomenal! It's so much fun... SPAAAAACE *-* The ending song is pretty good again, but I liked the one from Portal 1 a bit more.
Since English is not my mother tongue I played the game in both German and English. Both are pretty good voice acted.
Nothing more to say except, BUY IT!!! :) No matter what genre you prefere, you'll get to know, love and hate the game and especially GLaDOS. ;)

Portal 2 is the sequel to the puzzle game, Portal, which showed off revolutionary gameplay mechanics, along with great storytelling. Portal 2 builds upon the first game's storyline. You play as Chell, a test subject at Aperture Laboritories, where instead of using a normal gun, you must utilise the Portal Gun, which creates two connected points in space.
This game really knows how to create a great story. When the game starts, a sphere / droid called Wheatley saves you from your room and takes you with him to try and escape Aperture, only to awaken GLaDOS. The interactions between GLaDOS are really witty and funny, with great voice acting.
The puzzles themselves are very good. The mechanic of the portal, along with some very clever test elements (such as lasers, gels and turrets) are fun to work with. Almost every test chamber has a new way of solving something. However, the puzzles don't get overly hard, they mostly stay around the medium difficulty mark.
With this sequel there is now a coop mode, where you play with a friend as either Atlas or P-Body. This mode is a elcome edition, and the servers run smoothly, save for the occasional disconnect. The witty GLaDOS dialogue is still there, although now she's comparing the two bots, insulting them and even pitting them against eah other. The puzzles are still fun, and in most cases are harder than the main game. Cooperating is half the batlle, but this is helped by good microphone support and the 'ping' tool, which is used to mark locations.
Now that the new upate is in, new features have been added. There is now a time-trial mode for the single player and multiplayer modes, which is like a built in feature for speedrunners, where you can check your friend's times, as well as the world's. This works well, in my opinion. I haven't encountered any errors, though getting into a multiplayer time trial game is pretty hard.
Also, there is now a level editor! This is really easy to use, and yet beautifully complex. The menus are a bit fiddly though. Complex and challenging puzzles can and have been made and uploaded to the Steam Workshop, though a lot of these gems are surrounded by mindless garbage and maps that aren't even puzzles that somehow reach the front page.
All in all, I would recommend this game to any player of any skill level. Portal 2 is a puzzle game with tons of content and replayability.
+ Level editor!
+ Great puzzles and puzzle elements
+ Fun coop mode
+ Time Trail mode's a great edition
- Can be buggy
9.5 / 10
TL; DR: Buy it now.

Sequel to Portal, the absolute surprise of Orange Box. Even though its puzzles are easier than the ones from the original Portal, developers have decided to add more types of puzzles, in which you have to use Faith Plates, various gels which modify your motion, as well as hard light bridges and tractor beams.
This time you are in cryosleep, when suddenly a small robot, Wheatley, wakes you up. With his help you try to escape Aperture Science labs, now completely owergrown and in ruins, at least until Wheatley accidentaly reactivates GLaDoS...
Again there is a lot of humour in this game. GLaDoS still sarcastically comments on - well almost every action you do, but we could say that Wheatley is a star of this game, with his at times paranoic and "Trust me, I'm an engineer" attitude and later his power-caused lunacy.
Developers have had playing time in mind so you again go through loads of test chambers. Some of them are historical, and with guidance of audio records of Aperture Science's CEO, Cave Johnson, you solve them as well, but you also learn terrible secret. There is also a co-op campaign in which you and a friend of your choice control two robots, Atlas and P-Body, who are tested. And tested. And again.
You've probably seen this game's ratings, but since Metascore can be quite exaggerated (like with Bioshock), I'm happy to tell you that this time the ratings are true. Since you can get Portal 2 with discount every now and then, I strongly advise you do.

Portal 2 is the sequel to Portal and adds more puzzles and more fun.
At the beginning of Portal 2, Chell is awakened in a “long-term relaxation chamber” in Aperature Science by a little hilarious, British personality named Wheatley. Wheatley's goal is to help you escape, however you soon find out that GLaDOS is still alive. Chell is once again forced to use her portal gun to navigate the ruins of the facility and deal with the resurrected GLaDOS. The story takes some very interesting twists and turns along the way and the terrific dark humor of the first game remains intact.
The gameplay from the original game returns in all of its mind-bending glory. Players use the portal gun to shoot blue and orange colored portal holes onto walls to traverse over deadly pits, transport Weighted Storage Cubes to switches to open doors and lower elevators and redirect lasers. Additions to the gameplay include the propulsion and repulsion gels which do pretty much as they describe, either sliding the player off at great speed or sending them bouncing high into the air. In addition, players must redirect light bridges and conveyer beams with portals as well.
One of the most exciting new features in Portal 2 is the inclusion of co-op gameplay.
Co-op gameplay gets its own storyline and characters, Aperture Science robots ATLAS and P-Body, each armed with their own portal gun and even more challenging puzzles for the gamers to solve. You can either play with a friend (split-screen or online) or team up with a random player.
I highly recommend Portal 2 to anyone who is looking for a good fun game that will take up a few hours and even make you think instead of the average First Person Shooter.
Overall, Portal 2 is a masterpiece and definitely worth the money.

Portal took the gaming world by storm. Included as part of a bundle with the focus on other, more expensive Valve titles, the little student project that was Portal became one of the most beloved romps of the current console generation. With the sequel, Valve decided that bigger is better, and in this case, it's true. Portal 2 has a campaign that is nearly four times the length of the original, a co-op that is great fun with a buddy and neatly ties into the main story, several amusing easter eggs, a deepening of the original mystery of the facility and the story's ties to the Half-life games, hilarious new characters Wheatley (a troublesome robot who wants to help you escape) and Cave Johnson (the founder of Aperture Science), excellent voice acting, and that signature Valve wit. I honestly cannot think of another video game as quotable or laugh-out-loud funny as Portal 2. One of the rare sequels that outshines the original and just a lot of fun to play.

Reviews for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
---
With regard to accessibility for deaf/hoh gamers, I give Portal 2 a 10/10.
Gameplay
The only issues that come up with Portal 2 are with the multiplayer.  In single player, there are no problems since captions exist.  Multiplayer games are goal-oriented and require coordinated efforts.  The game allows coordination through a ping tool that drops a marker where you're looking that the other player can see.
Subtitles/Text
The game is fully captioned, so deaf/hoh can play single player effectively without missing anything.  Multiplayer games do not require subtitles.
Chatting/Communicating
You can use text chat in multiplayer games to augment the ping tool.

Compared to its predecessor, Portal 2 is a much more lengthy (around 11 hours compared to the original's 5 hours) story driven and an absolutely hilarious adventure. I have not laughed out loud as much in a Valve game as i did with Portal 2. In addition to all the improvements, there is now even a seperate co-op game mode which is very well implemented and just downright fun.
It improves on almost everything that made the first game so successful. No longer feeling like a linear series of puzzle rooms, this time all gameplay elements just fits in beautifully into a well crafted story.
Although the sense of novelty using the Portal gun may have been diminished with this sequel, it distinguishes itself now with the excellent story writing that is full of memorable characters, and expertly designed scripted events. The story is now also much more light-hearted compared to the original game.
Using an enhanced version of the Source Engine, the game looks very nice especially when it showcases its lighting and shadows. There are now more composed music and all of them are suitably atmospheric, although i personally felt that the end credits song "Want You Gone" was not as memorable and cute as "Still Alive". That said, i felt that the "Turret Opera" song was very well made and unique.
Character voice work quality are still as exceptional as ever. GLaDOS is now a much more complex and emotional character as compared to the first game. (She's still a homicidal maniac though lol) There are also some newcomers such as the character Wheatly who is downright hilarious and is a great addition to the cast.
Having a co-op mode definitely adds alot and its really fun to tackle the challenges with a friend. This game works very well indeed with co-op.
Downsides, loading screens are now more frequent and lengthy and i felt that it broke up the momentum of the game. This is probably due to the fact that Portal 2 was also ported to consoles. Newcomers who have not played Portal 1 may not be able to appreciate some of the story elements in Portal 2. Also, some questions remain unanswered. None of these issues however take away from the experience of the game.
Overall Rating: 9.5 / 10

If I had to sum up Portal 2 in one word, it would be "bigger."  Everything is bigger than the original:  the levels, the puzzles, and to some extent the comedy.  I was expecting really more of the same from the original: walk into a test chamber, do the puzzle, hear some jokes, repeat.  This is more or less how the game begins, but before you know it you're at the bottom of the veritable bottomless pit using your portaling skills to navigate your way back up.  You only realize after about 2 or 3 "puzzles" down there you are actually still playing the game proper, and not some intermission-type side quest.  A perfectly veiled way to make the puzzle mechanic feel fresh in my opinion.
The writing may be the one thing that I would dare say tops the original.  Where GlaDOS was the center of gravity around which the comedy orbited in Portal, Wheatley comes into Portal 2 and steals the entire show.  HIs changing roles in the game allow him to exhibit different dialogues with the player, and he ends up being the perfect go-between for this game world and the player on the couch.  Add in the returning GlaDOS and Aperture President and CEO Cave Johnson and you have a comedy team that will crack you up from start to finish.
Speaking of the couch, I elected to play Portal 2 there with my Xbox 360 controller.  Mostly because I shared playing repsonsibilities when I first played it with a friend, and partially because I was looking to utilize the still fairly new set up I had between my PC and TV.  The game plays almost exactly the same on the TV with one notable exception, there is little or no aim botting software guiding the aiming of the portal gun.  A system pioneered and mastered by the creators of Halo, the aim bot allows the inherently inaccurate and sloppy gamepad controller to partially auto aim FPS guns in-game as opposed to being done solely by the player.  So with the absence of that in this game, the player can immediately notice drastically lower accuracy playing the game.  Thankfully Portal 2 is not about super accurate gameplay, the player choosing to play the way I did simply has to get used to it.
Any modern video game released today seems to be required to come with some sort of multiplayer.  Portal 2 is no different; Valve put together an entire co-op campaign for everyone to play.  As I mentioned earlier, I played this game in its entirety in 2011 with a friend on my couch.  So when we finished the main game and it came time to play this co-op thing, we planned to simply load the game up and play it there.  Inexcusably, this co-op campaign did not feature a split screen option when it was releaseed, you could only play it through an internet connection.  Since I had zero intentions of ever playing this game with anyone else I knew or randomly with someone on the internet, this unincluded feature for co-op rendered this game mode in the never to be played category.  Valve has since added in split screen for the co-op, and maybe one day I'll finally get around to playing it, but I'm not holding my breath.
So my multiplayer experience for Portal 2 ended up simply being passing the controller back and forth with the main game while sitting on the couch with another Portal aficionado.  I mention this because that experience ended up being the most fun I had playing a video game with a friend in years.  Add in beer and pizza, and we spent several laugh-filled evenings trying to find our way through these puzzles and just enjoying the game.  With this new world we live in with perpetual internet connections, and multiplayer video games being almost exclusively played over that internet, I still find that the best social gaming experiences to be the ones where friends sit together and play together.  For me, my Portal 2 experience essentially rang the deathknell for the internet as the principle driver of multiplayer gaming.  For all its technologies and complexities, the internet is no match for a couch, beer and pizza when it come to having fun playing multiplayer video games with friends.

Portal 2: a spectacularly well-designed puzzle game with a lot of depth.
I went into Portal 2 thinking that I wouldn't enjoy the game. I am not a huge fan of games where puzzles are the primary part of the game. However, some of my favorite game series do contain a lot of puzzle elements (i.e. The Legend of Zelda). So I was sure exactly where Portal would fit into that.
However, upon starting Portal 2, I almost immediately fell in love with it. The storytelling and the humor are top-notch and hook you from the beginning of the single-player campaign. They also serve to keep the puzzles more interesting.
Speaking of the puzzles, they are all really well designed. Many of them seem so complicated at first, but have simple enough solutions that make you wonder how you didn't see them faster! The joy of finally figuring out a puzzle you've been working on for a while is so rewarding. Plus, the game constantly introduces new elements to the puzzles that keep them from becoming boring, and the different elements in the puzzles can be used in so many unique ways. All of the puzzles in the game feel very well planned out. I'd recommend playing through the game a second time on Commentary mode to see some of the thought behind the game's design.
There's also a two-player co-op mode which allows you and a buddy to take on specially-designed 2 player puzzles. This campaign is just as fun and well-designed as the single player story. You can play splitscreen or online with friends or random people. I'd recommend playing with someone you know and can talk to, though, for a more engaging experience.
As if all that wasn't enough, you can design puzzles and share them on Steam. There are some fantastic puzzles designed by the community for you to find and enjoy.
Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game. However, I would suggest playing the original Portal before playing this one. I played Portal 2 first, and ended up regretting it. It isn't too big of a deal, but you might not fully understand the story, and playing Portal 1 second will make Portal 1 seem a bit staler.

Talking about this game without mentioning it's predecessor is difficult. Because of this, I took the liberty of forgetting everything I know about the first game, all 300 hours of me playing and speedrunning it, and all 80 hours of me speedrunning the campaign of this game, and played through it as blind as possible.
The best parts about this game are it's story and dialogue. The graphics are good but you can't really compare it to anything because there's really nothing like it on this build of the Source engine besides CS:GO, but that game doesn't really look good compared to this. Great nonetheless.
I won't go through the story because it's too long to read. If you're doubting your purchase, wait until it's on sale or watch some videos, preferably not about the solo or co-op campaigns in order to not have the story ruined. I recommend watching videos on the custom chambers/stories because they add so much to the game thanks to the built in authoring tools you get, both built into the game and the seperate Hammer editor, the same editor used to make the maps in the story.
Throughout the game, you are put into some scenarios that require you to do some ninja moves, such as
and
(if you don't want the game spoiled don't look) but they're not really insane ninja moves. There's really no high difficulty to this. When I played through it the first time on XBox, I completed the game in a few combined hours, longer than PC because of controller issues. It's really not hard and that may be a turn off for the campaign, but custom chambers fix that difficulty itch.
The writers of this game deserve awards. I'm serious. The dialogue is the best in any campaign I've played, and yes, that's including GTA V. The dialogue alone for me was worth the $19.99 I spend on this game, twice (I have this game for XBox and PC).
Challenge mode is back from the first game but without "Least Steps," a challenging, careful, movement based challenge that made the game a real challenge outside the real game. But, at least the game now includes the challenge in one try. If you want to do a fast, least portals run, instead of timing that run seperately, you can run it and if you get a faster time than your run where you didn't care about the amount of portals used, it overwrites your time even though you were going for least portals. It's a time and pain saver. Bring back advanced challenges though.
That's all I'm going to say. If you want more, watch some videos, wait for a sale or a coupon, or just get the game, it's true it's one of the best games, if not, the best sequel to a game ever made.

Portal 2 Is a game where you play as the silent protagonist 'Chell' in Aperture Laboratories or as one of two testing robots in the cooperative initiative. This game revolves around the one thing that aperture has time and time again proven is it's most valuable item, the Aperture Science handheld portal device, There are multiple versions but they come in two phases, singular and dual portal, with the singular, you can only place one portal. The dual alternative, you get the idea. Portal 2 revolves around puzzles in rooms and physics to get there, and it's all thanks to the man, Cave Johnson. Why buy it? It's a great game that doesn't just end at the end of the campaign / singleplayer / story, There's coop mode which allows you to buddy up locally or over the net, maybe even with a stranger if necessary. Even once you finish that there's more, community-made tests. There are so many you'd be there for a whileif you plan to finish all of them. Why do people say cave hates lemons? Who is wheatley? Why is GLaDOS calling me a monster? "Let me answer those questions with a question: Who wants to make sixty dollars? Cash." Not really, just stop asking questions and see it for yourself.

If you liked Portal, you are sure to LOVE the amazingly done sequel. The graphics are amazing, the voice acting is spectacular. The story line finely tuned and continued not only through the story and Original Co-Op, but through the free Co-Op DLC and even the Map Making DLC.
Valve really did it this time, a real masterpiece. The replay value is through the roof, even more now with the new map making tool.
Playing with your friends online is a BLAST! Death is not a problem, you just respawn back. In fact it's quite fun to mess with your friends and their trust, portaling them into liquid goo instead of the finish. Or trapping them in a portal loop. It's all in good fun however, and you both can have a good laugh.
The puzzle solving aspect of the game is slightly revamped from the first game. Although at first a lot of the maps from the first maps are remastered into the game to reteach the basics, as the facility becomes more evolved the maps quickly get harder to complete, requiring more brain power and skill.
There are hardly any problems with it, like most games there are sometimes lag problems, loading may trail on a little bit for larger levels, but overall the game is very well put together and close to no glitches occur. This game goes highly on the list of games I recommend to my friends and play often. I suggest you give it a try as well!

From difficult brain teaser's involving almost a half hour to figure out and plan, to obvious press the button and the level is immediately beat, This game has a wide variety of levels in it. But not just that: The voice acting is top notch, The graphics are amazing even on the lowest settings, and the dialouge is hilarious; having me legitamitaly rolling around with laughter. And then after you beat the game there is a ton of other levels to do in co-op with a firend or random person, AND THEN after that you can play countless user-created levels. You are almost paying for everything.
Summarize- The game is so good you even get the moon. Literally.

Did you like the first game for it's dark humor? Now you can enjoy a game where that same dark humor is now 200% less subtle!
This game immediately alienates those who were familiar with the first title by throwing an updated version of the Source engine in the game, which gives a distinct disconnect between how you're controlling and what's actually onscreen compared to the first game.
Artstyle is okay. The updated look of the Portals is pretty poor compared to the first game, and the only area of the game that really stood out visually was That Middle Section of the Game I won't describe because spoilers. The rest of the game suffers from too little white space with which to shoot portals. You have to go into the single player accepting the fact that you aren't playing Portal, a first person puzzle platformer, but Portal 2, a first person adventure game.
To go with the game's new role as an adventure game, the voice acting direction to lose all semblance of the bland robotic tone from the first game. Steven Merchant has hardly any distortion applied to his voice, and H.K. Simmons's script is literally nothing but one-off jokes that prevent the player from properly connecting with him. Ellen McLain is fine, nothing fantastic but she has to walk through the same sludge script as the rest of the cast. The script just sucks, too many blantant attempts at jokes, not enough off-kilter or black humor which helped lend the game its unique atmosphere. So many elements from Portal 1 are reused that you wonder why Valve bothered.
Can't comment on multiplayer, have no interest getting frustrated trying to complete puzzles that are likely by Valve's standards 4 times as hard as single player ones. No comment on the workshop levels either, no experience with modding or level designing.
Game's lack of a true difficulty curve results in resetting at multiple points in the game while you learn new concepts instead of adding on to previously learned ones.
Plot is dumb, a bunch of material that stresses the plausability of a scenario I found perfectly reasonable in the first game by way of overexposition.

The singular most amazing, mind-boggling, brain-teasing and beautiful puzzler I have ever seen. 10/10. Well done. Valve, I salute you.
Edit: Even years after it's release, this is still an amazing game!

I can honestley say that this has grown to be one of my favorite games, the plot is good, the characters are great, and the mechanics are excellent. I'm not going to give anymore of this game away but I loved every second of it, and Wheatly has become one of my all-time favorite video game charachters. With witty, funny dialouge throughout, loads of suprises, and interesting new ideas added to this game, it creates a whopping 15 hours (I got stuck on some puzzles and didn;t cheat, so time varies on ow smart you are with portals) of gameplay, which is quite impressive compared to the original. Another neat and cool thing is the steam workshop, with lots of new testing chambers every day to try out when you've soaked every bit of entertainment you could out of singleplayer, as well as a co-op mode! My final rating of this game is a 9.5/10 a great game for new and old players of the franchise, Valve really has a gift for game making :)

All of the old tricks, a bunch of new tricks, and even more GlaDOS than ever before - what's there not to love? This time, the trusty portal gun will be not only your weapon in a battle of wits against cybernetic malevolence, but also an instrument of story-telling and a tool of exploration as the game throws you out of the septic confinement of test chambers and into cyclopean environments that guard the history of Aperture Labs. Some of the locations have an almost "open world" feeling about them and the puzzles will often turn into a challenge of "Find Waldo" involving portal-able surfaces, and many of them could be described as "cheap" in retrospect. Yet the story and the consistently amazing character writing are enough to keep you going even through the most frustrating of trials.

A VAST improvement on the first, and notably longer. It's a much more plot-driven game this time around and adds a lot of flavor to the game, but it doesn't focus so much on the story so as to distract from the main gameplay. It's the PERFECT balance between story and gameplay for a game of its kind. New gameplay mechanics (i.e. gels and lasers) make for a myriad of new puzzles and head-scratching moments to be had, community levels make for an almost endless array of levels and fun, and co-op is a great way to spend time with your friends and solve puzzles together...
...or let them do all the work while you sit around dunking them in acid as they cross a hard light bridge under your control.
BUT ALL IN ALL, this game is nothing short of amazing, and I honestly think it's one of those must-have games.

Take Portal 1.
Add a better story.
Subtract the cake jokes.
Add a buddy banter system.
Add more puzzle elements.
THEN add custom maps, coop play, competitive play....
This equation makes for a wonderfully fun puzzle adventure. It's a Valve game, and the quality shows.
Sound: 5/5- Wonderful, especially the voice acting. Wheatley and Cave Johnson are amazing. Even the puzzle elements have their own little sounds and tunes!
Graphics: 4/5- Quite good and should run on almost every system. Source is pretty well optimized, at this point, or so it seems. This accessibility means that it isn't jaw dropping.
Gameplay: 5/5- Short but sweet. The <10 hours you play the main story are amazing 100% of the time. But there's so much more this time around with the extra modes and content.
Overall: 5- Just amazing. Unless you -hate- physics puzzles, play this game!

The quiet, mundane Portal is obviously too quiet for most people. So now there's Portal 2. It's another great Vavle game, but i think some of the magic of the original Portal is lost in it.
You pick up where Portal left off; same girl, still testing, but you have this buddy robot named Wheatly who's got a killer British accent but not much of a brain. GLADOS is back too. As you continue testing, both computer-bots change alliances as you discover the origins of the Portal company. The chambers start off easier than the originals but get exponentially harder with each chapter (the game is much longer than the original).
What is by far the most interesting is co-op mode, in which you and a friend play two robots that have replaced human testers. Not much else to say except that it's fun as heck.
I give Portal 2 an 8 out of 10.

Portal 2 delivers an excellent single player experience which lasted around 12 hours for me to complete, the puzzles got harder as you went along, I often found myself stuck in certain test chambers. The storyline of Portal 2 is one which will keep you playing, as during the middle of the game, a huge shock happens which I wont spoil, but I just had to see what happens next. The singleplayer isn't the only part of Portal 2 however, the all new Co Op mode lasted around 10 hours itself, which lacked storyline but was still alot of more than the Singleplayer as you had to work with someone else, which worked really slick and smoothly (especially the ping tool, that was just great), the Co Op mode also comes equipped with the Robot Enrichment micro transactions store, kind of like the Man Co Store in TF2, this adds purely costmic customizations for your Co Op character, whch I think is a really good addition to the game for those people who have spare money to spend.

Portal 2 - to sequel gry Portal z 2007 roku. Premiera na Steamie miała miejsce 19 kwietnia 2011 roku. Gra posiada dwa tryby rozgrywki: dla pojedynczego gracza (Chell) i tryb kooperacji dla dwóch graczy (Atlas i P-body). Pięćdziesiąt dni po akcji pierwszej części Chell zostaje przebudzona w swojej komorze długoterminowej relaksacji i przechodzi szereg drobnych ćwiczeń, po czym zostaje uśpiona ponownie. Mija kilkaset lat w czasie których ośrodek Aperture Science Enrichment Center ulega poważnym uszkodzeniom. Kiedy wyczerpuje się awaryjne zasilanie Centrum relaksacji, bohaterka zostaje przebudzona przez rdzeń osobowości imieniem Wheatley. Razem, próbują uciec z kompleksu, ale Wheatley przez przypadek aktywuje cały ośrodek, w tym GLaDOS. Sztuczna inteligencja od razu poznaje bohaterkę i mszcząc się za swoją śmierć i jej przykre konsekwencje, postanawia kontynuować testy aż do końca jej życia.

All that good stuff I said about Portal?  It all applies here.  Portal was one of the best games ever.  Portal 2 is one of the best sequels ever.
Instead of rehashing the original game, or going off into a wierd, unrelated territory, Portal 2 is a faithful continuation of the original game.  Only this time, the world is larger, and the revelations are more disturbing and at the same time, hilarious.  This game strikes a careful balance between horror and humor, as you explore the remains of a monument to science gone mad.  This game may lack some of the brilliance of the original (according to some people, I didn't find it lacking at all), but it holds up very well.  And unlike Portal, this game is long, spanning 10 chapters and introduces some interesting new game play elements.  It is almost as though Portal were the prototype, and this is the full game.
Along with the massive single-player story, there is also a co-op mode.  I want to say more, but I'm out of spaaaaaaaaace...

Portal2 is a first person puzzle game developed by Valve and released 2011. This game was greatly anticipated when it was announced and we all waited in anticipation for the release.
The game was not a disappointment, the developers brought us back to Aperture Laboratories and put us to work on new and innovative puzzles, Portal1 and 2 will always be one of my most favorite puzzle games, period.

The whole game is based on the core concepts of two portals
, be it moving objects through these portals, moving yourself between these portals, or jumping off high objects to reach hard to reach places, the game is a brainteaser in such a wonderful way. As the catchphrase goes “prepare to think with portals”.
There are a number of features in Portal2, there are Single player, Co-op, Community Test Chambers/Workshop, Steam Achievements, and challenge modes where you can compete against your friends for fastest times, least portals used, steps, and more.
There are 51 Achievements for Portal2, Most of the single player achievements are straightforward fun and challenging to get... There are also Co-op achievements, so it would be best to make or get a friend to help you out.
Portal2 is priced at $19.99 that will be the best 20 dollars you spend. But if you're on a tight budget like me you might want to wait for a 75% off sale, since the game was released in 2011 there's a very good chance that there will be sale for it.
I really can't sum up how great Portal2 is without saying “look, if you're even remotely interested in trying it out, you don't grasp just what an outstanding puzzle game it is. I highly recommend Portal2 to everyone and anyone.

I had some serious doubts that there could be a sequel to Portal that would be better than the original game and this title is the absolute proof that I was wrong.
It not only has all the good points of the first Portal: innovative gameplay, really interesting mind-blowing puzzles and amazing immersive graphics, but also introduces new characters wilh vivid and real-like personality, new features that can perfectly co-exist with the previous seen in the series, leading to far more possible puzzles than before.
It's not farfetched to say, but this is one of my favourite games of all time. I simply couldn't see the hours go by.
Yet, on the other side, I don't know if I just maybe went by the puzzles too fast but I had the feeling, just like in the first game,  that the game itself is too short. Even though the story is pretty well conceived and fundamented, you reach the end always wanting a bit more. Anyway the few hours you spend on it are well spent. (wrote more, but Steam limits)

Portal was a phenomenon and redefined how puzzle games are made. The narrative was original and also helped create one of the best video game songs ever created ("Still Alive" by John Coulton). Portal 2 helps build upon this in so many ways and really helps show how a sequel should be done. Instead of just being stuck in lab testing rooms through the whole game there are more environments to enjoy and the narrative takes leaps forward instead of just GLaDOS's voice droning on through speakers.
You play as the voiceless Chell once again, but you awaken after being in a coma for some time. A mysterious robot named Wheatley helps you escape your room and you finally get to see what Aperture Laboratories is like outside the testing rooms. You get to see glimpses of the outside world, vegetation has taken over the facility, and the puzzles now take form in so many different ways. Half way through the game you get to see what Aperture was like 50 some odd years ago and find out back stories on yourself, GLaDOS, and the founder of Aperture. The narrative is top notch with lots of cinematic moments, but everything involves puzzle solving and it's so mind bending that each one of the 50+ puzzles feels satisfying. It also goes to show how clever Valve is that I didn't need a walkthrough once to figure out any of the puzzles. There's so many "AHA!" moments that you just don't want to put the game down.
However, there aren't just portals involved, but other game play elements have been fused into the mix. There are three types of gels that you can use to solve puzzles such as propulsion gel (orange stuff that makes you go really fast), fusion gel (blue stuff that makes things bounce), and conversion gel (it allows portals to be made on non-portal surfaces). Due to these new elements you have to totally rethink how you work with portals and it's a great new mechanic and super fun to use. There are a few other things such as jump pads, new types of companion cubes, turrets, and other items to solve puzzles, but explaining is almost impossible because you should just play it.
The puzzles are just so uniquely fused with the narrative that you never feel like your just jumping from room to room anymore. This really feels like a puzzle/adventure this time around and some of the puzzles span two to three rooms even. There's constant chatter from characters while solving puzzles so it doesn't feel as stale this time around. All the new characters are great and you'll like them (or hate them) quickly thanks to Valve's one-of-a-kind storytelling abilities. The music is one thing I love about this game because when you start bouncing around a room or sliding there's unique music that instantly plays when you're doing these things. You get a strong sense of vertigo thanks to the game's new take on heights, but the music is just phenomenal. This soundtrack is purchase worthy and the new GLaDOS song at the end is just as good as "Still Alive" but in other ways.
The visual quality is great, but Valve really needs a new next generation engine. Portal 2 uses the Left 4 Dead 2 Source engine, so everything looks nice and there's some great visual effects (the gel mainly) as well as great lighting, but it's not exactly up to par. Thankfully there's a huge variety of things to look at this time around (the game is over 10GB!) and the addition of a co-op campaign with an additional story and two new characters is a huge plus so it's like two games in one. There's also some quality extras such as developer commentary and you can customize your robots in the co-op campaign which is a nice touch.
Portal 2 is truly something unique for this generation and probably the most innovative puzzle game ever made. With a strong narrative, lovable characters, and tons of new game play mechanics its like the first game didn't even exist. Don't be overwhelmed by working with portals because this game takes your hand for awhile and slowly lets you go when you feel confident enough you'll know. Valve knows how to make great games and other developers need to follow suit.

Portal 2 draws from the award-winning formula of innovative gameplay, story, and music that earned the original Portal over 70 industry accolades and created a cult following.
The single-player portion of Portal 2 introduces a cast of dynamic new characters, a host of fresh puzzle elements, and a much larger set of devious test chambers. Players will explore never-before-seen areas of the Aperture Science Labs and be reunited with GLaDOS, the occasionally murderous computer companion who guided them through the original game.
The game’s two-player cooperative mode features its own entirely separate campaign with a unique story, test chambers, and two new player characters. This new mode forces players to reconsider everything they thought they knew about portals. Success will require them to not just act cooperatively, but to think cooperatively.

It was the first one-player game I played after getting steam, if I recall correctly, and I must say that I chose my games very well.
I have this game, and Valve as a company (and Nintrendo) to thank for bringing me joy, and a glance into what videogaming could be, if the creator is creative and tallented enough.
I strive to one day publish a game that I can be proud of, as undoubtedly the Valve team working on this game was.
The portal mechanic works flawlessly, which is to be expected, but not entirely without questioning if you ask me. It is amazing how they made it so perfect, that I'm still scratching my head about what kind of a magic spell they used. If the portal mechanic wasn't flawless, the world would not have been as emersive as it is, and I feel sadness for even thinking of a reality where the young me was playing Portal 2 for the first time, trying to figure out how the portals worked, and even sort of understand how they were made, just by looking at them.
It is the most immersive level-based game of all time, and I am truly happy to have this game as a reference for when designing my own games.
PS: This review was published in 2012, but the review was re-written on 2017-12-22. The original review went something like this: "I love this game! I have nothing to complain about!"

Portal 2 is a great game for the following reasons:
Graphics: 10/10. The game looks beautiful, nothing looks confusing, you know what everything is when you look at it.
Sound: 10/10. The soundtrack is simply great! I personally really enjoyed the gel music and the end credits which everyone loves. The voice acting and script is great, in Portal 1 I loved GLaDOS quotes, in this game I love both GLaDOS and Wheatley's quotes.
Gameplay: 8/10. The gameplay is simple, fun, but unfortunately it isn't hard enough. I like challenging games and this wasn't challenging.
Co-op: 10/10. Playing with a friend clearly tests who solves puzzles better than the other. Another reason why it's great? Free DLC of course!
Extras: 10/10. The inventory system (and trade mechanic which was never implemented from inside the game) is a bit lacking and skins are useless, feels like it really added nothing to the game. However, the Perpetual Testing Initiative DLC (which is also free) is absolutely fantastic! Who doesn't want to make their own Portal maps, and this makes it easy.
I absolutely love the game and I remember waiting for its release back in 2011.

I didn't enjoy playing "find the one section of portalable wall;" I didn't enjoy trying to find out which square inch of floor I was supposed to cover with rainbow slime; and I didn't particularly enjoy the game taking the originally brilliant narrative and trying to cram in as much additional zaniness as possible.

What more can be said about Portal 2 that already hasnt been said? The game takes a simple concept, and reshapes it into a challenging puzzler that will sure to make your brain cramp. You are a tester at Aperature Sciences. You have awoken from a deep sleep, and immediatley find yourself solving puzzles in order to escape the evil computer, GLADOS, who wants to make your life a living hell. You are also joined by a little robot friend with hilarious dialogue who assists you on your journey. The dialogue within  this game is what makes it a sheer masterpiece. You are constantly called fat, ungly, and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, in the literal sense, on a hourly basis, perhaps, forcing you to question whether you are what the game paints you as. I mean, the dialogue is top notch, better than GTA in my opinion. Anyway, I digress. What puts the icing on the nonexistent cake are the NUMEROUS puzzles. The learning curve is perfect, and you dont feel codled and taken care of. All in all, this game is a masterpiece, one I would put above GTA and TLOU any day.
A little late to the party, but wow! Just as fun as the original!

In my opinion this is the greatest franchise Valve has ever come out with.
This game in its entirety is genius to me; the whole concept is just amazing. It has mind boggling puzzles that are extremely creative (which now you can make your own with steamworks), and an amazing plotline with a real cinematic feeling to it when it comes to the cut scenes. There’s one scene that gives me a chill every time, and that in itself is amazing.
For a puzzle game it sure does feel like there is a lot of action in this game. It can be very fast paced at times, and slow paced at others. Which I like, it’s nice to be stood there for ages thinking so hard at one point and running around franticly trying not to die at another.
There’s an amazing set of characters which are so perfectly done in terms of voice acting. I really couldn’t think of any better match for the characters they came up with. It has awesome little secrets and things to find that really expand your curiosity even further and make you really want to know more about the goings on at Aperture Science Laboratories.
The humour in this game is wonderful, and there was more than a few times I had a real chuckle to myself, I was pretty impressed with how well it was done.
There is a lot to this game, and it really is one of the best gaming experiences I have ever had.
You are a test subject, and you are once again trying to find your way out. But a lot stands in your way.
I was pretty sad when I finished this game, as I’m not sure there’s anything to go on to turn into a future game. If there is, bring it on. I would love to once again be thrown into this world, but sadly I doubt there will be. It’s an amazing franchise, definitely one I can see myself playing again in future.
There is also a comic online on the Portal website for anyone that would like to see a beautifully constructed comic with some wonderful art that fills in some gaps and shows you how Aperture Science got to be how it is today.
